When he prepared heaven, I was beside him, and when he marked out his seat. When above the winds he made the clouds strong on high, and when he set the springs firmly [Note: [Col. 0696C] “set the mountains” cod. 1.] beneath heaven, when he made the foundations of the earth strong, [Col. 0696C] I was beside him, arranging all things. I was the one in whom he rejoiced. And daily I delighted before his face at all times, as he rejoiced in the perfected world” (Prov. VIII, 22).

Likewise, in the same author, in Ecclesiasticus: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature. In the heavens I caused unfailing light to arise, and with mist I covered [Note: [Col. 0696D] “with mist I covered” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Bod. 2, 3, 4; “with a cloud” Bod. 1; “clouds” Oxon.] the whole earth. I dwelt [Col. 0697A] in the heights [Note: [Col. 0697C] “in the highest places” Bod. 1, 2. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.], and my throne was in a pillar of cloud. I traversed the circuit of heaven [Note: [Col. 0697C] “I alone traversed” Lam. Bod. 2, 3. NC. 1.], penetrated the depth of the abyss, walked upon the waves of the sea, stood throughout the whole earth, and held primacy among every people and every nation [Note: [Col. 0697C] “maintained primacy” Bod. 2. Lam.]; and by my own power I trod upon the hearts of all, both exalted and lowly [Note: [Col. 0697C] “by power I trod upon the hearts” Thu. Corb. Benev. Ver.]. In me is every hope of life and power [Note: [Col. 0697D] “In me is the way of life” Lin.; “the hope of life” Foss.]. Come over to me, all you who desire me” (Ecclus. XXIV, 5).

Likewise in Psalm LXXXVIII: “And I shall make him my firstborn [Note: [Col. 0697D] “I shall make him my firstborn, exalted above the kings of the earth” NC. 2.], the Most High among the kings of the earth. Forever I shall preserve my mercy for him, and my covenant shall be faithful to him; and I shall establish his seed forever and ever [Note: [Col. 0697D] “his seed, and his throne like the days of heaven” NC. 2.]. If his sons forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments, if they profane my ordinances and do not observe my commandments, I shall visit their crimes with a rod and their offenses with scourges. Yet I shall not scatter my mercy from them.”

Likewise, in the Gospel according to John, the Lord says: “Now this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only and true [285] God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent. I have glorified you upon the earth [Note: [Col. 0697D] “I have glorified you above the earth” Lam. NC. 1.]; I have completed the work [Note: [Col. 0697D] “the work having been completed” Lin.; “which you gave me” Foss.] which you gave me to do. And now glorify me [Note: [Col. 0697D] “glorify me, Father” Lin.] in your own presence with the glory that I had with you before the world came to be” (John XVII, 3).

Likewise Paul to the Colossians: “Who is the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of all creation” (Col. I, 15). Likewise there: “The firstborn from the dead, so that he himself might hold primacy in all things.”

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “I am α and ω, the beginning and the end. To him who thirsts I shall freely give from the fountain of the water of life [Note: [Col. 0697D] “of living water, freely” NC. 1, 2. Lam.]” (Apoc. XXI, 6).

That the same is both the Wisdom and the Power of God. Paul in First Corinthians: “Since the Jews desire signs [Note: [Col. 0697D] “ask for signs” Lin.], and the Greeks seek prudence [Note: [Col. 0697D] Bod. 1, Voss. 3, Morell., and Tert. read “wisdom.” In Greek, σοφία (*sophia*, “wisdom”). “Prudence” in most printed editions and manuscripts.]. But we preach Christ crucified: to the Jews, [Col. 0697C] indeed, a stumbling block; to the Gentiles, foolishness; but to those who are called, Jews and Greeks alike, Christ the Power of God and the Wisdom of God” (I Cor. I, 22).

## CHAPTER II.—THAT CHRIST IS THE WISDOM OF GOD; AND CONCERNING THE MYSTERY OF HIS INCARNATION [Note: [Col. 0697D] “concorporation” Lin. NC. 2. Thu. Bod. 3, 4.], HIS PASSION, THE CUP AND THE ALTAR, AND THE APOSTLES WHO WERE SENT AND PREACHED

In Solomon, in Proverbs: “Wisdom built herself a house and placed beneath it [Note: [Col. 0697D] “hewed out” Lam. NC. 1.] seven pillars. She slaughtered [Col. 0698A] her victims [Note: [Col. 0697D] “her victim” Thu. Foss. Corb.], mixed her wine in the bowl [Note: [Col. 0697D] “wine in the bowl” Lam. Thu. Corb. NC. Bod. 1, 2; “into the bowl” Bod. 3.], prepared her table, and sent her servants, summoning people with a proclamation from on high to the bowl, saying: ‘Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me.’ And to those lacking understanding she said: ‘Come, eat of my loaves and drink the wine that I have mixed for you. Forsake folly, seek prudence, and correct knowledge through understanding’ [Note: [Col. 0698C] “receive knowledge and understanding” Bod. 1, 4.]” (Prov. IX, 1ff.).

## CHAPTER III.—THAT CHRIST IS LIKEWISE THE WORD OF GOD

In Psalm XLIV: “My heart has poured forth a good word; I declare my works to the king” (Ps. XLIV, 1).

Likewise in Psalm XXXII: “By the Word [Note: [Col. 0698C] Thus Bod. 3, Foss., Spir., Remb., Eras. More recent printed editions and most manuscripts have: “By the Word of God the heavens were established.” “They were made firm” Oxon.] of God the heavens were established, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their power” (Ps. XXXII, 6).

Likewise in Isaiah: “A word completing and shortening in [Col. 0698B] righteousness; for God will make a shortened word throughout the whole world” (Isa. XVI, 23).

Likewise in Psalm CVI: “He sent his word [Note: [Col. 0698C] “his Word” Bod. 2. Lam. NC. 2.], and healed them” (Ps. CVI, 20).

Likewise in the Gospel according to John: “In the beginning was the Word [Note: [Col. 0698D] “was the Word” NC. 1, 2. Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4; and so thereafter.], and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He [Note: [Col. 0698D] “This was” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Foss. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made. In him was life [Note: [Col. 0698D] “Life is” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb. Ver. Benev. Man.; “What was made, in him was life” Pam. Rig.], and the life was the light of humankind; and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it [Note: [Col. 0698D] “and the darkness did not comprehend him” Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Corb.]” (John I, 1).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse; and the one seated upon it was called Faithful and True, judging with equity and justice [Note: [Col. 0698D] “true, and with justice” Bod. 1.], and he fought [Note: [Col. 0698D] Thus Mor. Man.; “they fought” Pam. Rig.; “warrior” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Voss. 3. Thu. Corb.; “judging and about to fight” Foss. Spir. Rem. Eras.]. He was covered with a garment sprinkled [Note: [Col. 0698D] “a garment sprinkled with blood” Thu. Corb.] with blood, and his name is called the Word of God” (Apoc. XIX, 11).

[Note: [Col. 0699D]

**CHAPTER IV.—Likewise there: “Behold, I have made you.”** Morellius was the first to attach this passage to this chapter. In his edition, however, it reads *in se retornatas*. Because certain old books that Pamelius had seen displayed *in se resformatas*, and because the English edition makes a note about certain old books, Pamelius thought that one ought to write *in serram formatas* (“fashioned into a saw”). I do not dispute whether this emendation is sound.]

## CHAPTER IV.—THAT CHRIST IS LIKEWISE THE HAND AND ARM OF GOD

[Col. 0698C]

In Isaiah: “Surely the hand of God is not powerless to save? Or has he made his ear heavy, so that he cannot hear? But your sins [Note: [Col. 0698D] “our sins” Bod. 3.] separate you from God, and because of your sins [Note: [Col. 0698D] “because of your debts” Veron.] he has turned his face away from you, lest he show mercy. For your hands are stained with blood [Note: [Col. 0698D] “your hands are full of blood” NC. 2. Bod. 3.], and your fingers with sins. Your lips have spoken crime, and your tongue meditates injustice [Note: [Col. 0698D] “will meditate injustice” Thu.]. No one speaks true things, nor is there true judgment. They trust in vanities [Col. 0699A] [Note: [Col. 0699C] “They put their trust in vanities” Bod. 1.] and speak empty things, conceiving pain [Note: [Col. 0699C] “who conceive pain” Bod. 4.] and giving birth to crime” (Isa. LIX, 1).

Likewise there: “Lord, who has believed what we heard? And to whom has the arm of God been revealed?” (Isa. LIII, 1).

Likewise in the same author: “Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth the footstool of my feet [Note: [Col. 0699C] “the stool of my feet” Bod. 1, 2, 3. Lam. NC. 1.]. What seat will you build for me [Note: [Col. 0699C] “What house will you build?” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Foss.]? Or what place is there for my rest? For my hand made all these things” (Isa. LXVI, 1).

Likewise in the same author: “Lord God, your arm is exalted, and they did not know it; but when they know it, they will be confounded [Note: [Col. 0699C] “But those who did not know will be confounded” Lin.]” (ibid. XXVI, 11).

Likewise in the same author: “The Lord has revealed that holy arm of his in the sight of all the nations. All the nations, the utmost parts of the earth themselves, will see salvation from God [Note: [Col. 0699C] “the salvation of God” Bod. 3, 4. What follows is absent from Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Thu. Foss. Corb. Benev. Ver. Spir. V. [Col. 0699D] Innom. Remb. Eras. Manut.]” (ibid. LII, 10).

Likewise there: “Behold, I have made you like the new, turned-back wheels of a threshing vehicle [Note: [Col. 0699D] “into a saw” Veron. and Benev.; *in seres formatas* (“fashioned into *seres*” [reading uncertain]) Voss. 4, two manuscripts, Pam.]; and [Col. 0699B] you will thresh [286] the mountains and grind the hills fine, make them like down, and winnow them; the wind will seize them and the tempest scatter them. But you will rejoice in the holy ones of Israel, and the poor and needy will exult. For they will seek water, and there will be none; their tongue will dry up from thirst. I, the Lord God, I, the God of Israel, shall hear and shall not forsake them; rather, I shall open rivers among the mountains and springs in the midst of the plains. I shall turn deserts into watery groves and the thirsty land into aqueducts. In waterless land I shall plant cedar and boxwood, myrtle and cypress [Note: [Col. 0699D] “myrrh and cypress” Pam. Rig.; “and elm and poplar” NC. 2. Bod. 1, 3, 4.], elm and poplar, so that they may see and know and understand and believe together that the hand of the Lord has made these things and the Holy One of Israel has displayed them” (Isa. XLI, 15–20).

## CHAPTER V.—THAT CHRIST IS BOTH ANGEL AND GOD

[Col. 0699C] In Genesis, to Abraham: “And the Angel of the Lord called him from heaven and said to him: ‘Abraham, Abraham.’ And he said: ‘Here I am.’ And he said: ‘Do not lay your hand upon the boy, nor do anything to him. For now I know that you fear your God [Note: [Col. 0699D] “you fear the Lord your God” Bod. 1, 2, 3.], and have not spared your most beloved son [Note: [Col. 0699D] “your beloved son” Bod. 1, 3. Ver. Benev.] because of me’” (Gen. XXII, 11, 12).

Likewise there, to Jacob: “And the Angel of the Lord said to me in a dream: ‘I am the God whom [Col. 0700A] you saw in the place of God, where [Note: [Col. 0699D] “in the place where” Bod. 3.] you anointed for me a stone monument and vowed a vow to me’” (Gen. XXXI, 13).

Likewise in Exodus: “Now God went before them, by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way [Note: [Col. 0700C] “showing them the way” Bod. 2.], and by night in a pillar of fire” (Exod. XIII, 21). And afterward there: “Then the Angel of God, who went before the army of the children of Israel, moved onward” (ibid. XIV, 19).

Likewise there: “Behold, I send my Angel before your face, to guard you on the way and lead you into the land [Note: [Col. 0700C] “into the good land” Bod. 1.] that I have prepared for you. Heed him [Note: [Col. 0700C] “him; do not be disobedient” Thu. Foss. Corb.; “him, for he will not” Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Corb. Spir.], obey him, and do not be disobedient to him, and he will not fail you. For my name is in him” (ibid. XXIII, 20, 21).

Hence he himself says in the Gospel: “I came in my Father’s name, and you did not receive me. When another comes in his own name, you will receive him” (John V, 43). And again in Psalm CXVII: [Col. 0700B] “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”

Likewise in Malachi [Note: [Col. 0700C] “Likewise in Malachi.” This and what follows are lacking in Benev. and Ver. Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 1, 2. V. Innom. mss. R. Thu. Foss. Corb.]: “My covenant was with life and peace, and I gave him [Note: [Col. 0700D] “I gave him fear of me” Bod. 3.] fear, that he might fear me, and that he might depart from the presence of my name. The law of truth was in his mouth [Note: [Col. 0700D] “his mouth, and injustice” Bod. 1.], and no injustice was found on his lips. Correcting in the peace of the tongue [Note: [Col. 0700D] “correcting in peace” NC. 2.], he walked with us and turned many away from injustice. For the lips of the priest will preserve knowledge, and they will seek the law from his mouth, because he is the Angel [Note: [Col. 0700D] “the Angel of the Lord” Bod. 1, 2, 4.] of the Almighty” (Mal. II, 5–7).

[Note: [Col. 0700D]

**CHAPTER VI.—That Christ.** See Erasmus’s *Annotations* on the first chapter of the Gospel according to John.

**Likewise in Malachi.** This and what follows as far as the end of the chapter are lacking in the old editions and in certain manuscript codices, as is also noted in the English edition. Morellius added it.

**CHAPTER VI.—They will fall into confusion.** In chapter XLIV of Lactantius’s *Epitome*, the printed reading is “into confession.” Pfaffius noted that perhaps “confusion” ought to be read. Correctly so. For Lactantius, book IV, chapter 13, when citing this same passage, wrote “confusion.”

**Put your finger here.** Avitus cites this passage from another version in Epistle III.

**God blessed.** It is certain that the word “God” does not occur [Col. 0702D] in the Fossatensis codex, as the most illustrious bishop of Oxford noted long ago. But it does occur in several others—at least fifteen that I have seen—and in the editions of Manutius and Morellius. In the margin of the edition called Gravius’s, however, the following note appears at this passage: “It is astonishing that ‘God’ is not added even in the most ancient copies, since it is present among the Greeks.” The same word also occurs [Col. 0703D] in Tertullian’s book *Against Praxeas*, where he cites this passage of Paul.]

## CHAPTER VI.—THAT CHRIST IS GOD

In Genesis: “Then God said to Jacob: ‘Arise and ascend to the place [Note: [Col. 0700D] “descend to the place” Lam. NC. 1.] Bethel; dwell there and there make an altar to that God who appeared to you when you fled from the face of your brother Esau’” (Gen. XXXV, 1).

Likewise in Isaiah: [Col. 0700C] “Thus says the Lord God Sabaoth: Egypt has grown weary, and the merchandise of the Ethiopians, and the tall men of Sabaim, will pass over to you and will be your servants; they will walk behind you [Note: [Col. 0700D] “and afterward they will walk” Foss.], bound in fetters, and they will worship you and pray to you, because God is in you, and there is no other God [Note: [Col. 0700D] “and there is no other” Bod. 1, 3.] besides you. For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior. All who oppose you will be confounded and ashamed, and they will fall into confusion [Note: [Col. 0700D] “in confusion” Thu. Foss.]” (Isa. XLV, 14–16).

Likewise in the same author: “The voice of one crying in the desert [Col. 0701A] [Note: [Col. 0701C] “in the wilderness” NC. 1. Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4.]: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0701C] “a way for the Lord” Bod. 3, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.]; make straight the paths of our God. Every stream [Note: [Col. 0701C] “every valley” NC. 2.] will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be made low; all crooked things [Note: [Col. 0701C] “all perverse things” NC. 2.] will become straight, and rough places a plain [Note: [Col. 0701C] “rough places into level roads” NC. 2.]. And the glory of the Lord will be seen [Note: [Col. 0701C] “all the glory” Bod. 3, 4. Foss.], and all flesh will see the salvation of God, because the Lord has spoken’” (Isa. XL, 3–5).

Likewise in Jeremiah: “This is our God [Note: [Col. 0701C] “This is my God” Bod. 3.], and no other will be accounted [Note: [Col. 0701C] “will be reckoned” Lin.] besides him, who discovered the whole way of prudence and gave it to Jacob [Note: [Col. 0701C] “and gave Jacob” Thu.; “to his beloved” Foss.], his servant, and to Israel, his beloved. After these things he was seen upon the earth and lived among human beings” (Baruch III, 35).

Likewise in Zechariah God says: “And they will pass through the narrow sea, strike the waves in the sea, and dry up [Note: [Col. 0701C] “and all will dry up” NC. 2.] all the depths of the rivers; every injury [287] of the Assyrians will be confounded [Note: [Col. 0701D] “all the injuries of the Assyrians will be confounded” Foss.], and the scepter of Egypt [Note: [Col. 0701D] “will be transferred” Bod. 1; “will be turned away” NC. Lam. Bod. 2.] will be taken away. And I shall strengthen them [Col. 0701B] in the Lord their God, and in his name they will glory, says the Lord” (Zech. X, 11, 12).

Likewise in Hosea the Lord says: “I shall not act according to the wrath of my indignation; I shall not permit Ephraim to be destroyed, because I am God and not a man, holy in you [Note: [Col. 0701D] “a man among the holy ones” Lamb. Bod. 2. Thu. Lin. NC. 1.], and I shall not enter [Note: [Col. 0701D] “I shall not go” Thu.] the city; I shall go after God” (Hos. XI, 9, 10).

Likewise in Psalm XLIV: “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the rod of equity is the rod of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated [Note: [Col. 0701D] “held in hatred” Lin. Thu. Corb.] iniquity [Note: [Col. 0701D] “injustice” Bod. 1, 4.]. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of exultation above your companions [Note: [Col. 0701D] “of gladness beyond your associates” NC. 2. Bod. 3.]” (Ps. XLIV, 7, 8).

Likewise in Psalm XLV: “Be still and know that I am God. I shall be exalted among the nations and exalted upon the earth” (Ps. LXV, 11).

Likewise in Psalm LXXXI: “They have neither known [Note: [Col. 0701D] “They have known me neither” Bod. 1.] nor understood; they will walk in shadow [Note: [Col. 0701D] “they walk” NC. 1. Lam.; “they walked” Lin.]” (Ps. LXXXI, 5).

Likewise in Psalm LXVII: “Sing to God; make melody [Col. 0701C] to his name; make a way for him who ascends toward the west: God is his name [Note: [Col. 0701D] “his name is” Bod. 1, 4.]” (Ps. LXVII, 3).

Likewise in the Gospel according to John: “In the beginning was the Word [Note: [Col. 0702C] “In the beginning there was” Thu. Foss. Corb.; “the Word” Lam. Bod. 2, 3, 4. NC. 1, 2.], and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John I, 1).

Likewise, in the same Gospel, the Lord says to Thomas: “Put your finger here and see my hands, and do not be unbelieving but faithful.” Thomas answered and said to him: “My Lord [Col. 0702A] and my God.” Jesus said to him: “Because you have seen me [Note: [Col. 0702C] “you have seen, you have believed” Bod. 1, 2, 4; “you have seen me, Thomas” Lin. Bod. 3; “they will believe” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.], you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed” (John XX, 27–29).

Likewise Paul to the Romans: “I myself wished to be anathema from Christ for the sake of my brothers and kinsmen [Note: [Col. 0702C] “my brothers, my kinsmen” Lam. Bod. 1, 2. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Thu. Corb.] according to the flesh, who are Israelites, to whom belong adoption, glory, the covenant, the establishment of the law, the service, and the promises; whose are the fathers [Note: [Col. 0702C] “whose are the fathers” NC. 1. Lam.], and from whom, according to the flesh, is Christ, who is over all things, God blessed forever” (Rom. IX, 3–5).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “I am α and ω [Note: [Col. 0702C] “I, α and ω” Bod. 1, 2.], the beginning and the end. To him who thirsts I shall freely give from the fountain of the water of life [Note: [Col. 0702C] “of living water” Foss.]. Whoever conquers [Note: [Col. 0702C] “whoever drinks” NC. 1. Lam.] will possess these things and their inheritance; and I shall be his God, and he will be my son” (Apoc. XXI, 6, 7).

Likewise in Psalm LXXXI: “God stood in the assembly of gods, and in their midst he judges the gods.” And again there: “I said: You are gods and all sons of the Most High; but you will die like human beings” (Ps. LXXXI, 1, 6, 7).

But if the righteous—those who have lived righteously and obeyed the divine commandments—can be called gods, how much more can Christ, the Son of God, be called God [Note: [Col. 0702D] “Christ, God’s Son” Foss.]? Thus he himself [Note: [Col. 0702D] “Just as he himself” Lin. NC. 1, 2. Thu. Foss. Corb.] says in the Gospel according to John: “Is it not written in the Law that I said: ‘You are gods’? If he called those gods [Note: [Col. 0702D] “called those gods, and it cannot” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.] to whom the word of God came—and Scripture cannot be annulled—do you say of the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme’ [Note: [Col. 0702D] “you are blasphemed” Bod. 1.], because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’? But if [Note: [Col. 0702D] “I am. If I do not” Thu. Foss. Corb.] I do not perform the works of the Father, do not believe me [Note: [Col. 0702D] “do not believe me; but if you are unwilling to believe me” Thu. Foss.]; but if I do perform them, and you are unwilling to believe me, believe the works, and know that the Father is in me and I in him” (John X, 34).

Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “And you will call his name Emmanuel, which is interpreted ‘God with us’” (Matt. I, 23).

## CHAPTER VII.—THAT CHRIST, GOD, WOULD COME AS THE ILLUMINATOR AND SAVIOR OF THE HUMAN RACE

[Col. 0702C]

In Isaiah: “Be strengthened, you feeble hands, and you weak knees; take courage [Note: [Col. 0702D] “Take courage, you who are fainthearted” Ver. Benev.]. You who are fainthearted [Note: [Col. 0702D] “Do not fear, do not be afraid” Thu. Foss.], do not be afraid. Our God will render judgment; he himself will come and save us. Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, [Col. 0703A] and the ears of the deaf will hear. Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will be fluent, because water has broken forth in the desert and a stream in the thirsty land” (Isa. XXXV, 3–6).

Likewise there: “Neither an elder nor an angel [Note: [Col. 0703C] “not an elder, nor an angel” Lam. and Bod. 3.], but the Lord himself will deliver them, because he will love them [Note: [Col. 0703C] “he loves them” Foss. Lam.; “them, and he himself will redeem” Thu. Corb.] and spare them, and he himself will redeem them” (Isa. LXIII, 9).

Likewise there: “I, the Lord God, have called you in righteousness, that I might hold your hand; I shall strengthen you and have given you as a covenant of my race, as a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring forth from bonds [Note: [Col. 0703C] “to bring forth out of bonds” Bod. 1.] those who are bound, and from the prison-house those who sit in darkness. I am the Lord God; this is my name [Note: [Col. 0703C] “God. My glory” Foss.]. I shall not give my glory to another, nor my powers to carved images” (Isa. XLII, 6–8).

Likewise in Psalm XXIV: “Show me your ways, Lord [288] [Note: [Col. 0703C] “make them known to me” NC. 2.], teach me your paths, lead me to your truth, and teach [Col. 0703B] me, because you, O God, are my Savior” (Ps. XXIV, 4–5).

Hence in the Gospel according to John the Lord says: “I am the light of the world [Note: [Col. 0703D] “I am the light of the world” Bod. 3.]. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life” (John VIII, 12).

Likewise according to Matthew, the angel Gabriel says to Joseph: “Joseph, son of David, do not fear [Note: [Col. 0703D] “do not be afraid” Lam. NC. 2. Lin. Bod. 3, 4.] to take Mary [Note: [Col. 0703D] “Mary your wife” NC. 1, 2. Lam.] as your wife. For that which will be born of her is of the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus. For he will save his people from their sins” (Matt. I, 20, 21).

Likewise according to Luke: “And Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: ‘Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who has looked toward the redemption [Note: [Col. 0703D] “who has accomplished redemption” NC. 2.] of his people and has raised up [Note: [Col. 0703D] “has caused to arise” NC. 2.] for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant’” (Luke I, 67, 68).

Likewise there, the Angel says to the shepherds: “Do not be afraid. For behold, [Col. 0703C] I announce to you that today a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ Jesus, in the city of David” (ibid. II, 7, 8).

**CHAPTER VIII.—Concerning the spirit of Antichrist.** See Erasmus’s annotations on this passage of Peter.]

## CHAPTER VIII.—THAT, ALTHOUGH HE HAD BEEN THE SON OF GOD FROM THE BEGINNING, HE WAS TO BE BEGOTTEN ANEW ACCORDING TO THE FLESH

In Psalm II: “The Lord said to me: ‘You are my Son; today I have begotten you [Note: [Col. 0703D] “today I have generated you” Bod. 4.]. Ask of me [Note: [Col. 0703D] “request of me” Lin. Bod. 1. Thu. Foss.; “seek” NC. 2.], and I shall give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession’” (Ps. II, 7, 8).

Likewise in the Gospel according to Luke: “And it happened [Note: [Col. 0703D] “And it happened, when she heard” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb. Ver. Benev.] that, when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the infant leaped in her womb; and she was filled with the Holy Spirit, [Col. 0704A] cried out with a loud voice, and said: ‘Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And how does it happen to me that the mother of my Lord should come [Note: [Col. 0703D] “that the mother of the Lord” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] to me?’” (Luke I, 41–43).

Likewise Paul to the Galatians: “But when the fulfillment of time arrived [Note: [Col. 0703D] “the completion” Thu. Voss. Corb.; “the fullness” Lin. Bod. 3.], God sent his Son, born of a woman [Note: [Col. 0703D] “born of a virgin” Lin. Bod. 3, 4.]” (Gal. IV, 4).

Likewise in the Epistle of John: “Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God. But the one who denies that he has come in the flesh is not from God [Note: [Col. 0703D] “has not been born of God, but is Antichrist” Bod. 3.], but is of the spirit of Antichrist” (I John IV, 2, 3).

## CHAPTER IX.—THAT THIS WOULD BE THE SIGN OF HIS NATIVITY: THAT MAN AND GOD, THE SON OF MAN AND OF GOD, WOULD BE BORN OF A VIRGIN

In Isaiah: “And the Lord continued speaking to Ahaz, saying [Note: [Col. 0704C] “Ahaz, ask” Thu. Foss. Corb. Bod. 1, 3, 4.]: ‘Ask for yourself a sign from God your Lord, in the height [Col. 0704B] [Note: [Col. 0704C] “in the height” Bod. 1.] above and in the depth below.’ And Ahaz said: ‘I shall not ask, and I shall not tempt the Lord my God.’ And he said: ‘Hear, therefore, O house of David [Note: [Col. 0704C] “therefore, O house of Jacob” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. NC. 1. Lin.]. Is it not a small [Note: [Col. 0704C] “Will it be a small” NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] contest for you to contend with human beings, since God supplies the contest? Therefore God himself will give you a sign. Behold, a virgin will conceive in her womb and bear a son, and you will call [Note: [Col. 0704C] “and you will call the name” Thu. Foss. Corb.; “will be called” Bod. 3; [Col. 0704D] “Jesus” Bod. 3.] his name Emmanuel. He will eat butter and honey [Note: [Col. 0704D] “will eat” Lin.] before he knows how to reject evil and choose good [Note: [Col. 0704D] “Before he knows to prefer evil things, he will exchange the good” Voss. 3, 4. Thu. Cor. Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Oxon.; “he exchanges” Voss. 3, 4. Benev.; “having been exchanged” Ver. printed editions; “he knows how to reject evil and choose good.”]’” (Isa. VII, 10–15).

God had foretold that this seed would proceed from a woman and crush the head of the devil. In Genesis: “Then God said to the serpent: ‘Because you have done this, you are accursed above every kind [Note: [Col. 0704D] “above every beast, and above” Lam. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.] of beast of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you will crawl, and the earth will be food for you all the days of your life. And I shall put enmity between you and the woman, and between her seed [Note: [Col. 0704D] “your seed and her seed” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.]. He will watch [Col. 0704C] [Note: [Col. 0704D] “She will watch” Benev. Ver. NC. 1. Lam. Bod. 2, 3.] your head, and you will watch his heel’” (Gen. III, 14, 15).

## CHAPTER X.—THAT CHRIST IS BOTH MAN AND GOD, COMPOUNDED OF BOTH KINDS, SO THAT HE COULD BE MEDIATOR BETWEEN US AND THE FATHER

In Jeremiah [Note: [Col. 0704D] “In Jeremiah it is said” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3, 4.]: “And he is a man, and who will know him?” (Jer. XVII, 9).

Likewise there: “A man will proceed from his seed and rule over many nations; his kingdom will be exalted like [Note: [Col. 0704D] “Gog will be exalted” Oxon.; “a giant” Bod. 1.] Gog, and [Col. 0705A] his kingdom will be increased. God brought him out of Egypt [Note: [Col. 0705C] “out of Egypt; his glory” Bod. 1.]; the radiance of a unicorn is his [Note: [Col. 0705C] “of a unicorn; and he will eat” NC. 1, 2. Lam. Lin. Thu. Foss.], and he will devour the nations of his enemies [Note: [Col. 0705C] “the flesh of his enemies” Foss.], extract the marrow from their fatness, and pierce the enemy with his ballistae [Note: [Col. 0705C] “will break” Bod. 1; “will destroy” Lin. 2. Bod. 3, 4.]. Lying down [Note: [Col. 0705C] Thus Bod. 1, 2, 3. Lam. Lin. Thu. Foss. Cor. NC. 1, 2; “reclining” Oxon.], he rested like a lion and like a lion’s cub. Who will rouse him? Hence in the Gospel according to Luke, Gabriel [Note: [Col. 0705C] “the angel Gabriel” Bod. 1.] says to Mary [Note: [Col. 0705C] “said to the Virgin Mary” Bod. 3, 4.]: “And the Angel answered and said to her: ‘The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you [Note: [Col. 0705D] “will cast its shadow upon you” Bod. 2. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.]. Therefore [Note: [Col. 0705D] “Therefore that holy thing which will be born of you” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Bod. 1, 3, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.] the holy thing that will be born [Col. 0705B] of you will be called the Son of God’” (Luke I, 35).

## CHAPTER XI.—THAT HE WAS TO BE BORN OF THE SEED OF DAVID ACCORDING TO THE FLESH

In the Second Book of Kingdoms (*Basileion*): “And the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying: ‘Go and say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord: You will not build me a house in which to dwell; but when your days have been fulfilled and you have fallen asleep with your fathers, I shall raise up your seed [Col. 0705C] after you, who will come from your womb, and I shall establish his kingdom. I shall be a father to him, and he will be a son to me; and his house will attain faithfulness, and his kingdom will endure forever in my sight’” (II Kings VII, 4, 5, 12, 14, 16).

Likewise in Isaiah: “And a rod will come forth [Note: [Col. 0705D] “came forth” Corb.; “will come forth” Thu.] from the root of Jesse, and a flower from his root [Col. 0706A] will rise [Note: [Col. 0705D] “descending from his root” Corb.]; and the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety; and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him [Note: [Col. 0706C] “of the fear of God” Thu. Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I saw a book in the right hand of God, who was seated [Col. 0706B] upon the throne, written within and on the back [Note: [Col. 0706C] “written within and secretly” NC. 2; “outside” Bod. 1.], sealed with seven signs [Note: [Col. 0706C] “seals” Bod. 1. Lam. Lin. NC. 1.]. And I saw a mighty Angel proclaiming with a loud voice: ‘Who is worthy to receive the book and open its signs?’ No one was able, either in heaven or upon the earth [Note: [Col. 0706C] “on earth” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lam. Lin. NC. 1.], or beneath the earth [Note: [Col. 0706C] “beneath the earth” Bod. 2, 3, 4.], to open the book or even to look into it. And I wept greatly because no one worthy [Note: [Col. 0706C] “no one worthy on earth” Bod. 1–4. Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] had been found to open the book or see it. And one of the elders said to me: ‘Do not weep; behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, so as to open the book and loose [Note: [Col. 0706C] “and the seven” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.] its seven signs’” (Apoc. V, 1–5).

[Note: [Col. 0705D]

CHAPTER XII.—With gifts. I have added these two words in accordance with the old editions, among which I also include those of Manutius and Morel. Pamelius struck them out as superfluous; Rigault and the English editors did likewise. Yet they occur in the Fossatensis manuscript, in the Beccensis, and in the very ancient manuscript 87 of Marmoutier [Col. 0706D] at Tours. The ancient author of the book *On Rebaptism*, p. 359, likewise read the text in this way. Indeed, in both ancient and modern missals the following antiphon is read on Epiphany: “We saw his star in the East, and have come with gifts to worship the Lord.”

In Micah: “And you, Bethlehem, house [Note: [Col. 0706D] “Bethlehem, his house” Lin. Bod. 1, 4. NC. 2. Thu. Foss. Corb.; “are you by any means small?” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Lin. NC. 2.] of Ephrathah, are not too small to be numbered among the thousands of Judah. NC. 1.] are from the beginning, from the days of eternity” (Mic. 5:2).

Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lin. NC. 1, 2.] from the East to Jerusalem, saying: ‘Where is he who has been born King of the Jews? ## CHAPTER XIII.—THAT HE WOULD COME IN HUMILITY AT HIS FIRST ADVENT

[Col. 0707A]

In Isaiah: “Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0707C] “The arm of God” Thu.; “has been announced” Lin.] been revealed? He has neither form nor splendor; and we saw him, and he had neither form nor beauty, but his appearance was without honor and inferior to all other men: a man given over to affliction and knowing how to bear weakness [Note: [Col. 0707D] “To bear infirmity” Lin.]; because his face was turned away [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Because his face was turned” Thu.; “his face was hostile” Foss.], he was dishonored and was not [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Was not changed” Bod. 1, 2.] esteemed. 290 He bears [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Bore” Bod. 1, 2, 3.] our sins and suffers [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Suffered” Bod. 1; “suffering” Bod. 3.] for us, and we thought [Note: [Col. 0707D] “We were thinking” Corb.] him to be in pain, affliction, and torment. But he was wounded because of our crimes and weakened because of our sins. The discipline of our peace was upon [Col. 0707B] him, and by his bruise [Note: [Col. 0707D] “By his bruise we all” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] we were healed. We all went astray like sheep; each man went astray on his own path. And God handed him over for our sins, and because he was afflicted, he did not open his mouth” (Isa. 53:1–7).

Likewise in the same prophet: “I am not rebellious, nor do I contradict; I gave my back to scourges and my cheeks to blows; I did not turn [Note: [Col. 0707D] “My face” Bod. 1. Likewise in Psalm 21: “But I am a worm and not a man, the accursed thing [Note: [Col. 0707D] “A man, the reproach” Lin.] of humankind and [Col. 0707C] the outcast [Note: [Col. 0707D] “A curse” Bod. 3; “accursed” Bod. 1; “of the people” Lin. Bod. 3; “the outcast of men” Thu. Foss. Corb.] of the people. All who saw me despised me [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Mocked me” Lin. NC. 2.], spoke with their lips [Note: [Col. 0707D] “With their own lips” Bod. 1.], and shook their heads. ‘He trusted in the Lord; let him rescue him. Likewise there: “My strength has dried up like a potsherd [Note: [Col. 0707D] “My strength like a potsherd” NC. Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.; “an earthen vessel” Ver.], and my tongue [Note: [Col. 0707D] “Has adhered” Lin. NC. 2.] has stuck to my throat.”

Likewise in Zechariah: “And the Lord showed me Jesus, that great priest, standing before the Angel of the Lord; and the devil stood at his right hand to oppose [Note: [Col. 0708C] “Began to oppose him” Corb. And he answered and said to those standing before him: ‘Take away [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Turn away his garments” Bod. 1.] the filthy garments from him.’ And he said to him: ‘Behold, I have taken away your iniquities. And clothe him in a full-length robe [Note: [Col. 0708D] *Podere* Lam. NC. 1.], [Col. 0708A] and place a clean turban upon his head’” (Zech. 3:1, 3–5).

Likewise Paul to the Philippians: “He, being established in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself [Note: [Col. 0708D] “But emptied himself” Lin. Ver. NC. 1, 2. Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3.], taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men [Note: [Col. 0708D] “In the likeness of man” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Thu. Corb.], and found in appearance as a man [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Found as a man” Thu.]. He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death—even death on a cross. Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name [Note: [Col. 0708D] “A name such that it is” Lin. Thu. Cor. Benev. Ver.] which is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend [Note: [Col. 0708D] “All should bend the knee” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Thu. Cor.; “should bow” Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 1, 4. Ver.]—of those in heaven, on earth, and beneath the earth—and every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Jesus is in the glory of God the Father” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. ## CHAPTER XIV.—THAT HE IS THE RIGHTEOUS ONE WHOM THE JEWS WOULD KILL

[Col. 0708B] In the Wisdom of Solomon: “Let us entrap the righteous man, because he is disagreeable [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Because he is useless to us” NC. 2.] to us and opposed to our works, and reproaches us [Note: [Col. 0708D] “And upbraids us” Corb. Ver.] for sins against the Law. He professes to possess knowledge of God and calls himself the Son of God. He has become a reproof [Note: [Col. 0708D] “A reproof of our thoughts” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] to our thoughts; he is burdensome to us even to behold, because his life is unlike that of others, and his ways have been changed. We have been regarded by him as triflers [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Esteemed as trifles” Lam. Bod. 2; “trifles” NC. 1.], and he keeps himself from our ways as from impurities; he holds up the final end of the righteous, and boasts that he has God as his father [Note: [Col. 0708D] “God as father” Bod. 4. Corb. Thu. Benev. Ver.]. Let us see, then, whether his words are true, and let us test what will happen to him. Let us examine him with insult and torment, so that we may learn his reverence [Note: [Col. 0708D] “His reverence and by death” Bod. 1, 3.] and test his patience. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death.’ These things they devised, and they went astray; for their own wickedness blinded them, [Col. 0708C] and they did not know the mysteries of God” (Wis. 2:12–17).

Likewise in Isaiah: “See how the righteous man perishes, and no one understands; righteous men are taken away, and no one recognizes it. For the righteous man has been removed from the presence of injustice, and his burial shall be in peace [Note: [Col. 0708D] “His memory shall be in peace” Bod. 3; “the righteous man; for he shall be in peace” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 4.]” (Isa. 57:1–2).

Concerning this very matter it was foretold in Exodus: “You shall not kill the innocent and righteous” (Exod. 23:7).

Likewise in the Gospel: “Judas, moved by repentance [Note: [Col. 0708D] “Driven by repentance” NC. 2.], said to the priests and elders: ‘I have sinned by betraying righteous blood’” (Matt. 27:3–4).

[Note: [Col. 0709D]

CHAPTER XV.—*Picridibus*. So the old editions and eight ancient manuscripts. Erasmus wrote “with wild lettuces,” as Pamelius notes that Saint Jerome translated it; this is true. Yet the same Jerome, in his letter to Marcella *On Gifts Received*, says: “Christ’s Passover is eaten with bitter herbs”; and in his letter to Gaudentius *On the Education of a Little Girl*, 600: “The Passover also is commanded to be eaten with bitter herbs.” So too in book II *Against Jovinian*. The manuscripts of Moissac and Grenoble have merely “with bitterness”; the Compiègne manuscript, “with bitterness, with bitter herbs”; the Tours and Corbie manuscripts and three English manuscripts, “with bitter herbs”; the Saint-Éloi manuscript, “with the richness of bitterness.” The Seventy translators used μετὰ πικρίδων, “with bitter herbs.” Jerome, in the prologue to his letter to Algasia: “I myself have seen nausea and dizziness of the head often cured by the antidote called πικρά (*pikra*, ‘the bitter remedy’).” Pliny, book XXII, chapter 22: “*Picris* receives its name from its remarkable bitterness.” [Col. 0710D] See the illustrious Pierre-Daniel Huet in his *Observations on Origen’s Commentaries*, p. 15.

I shall add here, from an ancient manuscript ordinal of the Church of Saint-Aignan at Orléans, a passage that seemed difficult to some when I was in that city. After the ceremonies performed on the third day of Rogations have been described, and after the procession to the church of Saint-Germain has been described, it reads there: “Then the procession departs from the church, singing the litany as far as its own church, in the same order in which they had come, with the one who carries the lettuces going before.” They could not understand what “lettuces” might mean in this passage. It is a copyist’s error: he wrote *lactucas* (“lettuces”) for *lectiones* (“readings”). For above it reads: “The fourth carries the book in which the sermons at Matins were read”; and a little later, after the responsory has been said, “One boy reads the lesson from the book that he brought with him.”]

## CHAPTER XV.—THAT HE WAS CALLED THE SHEEP AND THE LAMB WHO WAS TO BE SLAIN, AND CONCERNING THE MYSTERY 291 OF THE PASSION

In Isaiah: “Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and [Col. 0709A] like a lamb before its shearer [Note: [Col. 0709C] “Its shearer, without” Bod. 3. Thu. Corb.; “those shearing it” Foss.], voiceless, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who shall recount his generation [Note: [Col. 0709C] “But who shall recount his generation?” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.]? For his life shall be taken from the earth; because of the crimes of my people he was led to death. I shall give the wicked for his burial and the rich themselves [Note: [Col. 0709C] “And the rich” Bod. 1.] for his death, because he committed no crime, nor spoke deceit [Note: [Col. 0709C] “Nor was guile found in his mouth” Bod. 3; “plotting with his mouth” Lin.; “he plots” Thu.; “he spoke no deceit with his mouth” Bod. 4.] with his mouth. Therefore he shall obtain many [Note: [Col. 0709C] “He confesses many” Foss.], and shall divide the spoils of the strong, because his soul was handed over to death and he was numbered among criminals. And he bore the sins of many and was handed over because of their crimes” (Isa. 53:7, 9–12).

Likewise in Jeremiah: “Lord, make it known [Note: [Col. 0709C] “Lord, you made it known” NC. 1. Lam.] to me, and I shall know; then I saw their designs [Note: [Col. 0709C] “I saw their thoughts” Thu.]. I, like an innocent lamb, was led to slaughter. They devised a design against me, saying: ‘Come, let us put wood into [Col. 0709B] his bread [Note: [Col. 0709C] “In his bread” Thu. Foss. Corb. Lam.], and let us root out [Note: [Col. 0709C] “Let us remove his life from the earth” Bod. 3; “we shall cast out” Lin. Corb.] his life from the earth, and his name shall no longer be remembered [Note: [Col. 0709C] “For a memorial” Bod. 1, 4.]’” (Jer. 11:18–19).

Likewise in Exodus [Note: [Col. 0709C] “In Exodus God said” NC. 2.] God said to Moses: “Let each take for himself a sheep according to the houses of their tribes [Note: [Col. 0709C] “A sheep according to the tribes” Bod. 3.]; you shall have a sheep without blemish, perfect, male, one year old [Note: [Col. 0709C] “It shall be one year old” Bod. 1.]. You shall take it from the lambs and kids, and the entire multitude [Note: [Col. 0709C] “The entire multitude of the children” Foss.; “all the people” Bod. 3.] of the congregation of the children of Israel shall kill it at evening. And they shall take [Note: [Col. 0709C] “And they shall take some of the blood, and” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] some of its blood and put it upon the two doorposts and upon the lintel of the houses in which they shall eat it [Note: [Col. 0709C] “In which they shall eat” Lam. NC. 1; “these” Thu. Foss. Pla. NC. 2; “and the flesh itself” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Corb.]. They shall eat its flesh that same night, roasted with fire, and they shall eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs (*picridibus*) [Note: [Col. 0709C] “With bitter herbs” Lin. Bod. 1, 4. Corb.]. NC. 2; “but the inward parts by them” Lam. NC. 1, 2.] and inward parts. You shall leave [Col. 0710A] none [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Leaving” Thu. Foss.; “of it” Lin.] of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Bone” Lamb.; “bones” Affl.; “from it” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4.] of it. Whatever remains of it until morning shall be burned with fire. And thus shall you eat it: your loins [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Let your loins be” Bod. 1.] girded, your sandals [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Your footwear” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] on your feet, and your staffs [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Your staffs” Corb.] in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste, for it is the Passover [Note: [Col. 0710C] “It is the Lord’s” Corb.] of the Lord” (Exod. 12:3, 5–11).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I saw in the midst of the throne [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Of the throne, four living creatures” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2.] and the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent throughout the whole earth. And he came and received the book from the right hand of God [Note: [Col. 0710C] “From the right hand of him who sits” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Foss.] who sits upon the throne. And when he had received the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders prostrated themselves before the Lamb, each having harps and golden bowls [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Golden and bowls” Lam. Thu. Bod. 1, 2, 3. NC. 1, 2. Lin.; “golden vessels” Bod. 1. Corb.] full of the incense of supplications, which [Col. 0710B] are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying: ‘You are worthy, Lord, to receive the book and open its signs [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Seals” Bod. 3. NC. 2; “You are worthy to receive” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Lin. Bod. 1, 2.], because you were slain and redeemed us by your blood [Note: [Col. 0710C] “You redeemed us for God” Thu. Foss. Corb.; “you purchased” Ver.; “for our God, and priests, and they shall reign” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 4.] from every tribe and tongue and people and nation; and you made us a kingdom for our God, and made us priests, and they shall reign upon the earth’” (Rev. 5:6–10).

Likewise in the Gospel: “The next day John saw [Note: [Col. 0710C] “John, seeing Jesus coming toward him, said” Lam. Bod. 1, 2. NC. 2, 4. Lin.; “John saw” Foss. Corb.] Jesus coming toward him and said: ‘Behold the Lamb of God [Note: [Col. 0710C] “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Foss.; “will take away” Thu.], and behold him who takes away the sins of the world’” (John 1:29).

## CHAPTER XVI.—THAT HE WAS ALSO CALLED THE STONE

In Isaiah the Lord says thus: “Behold, I lay [Col. 0711A] [Note: [Col. 0711D] “I send” Bod. 1.] in the foundations of Zion a precious, chosen [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Chosen, pure, supreme” Bod. 2. Lam. Lin.], supreme, cornerstone, held in honor; and whoever believes in him shall not be confounded” (Isa. 28:16).

Likewise in Psalm 117: “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord [Note: [Col. 0711D] “This was done, and it is wonderful” Lin. Bod. 3.], and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is the day [Note: [Col. 0711D] “This is the day” Bod. 3.] that the Lord has made; let us exult and rejoice [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Let us be glad” Bod. 3. Lin. NC. 1, 2.] in it. O Lord, save now [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Save; grant prosperity” Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 1. Corb.]; O Lord, direct us now. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord” (Ps. 118:22–26).

Likewise in Zechariah: “Behold, I bring forth my servant. ‘Rising’ [Note: [Col. 0711D] “‘Dawn’ is his name” Lin. NC. 2. Thu. Foss.] is his name; for the stone that I set before Jesus—upon that one stone are seven eyes” (Zech. 3:8–9).

Likewise in Deuteronomy: “And you shall write [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Write upon” Bod. 3, 4.] upon the stone all this Law very plainly” (Deut. 27:8).

Likewise in Joshua son of Nun: “And he took a great stone [Col. 0711B] and set it there before the Lord; and Joshua said to the people: ‘Behold, this stone shall be a testimony to you, because it has heard [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Because you hear everything” Foss.] all that was spoken by the Lord, all that he has said [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Has said to you” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] to you today; and it shall be a testimony to you 292 in the last days, when you have departed from your God’” (Josh. 24:26–27).

Likewise Peter in the Acts of the Apostles: “Rulers of the people and elders of Israel [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Elders of Israel, behold” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Foss. Corb.], listen: Behold, today we are questioned by you concerning the good deed done to an infirm man [Note: [Col. 0711D] “This benefit to the man” Bod. 3.], by what means he was saved. Let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified and whom God raised from the dead [Note: [Col. 0711D] “God roused from the dead” Bod. 1, 3, 4.], in him this man stands healthy before you [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Stood healthy” Foss.], and in no other. He is the stone that was despised by you builders [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Which you will build” Bod. 1. Corb. Ver. Benev.; “was placed at the head” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3, 4.], which has become the head of the corner. For there is no other name under heaven given to humankind in which we must be saved” (Acts 4:8–12).

[Col. 0711C] He is the stone in Genesis (Gen. 28) that Jacob places beneath his head, because Christ is the head of man; and while sleeping he sees a ladder reaching to heaven, upon which the Lord stood, while angels ascended and descended. He consecrated and anointed that stone with the mystery of anointing, signifying Christ [Note: [Col. 0711D] “By the mystery, Christ” Thu.].

He is the stone in Exodus (Exod. 17) upon which Moses sat at the summit of the hill [Note: [Col. 0711D] “Summit of the mountain” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3, 4.] when Joshua son of Nun fought against Amalek [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Was fighting Amalek” Thu. Corb.; “fought by the mystery” Bod. 1.]; and by the mystery of the stone and the steadfastness of his sitting, Amalek was overcome by Joshua—that is, the devil was defeated by Christ.

He is the great stone in the First Book of Kingdoms (1 Sam. 4) upon which the ark of the covenant was placed, when the cattle carried it back on a cart after it had been sent away [Note: [Col. 0712D] “When by” Bod. 3.] and returned by the foreigners.

Likewise, he [Col. 0712A] is the stone in the Book of Kingdoms (1 Sam. 17) with which David struck Goliath on the forehead and killed him, signifying that the devil and his servants are thereby cast down—namely, that part of the head [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Defeated that part of the head” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4; “defeated” Bod. 3. Ver.] being vanquished which they do not have marked [Note: [Col. 0712D] “He would have” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.]. By that sign we too are always protected and live.

He is the stone that Samuel set up after Israel had defeated the foreigners, and whose name he called Ebenezer—that is, “stone of help” [Note: [Col. 0712D] “A helper to the fallen” NC. 2.] (1 Sam. 7:12).

## CHAPTER XVII.—THAT THIS SAME STONE WOULD THEN BECOME A MOUNTAIN AND FILL THE WHOLE EARTH

In Daniel: “And behold, an exceedingly great image, and the appearance of that image, fearsome and lofty, stood before you. Its head was of fine gold, its breast and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, and its feet [Col. 0712B] partly of iron and partly of clay, until a stone was cut from the mountain without the hands of cutters and struck the image upon its feet of iron and clay and crushed them into tiny fragments. Then the iron, earthenware [Note: [Col. 0712D] “And it was shattered all at once” Oxon.], bronze, silver, and gold were all together broken into small pieces; they became like chaff or dust on a threshing floor in summer, and the wind winnowed them away so that nothing remained [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Would remain among them” Bod. 1, 2. Thu.] of them. But the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth” (Dan. 2:31–35).

## CHAPTER XVIII.—THAT IN THE LAST TIMES THIS SAME MOUNTAIN WOULD BE REVEALED, TO WHICH THE NATIONS WOULD COME [Note: [Col. 0712D] “The nations would assemble” Bod. 3.], AND WHICH ALL THE RIGHTEOUS WOULD ASCEND

In Isaiah [Note: [Col. 0712D] “In Isaiah: And it shall be” Bod. 1, 3, 4.]: “In the last times the mountain of the Lord and the house of God shall be manifest above the summits of the mountains, [Col. 0712C] and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall come upon it. Many shall walk and say: ‘Come, let us ascend the mountain of the Lord and enter the house of the God of Jacob; he shall proclaim his way to us, and we shall walk [Note: [Col. 0712D] “And we shall enter” Lam. Bod. 2. Lin.] in it.’ For the Law shall go forth [Note: [Col. 0712D] “The Law shall go forth” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2.] from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. He shall judge among the nations and rebuke many peoples; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Into sickles; and nation shall no longer take up sword against nation, and they shall no longer learn” Ver. Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2; “learn to make war” Lin.], and they shall no longer learn to fight” (Isa. 2:2–5).

Likewise in Psalm 23: “Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in his holy place? One innocent in hands and pure in heart [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Pure in heart” Lam. NC. 1. Thu. Bod. 2.], who has not received his soul in vain and has not sworn deceitfully [Note: [Col. 0712D] “Nor sworn deceitfully” Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 3.] to his neighbor. He shall receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior. This is their generation [Note: [Col. 0712D] “This is the generation of those who seek” Lin. NC. 2.] who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob” (Ps. 23:3–6).

[Note: [Col. 0713]

CHAPTER XIX.—“Was made before me.” See Erasmus’s annotations on the first chapter of the Gospel according to John.]

## CHAPTER XIX.—THAT HE IS THE BRIDEGROOM, HAVING THE CHURCH AS HIS BRIDE, FROM WHOM SPIRITUAL CHILDREN WOULD BE BORN

[Col. 0713A]

293 In Joel: “Sound the trumpet in Zion; sanctify a fast and proclaim a healing; gather the people [Note: [Col. 0713C] “Assemble the people” Bod. 1, 3.]; sanctify the assembly; receive the elders; gather the nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come forth from his chamber [Note: [Col. 0713C] “From his bedchamber” Bod. 1, 2, 4.], and the bride from her bridal room” (Joel 2:15–16).

Likewise in Jeremiah: “And I shall take away from the cities of Judah and the crossroads [Note: [Col. 0713C] “Streets of Jerusalem” NC. 2.] of Jerusalem the voice of those rejoicing and the voice of those exulting, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride” (Jer. 16:9).

Likewise in Psalm 18: “And he is like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber. He exulted like a giant [Note: [Col. 0713C] “Like a giant” Bod. 1, 3; “to run the course” Lam. Lin. [Col. 0713D] Bod. 1, 2, 3. NC. 1, 2.] to run his course. His going forth is from the summit of heaven [Note: [Col. 0713D] “His departure from heaven” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.; “his procession” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.], and his circuit reaches its summit; and there is no one hidden [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Nor is there anyone who can hide himself” Lin. NC. 1, 2; “hidden from his heat” Lam. NC. 2. Bod. 2, 4.] from his heat” (Ps. [Col. 0713B] 18:6–7).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “‘Come, I shall show you the newly married bride, the wife of the Lamb.’ And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great mountain and showed me the holy city Jerusalem descending from heaven, from God, possessing the brightness [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Brightness likewise” Lam.] of God” (Rev. 21:9–11).

Likewise in the Gospel according to John: “You yourselves are my witnesses that I said to those who were sent to me from Jerusalem that I am not the Christ, but that I was sent before him. For he who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom is he who stands, hears him with joy, and rejoices because of the bridegroom’s voice” (John 3:28–29).

The mystery of this matter was shown in Joshua son of Nun, when he was commanded to remove his footwear [Note: [Col. 0713D] “That he should remove his footwear” Lin.], because he himself was not the bridegroom. For it was prescribed in the Law that whoever [Note: [Col. 0713D] “That whoever” Voss. 3. Lam. NC. 1.] refused marriage [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Excused himself from marriage” Bod. 1. Voss. 2.] should remove his shoe [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Should be unshod” Bod. 1.], whereas he who was to become the bridegroom [Col. 0713C] would be shod.

“And it happened when Joshua [Note: [Col. 0713D] “When Joshua was” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 4; “in the field at Jericho” Foss.] was in Jericho that he looked around with his eyes and saw a man standing before him, holding a sword [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Bearing a sword” Thu. Foss. Corb.] in his hand; and he said: ‘Are you one of ours or of our adversaries?’ But he said: ‘I am the commander of the host of the Lord; now I have come.’ And Joshua fell face down [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Upon his face” Bod. 1.] to the earth and said to him: ‘Lord, what do you command your servant [Note: [Col. 0713D] “Command your slave” Lam.]?’ And the commander of the host of the Lord said: ‘Remove the footwear from your feet, for the place upon which you stand is holy ground’” (Josh. 5:13–15).

Likewise in Exodus Moses is commanded to remove his footwear [Note: [Col. 0713D] “To loosen his footwear” Bod. 3.], because neither was he the bridegroom: “And the Angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame [Col. 0714A] of fire from a bush; and he saw that the bush burned with fire, but the bush was not consumed [Note: [Col. 0714C] “Was not burned up” Bod. 1; “was burning” Lam. NC. 2. Bod. 2.]. And Moses said: ‘I shall go over and see [Note: [Col. 0714C] “I shall go and see” Bod. 1.] this great sight, why the bush is not consumed [Note: [Col. 0714C] “Is not burned up” Bod. 1.].’ But when the Lord God saw that he was approaching to see, he called to him from the bush, saying: ‘Moses, Moses.’ He said [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Moses, Moses; and he said, ‘What is it?’”; the remainder is absent from MR.]: ‘What is it?’ And he said: ‘Do not approach here unless you remove the footwear from your feet. For the place upon which you stand is holy ground.’ And he said to him: ‘I am the God of your father [Note: [Col. 0714D] “The God of your fathers” NC. 1.], the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’” (Exod. 3:2–6).

This, moreover, was revealed in the Gospel according to John: “And John answered them: ‘I indeed [Note: [Col. 0714D] “I indeed baptize you” Bod. 1, 3, 4.] baptize in water; but in your midst stands one whom you do not know [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Whom you do not recognize” NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lin.]. For he is the one concerning whom I said: “The man coming after me was made [Note: [Col. 0714D] “The man, and before me” NC. 2. Bod. 1.] before me”; I am not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandal [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Of his sandals” Lam. NC. 2. Bod. 1, 2.]’” (John 1:[Col. 0714B] 26–27).

Likewise according to Luke: “Let your loins be girded [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Your loins girded” Bod. 1, 3, 4.] and your lamps burning [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Burning in your hands” Bod. 3.], and be like men waiting for their master when he comes [Note: [Col. 0714D] “When he returns” Lin. NC. 2.] from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him. Blessed [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Happy servants” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4.] are those servants whom the master, when he comes, finds watching” (Luke 12:35–37).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “The Lord God Almighty has reigned; let us rejoice and exult, and give him glorious [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Give him brightness” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.] splendor, because the wedding of the Lamb has come and his wife has prepared herself” (Rev. 19:6–7).

## CHAPTER XX.—THAT THE JEWS WOULD FASTEN HIM TO A CROSS

In Isaiah: “I spread out my hands all day long to a people insolent and contradicting me, who walk in ways that are not good [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Who do not walk in my ways” Bod. 3.], but after their own sins” (Isa. 65:2).

[Col. 0714C] Likewise in Jeremiah: “Come, let us put wood into his bread [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Wood in his bread” Thu. Corb. Voss.], and let us root out [Note: [Col. 0714D] “Tear from the earth” Bod. 3.] his life from the earth” (Jer. 11:19).

Likewise in Deuteronomy: “And your life shall hang before your eyes; you shall fear by day and night and shall not trust your own life” (Deut. 28:66).

Likewise in Psalm 21: “They dug through my hands and my feet; they counted 294 all my bones. They themselves gazed and looked upon me; they divided my garments among themselves and cast lots for my clothing. But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me; attend to my assistance. Deliver my soul from the sword, and [Col. 0715A] my only one from the power of the dog. Save me from the lion’s mouth and my humiliation from the horns of unicorns. I shall proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I shall praise you” (Ps. 21:17–22).

Likewise in Psalm 118: “Fasten my flesh with nails because of your fear [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Because of your dread” Lin. A little later, “Lifting up” Lin.]” (Ps. 118:120).

Likewise in Psalm 140: “The lifting up of my hands is an evening sacrifice” (Ps. 140:2).

Concerning this sacrifice Zephaniah said: “Be afraid before the Lord God, for his day is near, because the Lord has prepared [Note: [Col. 0715D] “The Lord has prepared” Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lam. NC. 1, 2. Corb.] his sacrifice and sanctified his chosen ones [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Sanctified those called” NC. 1, 2. Corb. Ver.]” (Zeph. 1:7).

Likewise in Zechariah: “And they shall look upon me, whom they pierced” (Zech. 12:10).

Likewise in Psalm 87: “I cried out to you, Lord, all day long; I stretched out my hands to you” (Ps. 87:10).

Likewise in Numbers: “God is not suspended like a man [Note: [Col. 0715D] “A man is suspended” Foss. Corb.; “the Son suffers by man,” Lin.], nor does he suffer threats like a son of man” [Col. 0715B] (Num. 23:19).

Hence in the Gospel [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Then in the Gospel” NC. 2.] the Lord says: “Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in the Son [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Believes in him” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2.] may have eternal life” (John 3:14–15).

## CHAPTER XXI.—THAT IN THE PASSION OF THE CROSS AND IN THE SIGN RESIDE ALL STRENGTH [Note: [Col. 0715D] “In the sign of strength” Lin.; “that there are strength and power” NC. 2. Bod. 1, 3, 4.] AND POWER

In Habakkuk: “His power covered [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Covered the heavens” Bod. 3.] the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise; and his splendor shall be like light [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Shall be like light” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4; “shall be” is absent from Oxon.]; horns shall be in his hands [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Are in his hands” Bod. 1, 4.]. And there the strength of his glory was established, and he established a mighty love. Before his face the word shall go, and shall proceed [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Shall go forth into the fields” Bod. 2, 3.] into the fields according to his steps [Note: [Col. 0715D] “According to his flocks” Lin. Bod. 4.]” (Hab. 3:3–5).

Likewise in Isaiah: “Behold, a child is born to us, and a son is given [Col. 0715C] to us, whose dominion is upon his shoulders; and his name was called ‘messenger of the great design’ [Note: [Col. 0715D] “Messenger of great counsel” Bod. 3.]” (Isa. 9:5).

By this sign of the cross Amalek too was defeated by Joshua through Moses. In Exodus Moses said to Joshua [Note: [Col. 0715D] “To Joshua son of Nun” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]: “Choose men for yourself, go out, and engage Amalek tomorrow [Note: [Col. 0716D] “On the morrow” Corb.; “and I shall stand” Bod. 1, 2.]. Behold, I shall stand on the summit of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand. And it happened that when Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed; but whenever Moses lowered his hands [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Lowered them, Amalek grew strong” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Foss. Corb.], Amalek grew strong. But Moses’ hands were heavy, so they took a stone and placed it beneath him, and he sat upon it. Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on each side, and Moses’ hands remained steady until sunset; and Joshua put [Col. 0716A] Amalek and all his people to flight. And the Lord said to Moses: ‘Write this as a memorial in a book and deliver it into Joshua’s ears [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Into his ears, because” Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 1, 2. Foss.], because I shall utterly erase the memory of Amalek from beneath heaven’” (Exod. 17:9–11).

## CHAPTER XXII.—THAT IN THIS SIGN OF THE CROSS THERE IS SALVATION FOR ALL WHO ARE MARKED [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Are marked” Bod. 3.] UPON THEIR FOREHEADS
In Ezekiel the Lord says: “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a sign upon the foreheads of the men who groan and mourn over the iniquities committed in their midst” (Ezek. IX, 4, 6). Likewise there: “Go [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Go, strike down,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. “Do not,” Bod. 3.] and strike them down, and let your eyes show no pity. Have no mercy upon old man or young man [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Upon old men and young men, virgins and little children,” Bod. 1, Corb. “The old men and,” Bod. 2.] or virgin; kill the little children and the women, so that they may be utterly destroyed. But do not touch anyone upon whom the sign has been written, and begin with my own [Note: [Col. 0716D] “With them, as with my holy ones,” Bod. 3.] holy ones.” Likewise in Exodus, God says to Moses: “And the [Col. 0716B] blood [Note: [Col. 0716D] “That blood,” Bod. 2. “As a sign,” Lin. Bod. 1, 3.] shall be a sign for you upon the houses in which you are; and I shall see the blood and protect you, and there shall be no destructive plague among you when I strike the land of Egypt” (Exod. XII, 13). Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I saw the Lamb standing upon Mount [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Onto the mountain,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] Zion, and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand; and they had his name and the name of his Father written upon their foreheads” (Apoc. XIV, 1). Likewise there: “I am alpha and omega (α et ω), the first and the last, the beginning and the end. Blessed are those who carry out his commandments, so that their authority may extend over the tree of life [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Over the tree,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Benev.]” (Apoc. XXII, 13–14).

[Note: [Col. 0715]

CHAPTER XXIII.—“It shall be darkened.” See Fronton du Duc’s notes on Chrysostom’s Homily VI *To the People of Antioch*.]

## CHAPTER XXIII.—THAT AT MIDDAY, DURING HIS PASSION, THERE WOULD BE DARKNESS

In Amos: “And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord, that the sun shall set at midday, and the daylight shall be darkened; 295 and I shall turn [Col. 0716C] your feast days into mourning and all your songs into lamentation” (Amos VIII, 9–10). Likewise in Jeremiah: “She who gives birth was terrified, and her soul grew weary [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Her soul caused weariness,” NC. 2, Bod. 2.]. Her sun went down while it was still midday; she was confounded and accursed. I shall give the rest of them to the sword [Note: [Col. 0716D] “I shall give them into the sword,” Bod. 1, 2.] in the sight of their enemies” (Jer. XV, 9). Likewise in the Gospel: “Now from the sixth hour darkness came over [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Throughout the whole earth,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. “The entire earth,” Bod. 3.] the whole earth until the ninth hour” (Matt. XXVII, 45).

## CHAPTER XXIV.—THAT HE WOULD NOT BE CONQUERED BY DEATH, NOR WOULD HE REMAIN IN THE LOWER WORLD

In Psalm XXIX: “Lord, you have brought back [Note: [Col. 0716D] “Lord, you have set [my soul] out of the lower world,” NC. 1, Lam. “You have brought forth,” NC. 2, Bod. 1, 2, 4. “You have recalled,” Lin. “Of the lower world,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] my soul from the lower world” [Col. 0717A] (Ps. XXIX, 3). Likewise in Psalm XV: “You will not abandon my soul in the lower world, nor will you permit your holy one to see corruption [Note: [Col. 0717D] “To see destruction,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.]” (Ps. XV, 10). Likewise in Psalm III: “I lay down and fell asleep [Note: [Col. 0717D] “I sank into sleep,” Lin. “I rested,” NC. 2. “I arose,” Bod. 1, 3.], and I arose again, because the Lord assisted me [Note: [Col. 0717D] “The Lord is my helper,” Bod. 2, 3. “Sustained me,” Lin. NC. 2.]” (Ps. III, 6). Likewise according to John: “No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. For I received this commandment from my Father” (John X, 10, 14).

## CHAPTER XXV.—THAT HE WOULD RISE FROM THE LOWER WORLD ON THE THIRD DAY

In Hosea: “He will give us life [Note: [Col. 0717D] “He gave us life,” Bod. 1, 3.] after two days; on the third day we shall rise [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Likewise on the third day,” Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.]” (Hos. VI, 2). Likewise in Exodus: “And [Col. 0717B] the Lord said to Moses: Go down and solemnly warn the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow; and let them wash their garment [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Their garments,” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 3.], and let them be ready for the day after tomorrow. For on the third day the Lord will descend upon Mount Sinai [Note: [Col. 0717D] “On Mount Sinai,” Bod. 1, 3.]” (Exod. XIX, 10–11). Likewise in the Gospel: “A wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Except Jonah the prophet,” Bod. 1, 4.]. For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster for three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth [Note: [Col. 0717D] The words “in the heart of the earth” are absent from Bod. 1, Foss. Corb.] for three days and three nights” (Matt. XVI, 4).

[Note: [Col. 0717]

CHAPTER XXVI.—“Living for ever and ever.” The Grenoble manuscript reads: “living in the Church of the saints.”]

## CHAPTER XXVI.—THAT, WHEN HE HAD RISEN, HE WOULD RECEIVE ALL AUTHORITY FROM THE FATHER, AND THAT HIS AUTHORITY IS ETERNAL

In Daniel: “I was looking in a vision by night [Note: [Col. 0717D] “In a vision of the night,” Bod. 2, Foss.]; and [Col. 0717C] behold, one like the Son of Man came upon the clouds of heaven and came as far as the Ancient of Days; and he stood in his sight, and those who attended him [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Those attending presented,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] presented him. And royal authority was given to him, and all the kings of the earth, by race [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Of the earth, and every nation,” Foss. “According to race,” Tert.], and all glory serving him [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Shall serve,” Lin.]; and his authority is eternal and shall not be taken away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed” (Dan. VII, 13–14). Likewise in Isaiah: “Now I shall arise, says the Lord; now I shall be glorified, now I shall be exalted. Now you shall see, now you shall understand, now you shall be confounded. The strength of your spirit shall be in vain; fire [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Fire shall consume you,” Lin. Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. “For fire,” Oxon.] shall consume you” (Isa. XXX, 10–11). Likewise in Psalm CIX: “The Lord said [Note: [Col. 0717D] “The Lord says,” Lam.] to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until [Note: [Col. 0717D] “Until I set,” Lin. Lam. NC. 1, 2.] I set your enemies as a footstool [Col. 0718A] [Note: [Col. 0718D] “A stool,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 3.] for your feet. God will send [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Will send forth,” Foss. “God from Zion,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.] the rod of your power from Zion, and you shall rule in the midst of your enemies” (Ps. CIX, 1–3). Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I turned and looked, to see the voice that was speaking with me. And I saw seven golden lampstands, and in the midst of the lampstands one like the Son of Man, clothed in a long robe; and he was girded above the breasts with a golden belt [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Above the breasts,” Bod. 1, 3, 4. “With a golden belt,” Foss. Corb.]. His head and hair were white as wool or snow, and his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet like burnished brass, as though from a furnace of fire [Note: [Col. 0718D] “A fiery furnace,” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Brev. Ver.], and his voice like the sound of many waters. He held seven stars in his right hand, and from his mouth came a sword sharpened on both sides [Note: [Col. 0718D] “A sword sharp on either side,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 4.]; and his face shone [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Was radiant,” Bod. 1.] like the sun in its strength. And when I had seen him, I fell at his feet as though dead; and he laid [Note: [Col. 0718D] “And placed,” Bod. 1, 4.] his right hand upon me, saying: [Col. 0718B] Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living One who was dead; and behold, I am living for ever and ever, and I hold the keys of death and the lower world” (Apoc. II, 12–18). Likewise in the Gospel, after the resurrection the Lord says [Note: [Col. 0718D] “After the resurrection, says,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] to the disciples: “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Go, therefore [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Go and teach,” Bod. 1.], and teach all nations, immersing [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Baptizing them,” NC. 2. Bod. 3.] them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe everything whatsoever I have commanded you [Note: [Col. 0718D] “I command you,” Bod. 1. “I enjoined,” Lin.]” (Matt. XXVII, 18–19).

## CHAPTER XXVII.—THAT GOD THE FATHER CANNOT BE REACHED EXCEPT THROUGH HIS SON [Note: [Col. 0718D] “Except through him,” Lam.], JESUS 296 CHRIST

In the Gospel: “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me” (John XIV, 6). Likewise there: “I am the door [Note: [Col. 0718D] “The gate,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3.]. If anyone enters through me [Note: [Col. 0718D] “He who enters through me,” Bod. Foss.], he shall be saved” [Col. 0718C] (Matt. XIII, 17). Likewise there: “Many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it” (John III, 36). Likewise there: “He who believes in the Son has eternal life. He who is not obedient to the Son [Note: [Col. 0718D] “He who does not obey the word,” Lam. Foss. “Is disobedient,” Lin. 2. Bod. 1, 4.] does not have life, but the wrath of God shall remain upon him.” Likewise Paul, in Ephesians: “And when he came, he proclaimed peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near, because through him we both have access [Note: [Col. 0718D] “We both have peace,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3, 4.] in one Spirit to the Father” (Eph. II, 17–18). Likewise to the Romans: “For all have sinned and are in need of the glory of God; but they are justified by his gift and grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus” (Rom. III, 23–24). Likewise in [Col. 0719A] the Epistle of the apostle Peter: “Christ died once for our sins [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Died for sins,” Bod. 1, 3, 4.], the righteous for the unrighteous [Note: [Col. 0719C] “The righteous for the wicked,” NC. 1. Lam.], that he might offer us to God” (1 Pet. III, 18). Likewise there: “For this reason the message was preached even to the dead, that they might be raised” (ibid. IV, 6). Likewise in the Epistle of John: “He who denies the Son does not have the Father either. He who confesses the Son [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Confesses the Son, also has the Father,” Bod. 1, 4. Foss.] has both the Son and the Father” (1 John II, 23).

[Note: [Col. 0719D]

CHAPTER XXVIII.—“Bringing forth the bound.” This passage differs slightly in the Burgundian manuscript, where it reads as follows: “Who brings forth the bound in strength, likewise those who provoke to wrath, who dwell in tombs. O God, when you went forth before your people, while you were passing through the desert.” Likewise in Psalm LXXXI: “Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you shall destroy among all the nations.” Likewise in the Gospel [Col. 0720D] according to Matthew: “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Why have you come here before the appointed time to destroy us?” Two ancient books cited in the English edition read: “who brings forth the bound in strength.” So too in one of my own.

“Whom he himself shall shepherd.” These words are not found in the Apocalypse and are absent from certain ancient books; they are also absent from the Greek.]

## CHAPTER XXVIII.—THAT HE HIMSELF WILL COME AS JUDGE

In Malachi: “Behold, the day of the Lord comes, burning like a furnace; and all foreigners and all the wicked shall be stubble, and the coming day shall set them ablaze, says the Lord” (Mal. IV, 1). Likewise in Psalm XLIX: “The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and summoned the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting. From Zion comes the appearance [Note: [Col. 0719C] “From Zion,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. “The appearance of his beauty,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] of his beauty. [Col. 0719B] God shall come manifestly [Note: [Col. 0719C] “God manifest,” Bod. 1, 2, 4.], our God, and he shall not be silent. Fire shall burn before him, and a mighty tempest [Note: [Col. 0719C] “A powerful storm around him,” Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 3.] shall surround him. He has summoned heaven above [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Heaven above, and the earth,” Ben. Ver.] and the earth [Note: [Col. 0719C] “That he might separate the people,” Foss. Corb.] so that he may separate his people. Gather his righteous ones to him [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Assemble his saints,” NC. 2.], those who establish his covenant [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Who have ordered,” NC. 2. Lin.] by sacrifices; and the heavens shall proclaim his righteousness, for God is judge” (Ps. XLIX, 1–6).
