Likewise in Isaiah: “The Lord God [Note: [Col. 0719C] “The Lord says, the God of powers,” Bod. 2.] of powers shall go forth and crush war. He shall rouse the conflict and cry out [Note: [Col. 0719C] “Cry aloud,” Bod. 1.] mightily against his enemies [Note: [Col. 0719D] “His enemies,” Foss.]: I have been silent [Note: [Col. 0719D] “I have indeed been silent; surely,” Bod. 3.]; surely I shall not always be silent?” (Isa. XLII, 13–14). Likewise in Psalm LXVII: “Let God arise and let his enemies be scattered [Note: [Col. 0719D] “Let his enemies be dispersed,” Bod. 1, 4.], and let those who hate him flee from his face. As smoke vanishes [Note: [Col. 0719D] “As it vanishes,” Foss. Corb. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. “As wax melts,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. “Wax shall flow,” Lin. NC. 2.], let them vanish. As wax melts before fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God; but let the righteous rejoice [Note: [Col. 0719D] “Let the righteous feast,” Lam. Bod. 2, 3. NC. 2.] and exult in the sight of God, and [Col. 0719C] be glad with rejoicing. Sing to God; make music to his name [Note: [Col. 0719D] “Sing a psalm,” Lin. NC. 2. “With rejoicing in God,” Bod. 3.]; make a road for him [Note: [Col. 0719D] “Make a way for him,” NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Foss. Corb.] who ascends into the west; God is his name. They shall be troubled before his face—the face of the father of orphans [Note: [Col. 0720C] “The fathers of orphans and the judges,” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Foss. Corb.] and the judge of widows. God is in his holy place, God who causes those of one accord [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Of one manner,” Lin.] to dwell in a house, bringing forth [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Who brings forth the bound in strength,” Lin. NC. 2.] the bound in strength, and likewise those who provoke to wrath [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Those who embitter,” Corb. “Those who dwell in tombs,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3, 4. Foss.], [Col. 0720A] who dwell in tombs. O God, when you went forth [Note: [Col. 0720C] “When you went out,” Lin. NC. 2.] in the sight of your people, while passing [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Of your people, while you passed,” Foss.] through the desert” (Ps. XLVII, 2, 8). Likewise in Psalm LXXXI: “Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you shall destroy [Note: [Col. 0720C] “You shall disinherit,” Bod. 2. Lam. “You shall destroy,” NC. 2.] among all the nations” (Ps. LXXXI, 8). Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “What have we to do with you, son of David? Why have you come here before the appointed time to punish us [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Destroy us,” Bod. 3.]?” (Matt. VIII, 29). Likewise according to John: “The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him” (John V, 22–23). Likewise in Paul’s Second Epistle to the Corinthians: “We must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may carry away [Note: [Col. 0720C] “So that each may receive,” Lam. NC. 1. Corb. “What he has done, whether good,” NC. 1. Lam.] what belongs to his own body according to what he has done, whether good or evil” (2 Cor. V, 10).

## CHAPTER XXIX.—THAT HE HIMSELF IS THE KING WHO WILL REIGN FOREVER

[Col. 0720B]

In Zechariah: “Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving, gentle, sitting upon an unbroken ass [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Upon an ass’s colt,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]” (Zech. IX, 9). Likewise in Isaiah: “Who shall tell you of that eternal place [Note: [Col. 0720C] “Who shall tell you that the fire burns? Who shall tell [Col. 0720D] you of that eternal place?” Lam. Bod. 2, 3, 4. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Foss.]? He who walks in righteousness and whose hands abstain from gifts, who stops his ears so that he does not hear a judgment of blood and closes his eyes so that he does not see injustice—he shall dwell [Note: [Col. 0720D] “He shall live,” Bod. 1.] in the lofty cavern of a strong rock. Bread shall be given to him, and his water is sure. You shall see the King in glory” (Isa. XXXIII, 14–17). Likewise in Malachi: “‘I am a great King,’ says the Lord, 297 ‘and my name is renowned among the nations’” (Mal. I, 14). Likewise in Psalm II: “But I have been appointed [Col. 0720C] King by him upon Zion, his holy mountain [Note: [Col. 0720D] “His holy mountain, proclaiming the commandment of the Lord,” NC. 2. Foss. “His sovereignty,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.], proclaiming his sovereignty” (Ps. II, 6–7). Likewise in Psalm XXI: “All the ends of the earth shall remember [Note: [Col. 0720D] “Shall remember and turn,” NC. 2.] and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship in your sight; for the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he shall rule [Note: [Col. 0720D] “Shall rule the nations,” Foss.] all the nations” (Ps. [Col. 0721A] XXI, 28–29). Likewise in Psalm XXIII: “Lift up your gates [Note: [Col. 0721C] “Lift up your gates, O princes,” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 3. “Be lifted up, O gates,” Bod. 1, 2, 3. Lam. NC. 1.], O princes, and be raised up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter. Who is this King of glory [Note: [Col. 0721C] “Eternal,” Bod. 4. “King of glory,” Bod. 1, 2, 3. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. “Of glory? The Lord mighty in battle,” Foss. “Mighty in battle; likewise in the Psalm,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.]? The Lord strong and powerful, the Lord mighty in battle. Lift up your gates, O princes, and be raised up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of powers—he is the King of glory” (Ps. XXIII, 7–10). Likewise in Psalm XLIV: “My heart has uttered a good discourse [Note: [Col. 0721C] “My heart a good word,” Bod. 2, 3. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.]; I declare my works to the King [Note: [Col. 0721C] “I declare my works to the King,” Bod. 1.]. My tongue is the pen of a writer [Note: [Col. 0721D] “The pen of a scribe,” Lam. Bod. 2, 3. Lin. NC. 1, 2. “Of a swift scribe,” Lam. Bod. 2, 3. Lin. NC. 1, 2.] writing swiftly; you are more beautiful in appearance than the sons of men [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Beautiful in form above the sons of men,” Lin. NC. 2.]. Grace has been poured [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Grace has been diffused,” Bod. 2, 3.] upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever [Note: [Col. 0721D] “God eternally,” Bod. 3.]. Gird your sword [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Your blade,” Lam. Bod. 2, 3, 4. “Sword,” Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 1.] upon your thigh, O most mighty one. In your beauty and comeliness, press forward, advance [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Ride forth prosperously,” Bod. 1, 3. “Go forth,” Lin. NC. 2.], and reign for the sake of truth [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Holiness and righteousness,” Lam. Bod. 1, 4. NC. 1. “Righteousness, and your right hand shall teach you wondrous things,” Bod. 3.], gentleness, and righteousness” (Ps. XLIV, 2, 5). [Col. 0721B] Likewise in Psalm V: “My King and my God, for to you I shall pray. Lord, in the morning you shall hear my voice; in the morning I shall stand before you [Note: [Col. 0721D] “In the morning I shall stand before you and see,” Lin. NC. 2.], and I shall behold you” (Ps. V, 3–4). Likewise in Psalm XCVI: “The Lord has reigned; let the earth exult, let the many islands rejoice [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Let the earth exult, let the islands be glad,” Bod. 2. Lin. NC. 2.]” (Ps. XCVI, 1). Likewise in Psalm XLIV: “The queen stood at your right hand in a gilded garment [Note: [Col. 0721D] “In gilded clothing, adorned all around and variegated,” Lin. “Enveloped in variegation,” NC. 2. “Enveloped and variegated,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.], clothed in variegated raiment. Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; and forget your people and your father’s house [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Your father’s house,” Corb.], for the King has desired your beauty, because he is the Lord your God [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Your Lord,” Bod. 1, 2, 3.]” (Ps. XLIV, 10–12). Likewise in Psalm LXXIII: “But God, our King before the age [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Before the ages,” Corb.], has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth” (Ps. LXXIII, 12). Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “And when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, Magi came from the East to Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Arrived at Jerusalem,” Bod. 1.], saying: [Col. 0721C] Where is he who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the East and have come to worship him” (Matt. II, 1–2). Likewise according to John, Jesus said: “My kingdom is not of this age. If my kingdom were of this age [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Of this world; if my kingdom were of this world,” Bod. 2. Lam. NC. 2.], my servants would be agitated [Note: [Col. 0721D] “Would certainly fight,” Bod. 3.] so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.” Pilate said [Note: [Col. 0722C] “But Pilate said,” Bod. 1.]: “Then you are a king?” Jesus answered: “You say that I am a king. For this I was born [Note: [Col. 0722C] “I was born and for this I came,” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lin. NC. 1. “For this I came into the world,” Oxon.], and for this I came into the world: that I might bear witness to the truth [Col. 0722A] [Note: [Col. 0722C] “Declare testimony,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Corb.]. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice” (John XVIII, 36–37).

## CHAPTER XXX.—THAT HE HIMSELF IS JUDGE AND KING [Note: [Col. 0722C] “That Christ, coming at the end of the age as judge of all, will repay the good with rewards and the evil with punishments according to their deserts,” Bod. 3.]

In Psalm LXXI: “O God, give your judgment to the King and your righteousness to the King’s son, to judge your people in righteousness” (Ps. LXXI, 1–2). Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And I saw heaven opened [Note: [Col. 0722D] “The whole heaven opened,” Bod. 4.]; and behold, a white horse, and he who sat upon it was called Faithful and True [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Faithful and truthful,” Foss. “And righteous,” Corb. “Judging righteously,” Lam. NC. 1. “A warrior,” Lam. NC. 1. Corb.]; he judges equitably and justly, and wages war. His eyes were like a flame of fire, and upon his head were many diadems; and he bore a written name known to no one other than himself [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Except to him alone,” Foss.]. And he was clothed in a garment sprinkled [Note: [Col. 0722D] “In a garment sprinkled,” Foss. “In a sprinkled garment,” Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 2.] with blood, and his name is called the Word of God [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Discourse of God.”]. And the armies that are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed [Col. 0722B] in clean white linen [Note: [Col. 0722D] “In clean linen,” Foss.]. And from his mouth came a sword sharp on both sides [Note: [Col. 0722D] “A sword sharp on either side,” Corb.], so that with it he might strike the nations whom he himself shall shepherd [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Shall shepherd,” Bod. 2, 3, 4.] with an iron rod. And he shall tread the winepress of the wine of the wrath of Almighty God. He also has a name written upon his garment and upon his thigh: King of kings and Lord of rulers [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Of lords,” Bod. 1, 4.]” (Apoc. XIX, 11–16). Likewise in the Gospel: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he shall sit upon the throne of his glory. And all the nations shall be gathered before him, and he shall separate them [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Shall separate those nations,” Corb.] from one another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats; and he shall place the sheep at his right hand, but the goats at his left [Note: [Col. 0722D] “On the left,” Corb. “At his right hand are,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.]. Then the King shall say to those who will be at his right hand: Come, you blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom prepared for you 298 from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food; [Col. 0722C] I was thirsty, and you gave me drink [Note: [Col. 0722D] “You gave me something to drink,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]; I was a stranger, and you brought me in [Note: [Col. 0722D] “You received me,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]; I was naked, and you covered me [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Naked, and you covered me,” Lam. NC. 1.]; I was sick [Note: [Col. 0722D] “I became sick,” Ver.], and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me. Then the righteous shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and bring you in [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Receive you,” Bod. 2. “Lead you away,” Ver.]? Or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you sick [Note: [Col. 0722D] “Become sick,” Bod. 1, 3, 4.] and in prison, and come to you? And the King shall answer [Note: [Col. 0722D] “The King answered and says,” Bod. 1.] and say to them: Amen, I say to you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these [Col. 0723A] my brothers, you did it to me. Then he shall say to those who will be at his left hand [Note: [Col. 0723A] “Who are at the left,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2.]: Depart from me, you accursed, into the eternal fire that my Father prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink [Note: [Col. 0723A] “You gave me something to drink,” Bod. 2. “You gave me drink; I was a stranger and you did not receive me,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod.]; I was a stranger, and you did not bring me in; I was naked, and you did not clothe me [Note: [Col. 0724A] “You did not come to me,” Bod. 3, 4. “You led away,” Ver.]; I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me. Then they too shall answer [Col. 0724A] and say: Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to you? And he shall answer them [Note: [Col. 0724A] “The King shall answer them, saying,” Lam. NC. 1.]: Amen, I say to you, insofar as you did not do it to one of these least ones, neither did you do it to me. And these shall go away into eternal burning [Note: [Col. 0724A] “Into eternal fire,” NC. 2.], but the righteous into eternal life” (Matt. XXV, 21–46).

# BOOK THREE [Note: [Col. 0723D] “On the chapters of God’s commandments pertaining to the discipline of the Christian religion.” Oxon., in a note.]

[Col. 0723]

[Col. 0723B] **CYPRIAN TO HIS SON QUIRINUS, GREETINGS.**

Because of the faith and devotion [Note: [Col. 0723D] “Faith and love,” Lam. NC. 1. Ben.] that you display toward the Lord God, dearest son, you asked me, for your instruction, to excerpt from the Holy Scriptures certain chapters pertaining to the religious discipline of our sect, seeking a concise study of the divine reading, so that a mind devoted to God might not be wearied by long or numerous volumes of books, but, instructed by a compendium of heavenly commandments, might possess a wholesome and substantial abridgment with which to nourish its memory. And because I owe you an obedience full of love, I have done what you asked: that I should labor once, so that you would not always have to labor. Therefore, insofar as my limited ability could encompass it, I have collected certain commandments of the Lord and divine teachings. These may be easy [Note: [Col. 0723D] “Both be easy,” NC. 2. Bod. 1.] and useful for readers, since the few items arranged in an abridgment can be read through quickly [Col. 0723C] and repeated frequently. I pray, dearest son, that you may always fare well.

## CHAPTER HEADINGS
I. On the Good of Works and Mercy [Note: [Col. 0723D] “On the work of mercy,” Corb. Lam. NC. 1.].  
II. In works and almsgiving, even if less is done because of limited means, the intention itself is sufficient [Note: [Col. 0723D] “By the intention itself,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 4.].  
III. *Agapē* and brotherly love must be practiced devoutly and steadfastly.  
IV. One must glory in nothing, since nothing is ours.  
V. Humility and quietness must be maintained in all things.  
299 VI. All the good [Note: [Col. 0723D] “The good also,” Bod. 1, 4.] and just labor more [Note: [Col. 0723D] “Labor very greatly,” Corb.], but must endure, because they are being tested.  
VII. The Holy Spirit whom [Col. 0723D] we have received must not be grieved [Note: [Col. 0723D] “Do not grieve,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.].  
VIII. Anger must be overcome, lest it compel one to sin.  
[Col. 0724B] IX. Brothers must bear with one another.  
X. Trust must be placed in God alone [Note: [Col. 0723D] “In God alone,” Bod. 1, 2; “one must trust,” Corb.], and in him alone must one glory.  
XI. He who has attained faith, having put off [Note: [Col. 0724D] “Having stripped off the former man,” Thu.] the former man, must think only of heavenly and spiritual things and pay no attention to the world, which he has already renounced [Note: [Col. 0724D] “Which we have renounced,” Bod. 1, 3, 4.].  
XII. One must not swear.  
XIII. One must not curse.  
XIV. One must never murmur, but must bless God concerning everything that happens [Note: [Col. 0724D] “That always happens,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.].  
XV. People are tempted by God so that they may be tested [Note: [Col. 0724D] “By God so that they may be examined,” NC. 2. Bod. 1, 4.].  
XVI. On the Good of Martyrdom.  
XVII. The things we suffer in the world are less than the reward that has been promised.  
XVIII. Nothing must be preferred to the love of God and Christ.  
[Col. 0724C] XIX. We must obey not our own will, but God’s.  
XX. Fear [Note: [Col. 0724D] Bod. 4 adds “of God.”] is the foundation and support of hope and faith.  
XXI. One must not judge another rashly.  
XXII. When an injury has been received [Note: [Col. 0724D] “An injury received must be remitted and endured,” Lam. NC. 2. Corb.], it must be remitted and forgiven.  
XXIII. Evil must not be repaid in kind.  
XXIV. The Father cannot be reached [Note: [Col. 0724D] “God the Father cannot be reached,” Corb.; “be approached,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu.; “except through Christ,” Bod. 1, 2. Corb. Thu.] except through Christ.  
XXV. No one can reach the kingdom of God unless he has been baptized and born anew.  
XXVI. It is too little merely to be baptized and receive the Eucharist unless one advances in deeds and works.  
XXVII. Even one who has been baptized may lose the grace he has attained [Note: [Col. 0724D] “Has attained,” Thu. Corb.] unless he preserves innocence.  
[Col. 0724D] XXVIII. One who has sinned against God cannot be forgiven in the Church.  
[Col. 0725A] XXIX. On the hatred of the Name foretold beforehand.  
XXX. What one has vowed to God must be rendered promptly.  
XXXI. He who has not believed has already been judged.  
XXXII. On the Good of Virginity and Continence.  
XXXIII. The Father judges nothing, but the Son does; and the Father is not honored by one by whom the Son is not honored [Note: [Col. 0725D] “The Son also is not honored,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.].  
XXXIV. A believer ought not to live as a Gentile [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Must not,” Corb.].  
XXXV. God is patient for this purpose: that we may repent [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Repent of our sins,” Lam. NC. 1.] of our sin and be reformed.  
XXXVI. A woman must not adorn herself in a worldly fashion [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Ought not,” Lam. NC. 1.].  
XXXVII. A believer ought not to be punished for any offenses other than for the Name alone.  
XXXVIII. A servant of God must be innocent, lest he incur secular punishment.  
[Col. 0725B] XXXIX. An example of how to live has been given to us in Christ.  
XL. One must not act boastfully or tumultuously.  
XLI. One must not speak foolishly and buffoonishly [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Foolishly and in a worldly manner,” Bod. 3.].  
300 XLII. Faith is wholly [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Only,” NC. 2; “whole,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.] effective, and we can do as much as we believe.  
XLIII. He who has truly believed can attain immediately.  
XLIV. Believers who dispute among themselves must not resort to a Gentile judge.  
XLV. Hope concerns future things, and therefore faith [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Our faith,” Impr. Thu. Corb.] must be patient regarding what has been promised.  
XLVI. A woman must be silent in church.  
XLVII. It comes about through our own sin and desert that we suffer and do not perceive God’s aid in all things.  
XLVIII. One must not lend at interest.  
[Col. 0725C] XLIX. Even enemies must be loved.  
L. The mystery of faith must not be profaned.  
LI. No one should be exalted by his own work.  
LII. The freedom to believe or not to believe rests in free choice.  
LIII. God’s mysteries cannot be perceived fully, and therefore our faith must be simple.  
LIV. No one is without stain and without sin.  
LV. We must please not human beings, but God.  
LVI. Nothing that is done escapes God’s notice.  
LVII. The believer is corrected and preserved.  
LVIII. No one should be grieved by death, since in living there is toil and danger, but in dying [Note: [Col. 0725D] “But in dying,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.] there is peace and the assurance of resurrection [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Assurance in rising again,” Bod. 2.].  
LIX. On the idols that the Gentiles regard as gods.  
[Col. 0725D] LX. An excessive craving for food must not be pursued.  
LXI. The desire to possess and money must not [Note: [Col. 0725D] “Must not be admitted,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] be pursued.  
[Col. 0726A] LXII. Marriage must not be contracted with Gentiles.  
LXIII. Fornication is a grave [Note: [Col. 0725D] “More grievous,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4; “to fornicate,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] sin.  
LXIV. What the works of the flesh are that produce death, and what the spiritual works are that lead to life [Note: [Col. 0726D] “Lead to eternal life,” Lin.].  
LXV. All sins are put away in Baptism.  
LXVI. God’s discipline must be observed in ecclesiastical precepts.  
LXVII. It was foretold that people would spurn sound discipline.  
LXVIII. One must withdraw from a person who lives disorderly [Note: [Col. 0726D] “Disorderly and without discipline,” Lin.; “walks disorderly,” Corb.; “contrary to God’s discipline,” Lam. NC. 1.] and contrary to discipline.  
LXIX. The kingdom of God consists neither in worldly wisdom nor in eloquence, but in faith in the cross and the power of conduct.  
LXX. Parents must be obeyed.  
[Col. 0726B] LXXI. Fathers also ought not to be harsh toward their children [Note: [Col. 0726D] “Must not be,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 4.].  
LXXII. When slaves have believed, they must serve their earthly masters all the more.  
LXXIII. Masters likewise must be gentler.  
LXXIV. Every widow who has been approved must be honored.  
LXXV. Each person must exercise greater care for his own, and especially for believers.  
LXXVI. An elder must not be accused rashly.  
LXXVII. One who sins must be rebuked publicly.  
LXXVIII. One must not speak with heretics.  
LXXIX. Innocence [Note: [Col. 0726D] “An innocent person faithfully,” NC. 1.] asks confidently and obtains.  
LXXX. The devil has no power over a person unless God has permitted it.  
301 LXXXI. The laborer’s wage [Note: [Col. 0726D] “Wages,” etc., Lin.] must be paid promptly.  
[Col. 0726C] LXXXII. One must not practice augury.  
LXXXIII. A lock of hair must not be worn [Note: [Col. 0726D] “A lock of hair must not be worn,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] on the head.  
LXXXIV. Hair must not be plucked [Note: [Col. 0726D] Bod. 1 adds “hair.”].  
LXXXV. One must rise when a bishop or presbyter enters.  
LXXXVI. A schism must not be made, even if the person who withdraws remains in the one faith and the same tradition.  
LXXXVII. Believers must be guileless as well as prudent.  
LXXXVIII. A brother must not be defrauded.  
LXXXIX. The end of the world will come suddenly.  
XC. A wife must not leave her husband; or, if she has left him, she must remain unmarried [Note: [Col. 0726D] “Remain unmarried,” Voss.; “Continue unmarried,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.].  
XCI. Each person is tempted only as much as he can endure.  
[Col. 0726D] XCII. Not everything that is lawful ought to be done.  
XCIII. It was foretold that heresies would arise.  
XCIV. The Eucharist must be received with fear and honor.  
[Col. 0727A] XCV. One must associate with the good [Note: [Col. 0727C] “Associate,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Thu. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4; “come together,” Oxon.], but avoid the wicked.  
XCVI. One must act in deeds, not words [Note: [Col. 0727C] “Obey,” Bod. 1.].  
XCVII. One must hasten toward faith and attainment [Note: [Col. 0727C] “Hasten,” Oxon.].  
XCVIII. A catechumen ought no longer to sin [Note: [Col. 0727C] “Ought not to sin,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.].  
XCIX. Judgment will be according to the periods: by equity before the Law, or by the Law after Moses.  
C. God’s grace must be free of charge.  
CI. The Holy Spirit frequently [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Always in fire,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] appeared in fire.  
CII. All good people [Note: [Col. 0727D] “The good also,” Bod. 2, 3, 4.] must willingly listen to correction.  
CIII. One must refrain from excessive speech.  
CIV. One must not lie.  
CV. Those who commit offenses in household [Col. 0727B] service must frequently be corrected.  
CVI. When an injury has been received, patience [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Patience must be,” Lam. NC. 1.] must be maintained and vengeance left to God.  
CVII. One must not slander.  
CVIII. One must not plot against one’s neighbor.  
CIX. The sick must be visited.  
CX. Whisperers [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Whisperers and the double-tongued,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.] are accursed.  
CXI. The sacrifices of the wicked are not acceptable.  
CXII. Those who have possessed greater power in the world will be judged more severely.  
CXIII. Widows [Note: [Col. 0727D] “A widow,” Oxon.] and orphans must be protected.  
CXIV. While a person is in the flesh, he must make *exomologesis*—public confession.  
CXV. Flattery is pernicious.  
CXVI. God is loved more by the person to whom more [Col. 0727C] sins are forgiven in Baptism.  
CXVII. The struggle against the devil is fierce; therefore we must stand firmly so that we may conquer.  
CXVIII. On the Antichrist: that he comes in a human being [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Will come into a human being,” Corb.].  
CXIX. The yoke of the Law, which has been cast off by us [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Not taken up,” Corb.], was heavy, while the yoke of the Lord, which has been taken up by us, is light.  
CXX. One must persevere in prayers.

[Note: [Col. 0727D]

**CHAP. I.—“Why do you fast for me?”** See Fronto Ducaeus’s notes on Chrysostom’s *Homily VI to the People of Antioch*.

[Col. 0728D] **“Unless he humble.”** See Cotelerius’s notes on chapter III of the *Epistle of Barnabas*.

[Col. 0729D] **“I was younger.”** Most ancient books have *juvenior*. Apuleius, *Metamorphoses*, book 8: “But one above the others, both braver in spirit and younger in age.” Sosipater [Col. 0730D] Charisius, book II: “Sometimes the positive and comparative forms are used, as *senex, senior* (‘old, older’), *juvenis, juvenior* (‘young, younger’).” So too in Fulgentius Placiades, book I of the *Etymologies*.

[Col. 0731D] **“Likewise there: When he comes.”** The material from here through “But the just into eternal life” is absent from the Burgundian codex and the [Col. 0732D] Lamonian codex.]

302 **CHAP. I.—ON THE GOOD OF WORKS AND MERCY** [Note: [Col. 0727D] “On the good work and mercy,” Lam. NC. 1. Corb.].

[Col. 0728A]

In Isaiah: “Cry out,” he says, “with strength [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Cry out with strength,” Voss. 2.], and do not hold back; raise your voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people [Note: [Col. 0727D] “To your people,” Voss. 2.] their sins, and to the house of Jacob their crimes. They seek me from day to day and desire to know my ways, as though they were a people who had practiced righteousness and had not forsaken God’s judgment [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Judgment” omitted, Voss. 4.] [Note: [Col. 0727D] “Abandoned,” Lin.]. They now ask me for a just judgment and desire to draw near to God, saying: ‘Why have we fasted [Note: [Col. 0728C] “Why have we fasted?” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.], and you did not see? We humbled our souls, and you did not take notice [Note: [Col. 0728C] “And you did not know,” Lin.]. For in the days of your fasting [Note: [Col. 0728C] “Of your fasts,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] your own desires [Note: [Col. 0728C] “Pleasures,” Lin. Thu. Corb.] are found. For either you goad those subject to you, or you fast for lawsuits and disputes, or you strike your neighbors with your fists. Why do you fast for me, so that today your voice may be heard in an outcry? This is not the fast [Note: [Col. 0728C] “Which I have chosen,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Voss. [Col. 0728D] 5. Cott.] I have chosen, unless [Note: [Col. 0728D] “But for a person to humble himself,” Cott.; “A fast, says the Lord, for a person to humble his soul for a day, even though you twist it like a ring,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Cott. Voss. 3.] a person humbles his [Col. 0728B] soul. Even if you bend your neck like a ring and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, not even so [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Not even so will this,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2; “this will not so,” Cott.] will it be called an acceptable fast. I did not choose such a fast, says the Lord; rather, loose every knot of injustice, undo the strangling bonds of oppressive contracts. Release the shattered into rest, and tear apart every unjust written obligation [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Written obligation of injustice,” NC. 1.]. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the needy who have no roof into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Clothe him,” Cott.]; and you shall not despise the members of your own family line. Then your early light will break forth, and your healing will swiftly arise. Righteousness will go before you, and God’s brightness will surround you. Then you will cry out, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking, he will say, ‘Behold, I am here [Note: [Col. 0728D] “I am near,” Cott.]’” (Isa. LVIII, 1–9).

On the same subject in Job: “I preserved the needy from the hand of the powerful, and I helped the orphan who had no helper. [Col. 0728C] The mouth of the widow blessed me, since I was the eye of the blind; I was also the foot of the lame and the father of the weak” (Job XXIX, 12, 13, 15, 16).

On the same subject in Tobit: “And I said to my son Tobias [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Tobit said to his son,” Lam. NC. 2. Bod. 1, 2. Voss. 4.]: ‘Go and bring back any poor man you find among our brothers, provided that he keeps God in mind with all [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Who nevertheless has the Lord in his whole,” Lam. NC. 1.] his heart. Bring him here [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Bring him here,” Corb.], and he will eat this meal together with me [Note: [Col. 0728D] “Together with me,” Thu. Corb. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2. Voss. 2.]. Behold, my son, I shall wait for you until you come’” (Tob. II, 2).

Likewise there: “All the days of your life, my son, keep God in mind, and do not [Col. 0729A] transgress his commandments. Practice righteousness all the days of your life, and do not walk the path [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Into the path,” Voss. 2.] of iniquity; for when you act in accordance with truth, your works will be regarded favorably. Give alms from your substance, and do not turn your face away from any poor person. Thus it will come about that the face of God will not be turned away from you. Give according to what you have, my son. If your substance is abundant, give more of it as alms. If you have little [Note: [Col. 0729C] “According as you have,” Bod. 2. Voss. 2. Thu. Lam.], share from that very little. And do not be afraid when you give alms: you are laying up a good reward for yourself against the day of necessity. For almsgiving delivers from death and does not permit one to enter darkness. Almsgiving is a good gift [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Almsgiving, for all who practice it,” Corb.] for all who practice it before the Most High God” (Tob. IV, 5–11).

On the same subject in Solomon’s Proverbs: “He who has mercy on the poor [Note: [Col. 0729C] Thus Lam. Voss. 3; “the poor,” Oxon.; “lends to God,” Thu. Corb.] lends to God” (Prov. XIX, 17).

Likewise there: “He who gives to the poor [Col. 0729B] will never be in need. But he who turns away his eye [Note: [Col. 0729C] “His eye, into many,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lam. Thu. Corb.] will be in great want [Note: [Col. 0729C] “In great need,” NC. 2.]” (Prov. XXVIII, 27).

Likewise there: “By almsgiving [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Alms,” Bod. 1. Voss. 2.] and faith sins are cleansed [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Offenses are cleansed,” Bod. 1, 2, 3.]” (Prov. XVI, 6).

Likewise there: “If your enemy is hungry, feed [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Nourish,” Lin. Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Voss. 2.] him; and if he is thirsty, give him drink [Note: [Col. 0729C] Thus Voss. 3. Bod. 2; “you will give drink,” Impr.; “give drink,” Oxon.]. For by doing this you will heap burning coals [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Coals of fire,” NC. 2. Cott.] upon his head [Note: [Col. 0729C] “Upon his head,” Lam. Lin. Bod. 1, 2. Thu. Voss. 2; “will place upon his head,” Corb. Cott.]” (Prov. XXV, 21, 22).

Likewise there: “Just as water extinguishes fire, so almsgiving extinguishes sin” (Ecclus. III, 33).

In the same author’s Proverbs: “Do not say, ‘Go away and return [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Go and return,” Cott.; “Tomorrow I shall give to you,” Lam. NC. 1, 2.]; tomorrow I shall give,’ when you are able to do good at once. For you do not know what may happen on the following day” (Prov. III, 28).

Likewise there: “He who stops his ears [Note: [Col. 0729D] “His ears, lest he hear,” Bod. 1, 3. Voss. 2.] so as not to hear the weak [Note: [Col. 0729D] “The infirm,” Cott.] will himself call upon God, and there will be no one to hear him” (Prov. XXI, 13).

Likewise there: “He who conducts himself blamelessly in righteousness [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Blame regarding righteousness,” Cott.] leaves blessed children behind [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Will leave,” Cott. Voss. 2.]” (Prov. XX, 7).

In the same author, in Ecclesiasticus: “My son, if you have possessions, do good to yourself, and offer offerings worthy of God [Note: [Col. 0729D] “You shall offer offerings,” NC. 1, 2. Cott. Lam. Voss. 2.]; remember that death does not delay” (Ecclus. XIV, 11, 12).

Likewise there: “Enclose almsgiving in the heart of the poor, and 303 it will pray for you [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Will entreat on your behalf,” Corb. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lam. Thu. Voss. 2.] against every evil” (Ecclus. XXIX, 12).

On the same subject in Psalm [Col. 0730A] XXXVI, that mercy [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Practice mercy and you will be able to benefit,” Corb.] also benefits one’s posterity: “I was young, and indeed I have grown old [Note: [Col. 0729D] “I was younger and have grown old, and never,” Cott. Corb.], and I have not seen the just man abandoned, nor his seed seeking bread. All day long he shows mercy and lends [Note: [Col. 0729D] “Shows mercy and makes loans,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Voss. 2.], and his seed is under a blessing [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Will be under a blessing,” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Cott.]” (Ps. XXXVI, 25, 26).

On the same subject in Psalm XL: “Blessed [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Happy is he who,” Bod. 4. Thu. Corb.] is he who understands the needy and the poor; on the evil day God will deliver him” (Ps. XL, 2).

Likewise in Psalm CXI: “He distributed [Note: [Col. 0730C] “He scattered,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Cott. Voss. 2. Thu. Corb.], he gave to the poor; his righteousness will remain forever and ever” (Ps. CXI, 9).

On the same subject in Hosea: “I desire mercy rather [Note: [Col. 0730C] “I prefer mercy to,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] than sacrifice, and knowledge of God more than [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Of God than,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Thu. Corb. Cott.] burnt offerings” (Hos. VI, 6).

On the same subject in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Blessed are the hungry and thirsty,” Voss. 2. Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.], for they shall be filled” (Matt. V, 6).

Likewise there: [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Happy are the merciful,” Bod. 4. Thu.] “Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy” (ibid., 7).

Likewise there: “Lay up [Col. 0730B] treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consuming decay [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Consuming decay destroys,” Cott.] destroys, and where thieves do not dig through and steal [Note: [Col. 0730C] “Dig through. Where,” Lin. NC. 2. Thu. Bod. 1, 4. Voss. 4; “nor steal,” above in *On Works and Almsgiving*.]” (ibid. VI, 20, 21). “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”

Likewise there: “The kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking fine pearls; and when he found a precious pearl [Note: [Col. 0730C] “A fine pearl,” Cott.], he went away and sold everything he had and bought it [Note: [Col. 0730D] “In order to buy it,” Lin.]” (Matt. XIII, 45, 46).

**That even a small work is beneficial.** Likewise there: “And whoever gives [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Gives to one,” Cott.; “only in my name,” Cott.] one of these least ones a cup of cold water in the name of a disciple, amen I say to you, his reward shall not perish [Note: [Col. 0730D] “He shall not lose his reward,” Cott.]” (Matt. X, 42).

**That alms must be denied to no one.** Likewise there: “Give to everyone who asks you [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Give to the one who asks,” Cott.], and do not turn away from one who wishes to borrow [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Do not turn yourself away,” Bod. 3. Voss. 4.]” (Matt. V, 42).

Likewise there: “If you wish to enter life [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Into life,” Cott.], keep the commandments.” He said, “Which ones?” Jesus said to him: “You shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery, [Col. 0730C] you shall not bear false witness [Note: [Col. 0730D] “You shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false,” Cott.], honor your father and mother, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Your neighbor as yourself,” Cott.; “your neighbor as,” Thu.].” The young man said to him: “I have observed all these things. What do I still lack?” Jesus said to him: “If you wish to be perfect, go and sell [Note: [Col. 0730D] “Sell your goods,” Bod. 1, 2, 4; “all your goods,” Cott. Voss. 2.] all that is yours and give to the poor [Note: [Col. 0730D] “The needy,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Thu. Voss. 2.], and you will have treasure [Col. 0731A] in heaven; then come, follow me” (Matt. XIX, 17–21).

Likewise there: “When the Son of Man comes in his majesty [Note: [Col. 0731C] “In his glory,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] and all the angels with him, then he will sit upon the throne of his glory [Note: [Col. 0731C] “Upon the seat of his majesty,” Cott.], and all [Note: [Col. 0731C] “All the nations of the earth,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] nations will be gathered [Note: [Col. 0731C] “Were gathered before,” Cott.] before him. And he will separate [Note: [Col. 0731C] “Divide,” Cott.] them from one another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will place the sheep at his right hand [Note: [Col. 0731C] “The sheep indeed at the right,” Cott.], but the goats at his left [Note: [Col. 0731C] “At the left,” Cott.].

“Then the King will say to those who are at his right hand: ‘Come, you blessed of my Father; receive [Note: [Col. 0731C] “Possess the prepared,” Cott.] the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink [Note: [Col. 0731C] “You gave me a drink,” Lin.; “something to drink,” Cott.]; I was a stranger, and you brought me in [Note: [Col. 0731C] “And took me in,” Cott.]; naked, and you covered me [Note: [Col. 0731C] “Clothed me,” Cott.]; I became sick [Note: [Col. 0731C] “I was sick,” Corb. Voss. 2; so above, book II, Voss. 2.], and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came [Note: [Col. 0731D] “You visited me,” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] to me.’

“Then the just will answer him, saying: ‘Lord, when did we see you as a stranger and bring you in [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Take you in.”], or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you [Col. 0731B] sick [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Become sick,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.; so above, book II. Cott.] or in prison and come to you?’ And the King will answer and say to them: ‘Amen I say to you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’

“Then he will say to those at his left [Note: [Col. 0731D] “At the left,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott. Voss. 2.]: ‘Depart from me, you accursed, into the eternal fire [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Into eternal punishment,” Cott.] that my Father prepared [Note: [Col. 0731D] “That he prepared,” Bod. 1; so above.] for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry, and you gave me no food; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink; I was a stranger, and you did not bring me in; I was naked, and you did not clothe me; I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Come to me,” Lin.] me.’

“Then they too will answer, saying: ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Render service,” Bod. 1, 4. Thu.; so above, Voss. 2.] to you?’ And he will answer them [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Then he will answer,” Lam. NC. 1. Corb.]: ‘Amen I say to you, insofar as you did not do it to one of these least ones, neither did you do it to me.’ And these will go away into eternal burning, but the just into eternal life” [Col. 0731C] (Matt. XXV, 31–46).

On the same subject in the Gospel according to Luke: “Sell your possessions [Note: [Col. 0731D] “Sell what you possess,” Lin.] and give alms” (Luke XII, 33).

Likewise there: “He who made what is within also made what is without. Nevertheless [Note: [Col. 0731D] “But give,” Bod. 1, 3, 4; “All things are clean for you,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.], give alms, and behold, all things are clean for you” (Luke XI, 40, 41).

Likewise there: “Behold, I give half of my substance to the needy; and if I have [Col. 0732A] defrauded [Note: [Col. 0732C] “Defrauded,” Lin.] anyone of anything, I repay [Note: [Col. 0732C] “I shall repay,” Lam. NC. 1. Corb.] it fourfold.” And 304 Jesus said that salvation had come to this house today, since this man too was a son of Abraham (Luke XIX, 8, 9).

On the same subject [Note: [Col. 0732C] “Paul to,” NC. 1, 2. Corb.] in Second Corinthians: “Let your abundance supply their need, so that their abundance may in turn supply your need, that there may be equality, as it is written: ‘He who had much had no excess, and he who had little was not in need [Note: [Col. 0732C] “Will not be in need,” Corb.; “did not diminish,” Bod. 1. Voss. 2.]’” (II Cor. VIII, 14, 15).

Likewise there: “He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows with blessing [Note: [Col. 0732C] “For a blessing,” Thu.] will also reap from the blessing [Note: [Col. 0732C] “Will reap eternal life,” Lam. NC. 1. Cott.]. But let each person give as he has determined in his heart, not as though from sorrow or necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.”

Likewise there, as it is written: “He distributed, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever.”

Likewise there: “Now he who supplies [Note: [Col. 0732C] “He who supplies,” Lam. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. NC. 1, 2. Thu. Corb.] seed to the sower will also provide bread for eating [Col. 0732B], and he will multiply your seed [Note: [Col. 0732C] “Your sowing,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Benev. Voss. 2.] and increase the produce of your righteousness, so that you may be enriched in all things.”

Likewise there: “The administration of this service not only supplied what the saints lacked, but abounded [Note: [Col. 0732C] “But also abounded,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2; “will abound,” Bod. 2. Thu. Voss. 4.] through many [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Through the thanksgiving of many,” Lam. NC. 1. Cott. Voss. 2.] acts of thanksgiving to God” (II Cor. IX, 6, 7, 9–12).

On the same subject in the Epistle of John: “Whoever possesses the substance of the world [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Of this world,” Lam. NC. 1. Cott.] and sees his brother in need [Note: [Col. 0732D] “In need of something,” Lam. Bod. 2. Ver.], yet closes his inward compassion [Note: [Col. 0732D] “His inward compassion—how,” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Voss. 2.] against him—how does the love of God [Note: [Col. 0732D] “The *agapē* of God,” Benev.] remain in him [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Will remain in him,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]?” (I John III, 17).

On the same subject in the Gospel according to Luke: “When you make a luncheon or dinner, do not invite your friends, or your brothers [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Or your relatives, or your neighbors,” Cott.], or your neighbors, or the rich, lest perhaps they too invite you in return and repayment be made to you. But when you make a feast, invite [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Invite beggars,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott. Voss. 2.] the poor, the disabled, the blind, and the lame; and you will be blessed [Note: [Col. 0732D] “You will be happy,” Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Ver. Voss. 2.], because they have no means of repaying you. But repayment will be made [Note: [Col. 0732D] “But it will be restored,” NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu.] to you at the resurrection [Col. 0732C] of the just” (Luke XIV, 12–14).

**CHAP. II.—IN WORKS AND ALMSGIVING, EVEN IF LESS IS DONE BECAUSE OF LIMITED MEANS, THE INTENTION ITSELF IS SUFFICIENT**

In Paul’s Second Epistle to the Corinthians: “If the intention is ready, the gift is acceptable according to whatever [Note: [Col. 0732D] “By the intention itself, according to what he has,” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2; “according to what each person,” Corb. Voss. 2.] a person has [Note: [Col. 0732D] “Acceptable,” NC. 2.] [Note: [Col. 0731D] “The least of mine,” Corb.] [Col. 0733A], not according to what [Note: [Col. 0733C] “What he did not have,” Lam.] he does not have; nor should there be relief for others [Note: [Col. 0733C] “So that there may be relief for others,” Corb. Bod. 1, 2; “so that others may have relief and you affliction,” Thu.], but affliction for you” (II Cor. VIII, 12, 13).

**CHAP. III.—THAT *AGAPĒ*** [Note: [Col. 0733C] “Love,” Lam. NC. 2. Bod. 1. Voss. 2.] **AND BROTHERLY LOVE MUST BE PRACTICED DEVOUTLY AND STEADFASTLY**

In Malachi: “Did not one God create us? Is there not one father of us all [Note: [Col. 0733C] “Of all? Why,” Corb.]? Why, then, has each one abandoned [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Why does each one despise,” NC. 2. Corb.] his brother?” (Mal. II, 10).

On the same subject according to John: “Peace [Note: [Col. 0733D] “My peace I give you; my peace I leave,” Cott.] I leave with you; my peace I give you” (John XIV, 27).

Likewise there: “This is my commandment: that you love one another just as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this: that a person lay down his life for his friends” (John XV, 12–13).

Likewise there: “Blessed [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Happy,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lam. Thu.] are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God” (Matt. V, 9).

Likewise there: “Amen [Col. 0733B] I say to you that if two [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Two of you agree,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3.] of you agree on earth [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Upon the earth,” Cott.] concerning anything whatsoever that you ask, it will be granted to you by my Father who is in heaven. For wherever two or three are gathered in my name, I am there with them” (Matt. XVIII, 19).

On the same subject in First Corinthians: “And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal people—as to infants [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Little children in Christ,” Cott.] in Christ. I gave you milk to drink [Note: [Col. 0733D] “I fed you with milk,” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Ver. Benev. Thu. Corb.], not solid food [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Not with food,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Thu. Corb.]. For while [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Solid food, for you were not yet able,” Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 2.] you were still little, you were not able to receive it; indeed, even now you are not able, for you are still carnal. For where jealousy [Note: [Col. 0733D] “Jealousy arises among you,” Bod. 3; “among you there are,” Cott.], contention, and dissensions exist among you, are you not carnal, and do you not walk according to man?” (I Cor. III, 1–3).

Likewise there: “Even if I possess all faith, so that I might move mountains, but do not possess love, I am nothing [Note: [Col. 0733D] “I gain nothing,” Bod. 3. NC. 2.]. Even if I distribute everything I possess for food [Note: [Col. 0733D] “For food for the poor,” Lam.], and even if I hand over my [Col. 0733C] body to be burned [Note: [Col. 0733D] “So that it may burn,” Benev. Ver. Corb.], but do not possess love [Note: [Col. 0733D] “*Agapē*,” Lam. NC. 1. Thu. Lin.; so frequently below.], I gain nothing [Note: [Col. 0733D] “I am nothing,” Cott.].

“Love is magnanimous; love [Note: [Col. 0733D] “It is magnanimous, patient, kind; it is not puffed up, does not behave dishonorably, does not seek its own, does not devise evil, rejoices in injustice,” Cott.] is kind. Love is not jealous; love does not behave perversely; it is not puffed up, is not provoked, does not devise evil, does not rejoice over injustice, but rejoices together with the truth. It loves all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things [Note: [Col. 0734C] “Bears all things,” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.]. Love will never fail” (I Cor. XIII, 2–8).

On the same subject in Galatians: “You shall love your neighbor [Note: [Col. 0734C] “Your neighbor as yourself,” Cott. Thu. Corb. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.] as yourself. But if you bite [Note: [Col. 0734C] “Bite and accuse,” Bod. 1; “accuse,” Lam. Bod. 2; “one another,” Bod. 3.] and accuse one another, see that you are not consumed by one another” (Gal. V, 14–16).

On the same [Col. 0734A] subject in the Epistle of John: “By this the children [Note: [Col. 0734D] “The children will become apparent,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] of God and the children of the devil become apparent. Everyone who is not righteous is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother. For he who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him” (I John III, 10, 15).

Likewise there [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Likewise there: He who [hates] his brother,” Thu. Cor.]: “If anyone says that he loves God and hates his brother, he is a liar. For how can one who does not love the brother whom he sees [Note: [Col. 0734D] “The brother whom he sees daily,” Cott.] love God, whom he does not see?”

On the same subject in the Acts of the Apostles: “Now the multitude of those who had believed acted with one soul and one mind; there was no distinction at all among them, nor did they regard anything from the goods [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Nor did anyone regard as his own any of the goods,” Corb.] they possessed as their own, but all things were held by them in common” (Acts IV, 32).

On the same subject in the Gospel [Note: [Col. 0734D] “In the Gospel” is absent from Thu.] according to Matthew: “If you offer your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother [Col. 0734B] has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Then you shall offer,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] your gift at the altar” (Matt. V, 23–24).

Likewise in the Epistle of John: “God is love, and he who remains in love [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Remains in affection,” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] remains in God, and God [Note: [Col. 0734D] “God will be in him,” Bod. 1; “remains in God. Likewise,” Bod. 2, 3, 4.] in him” (I John IV, 16).

Likewise there: “He who says that he is in the light and hates his brother is a liar [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Hates him, is a murderer,” Bod. 3.], and walks in darkness even until now” (I John II, 9).

**CHAP. IV.—ONE MUST GLORY IN NOTHING, SINCE NOTHING IS OURS**
In the Gospel according to John: “No one can receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven” (John 3:27). Likewise in Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “For what do you have that you did not receive? But if you received it, [Col. 0734C] why do you boast as though you had not received it?” [Note: [Col. 0734D] “You received.” Lam. Bod. 1, 2. NC. 1] (1 Cor. 4:7). Likewise in the First Book of Kingdoms: “Do not boast, nor speak lofty things [Note: [Col. 0734D] ‘Utter.’ Bod. 2.] [Note: [Col. 0734D] ‘Loftily.’ Corb.], and let no grandiloquence [Note: [Col. 0734D] ‘Grandiloquent speech.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] proceed from your mouth, because the Lord is a God of knowledge” [Note: [Col. 0734D] “The Lord is a God of knowledge.” Cott.] (1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:3). Likewise there: “The bow of the mighty has been weakened, and the weak have been girded with strength” [Note: [Col. 0734D] “Have been girded with might.” Bod. 3.]. On this same subject in Maccabees: “It is right to be subject to God and, being mortal, not to think oneself equal to God” (2 Macc. 9:12). Likewise there: “And do not fear the words of a sinful man [Note: [Col. 0734D] ‘Do not fear,’ singular. Lam. Lin. NC. Bod. 4. Cott.], because his glory will become dung [Note: [Col. 0734D] ‘In dung.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1.] and worms. Today [Col. 0735A] he will be exalted [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘He is exalted.’ Bod. 2.], and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his thought [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Will perish.’ Lam. Lin. Cott. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] has perished” (1 Macc. 2:62).

## CHAPTER V.—HUMILITY AND QUIETNESS MUST BE MAINTAINED IN ALL THINGS

In Isaiah the Lord God says thus: “Heaven is my throne [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Seat.’ Corb.], and the earth the footstool of my feet. What dwelling [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘What house for me.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.] will you build for me, or what place will be my resting place? For my hand made all these things, and all these things are mine. And upon whom else shall I look [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Upon whom shall I look, except.’ Bod. 2.], except upon the humble and quiet person who trembles [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘And fears.’ Bod. 3.] at my words?” (Isa. 66:1–2). On this same subject in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Blessed are the meek [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Happy are the meek.’ Bod. 4. Thu.], for they shall inherit the earth” (Matt. 5:5). On this same subject according to Luke: “Whoever [Col. 0735B] is least [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Whoever shall be least.’ Bod. 3.] among all of you, he shall be great” (Luke 9:48). Likewise there: “Whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted” (ibid. 14:11). On this same subject, to the Romans: “Do not be high-minded [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Do not look upon lofty things.’ Bod. 3.], but fear. For if God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either” (Rom. 11:20). On this same subject in Psalm 33: “And he will save the humble in spirit.” Likewise to the Romans: “Render to everyone what is owed [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘What is due to everyone.’ Bod. 1.]: tribute to whom tribute is due, tax to whom tax is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due. Owe no one anything except to love one another” (Rom. 13:7). Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “They love the first place at table at banquets [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘At a meal.’ Bod. 3.], the first seats in the synagogues, greetings in the marketplace, and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by people. But do not be called [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Do not be called.’ Lin. ‘Do not let yourselves be called.’ NC. 2. ‘If you have been called.’ Corb.] ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one teacher” [Col. 0735C] (Matt. 23:6–8). Likewise in the Gospel according to John: “A servant is not greater than his master, nor an apostle greater than the one who sent him. Knowing these things, you will be blessed [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘You will be happy.’ Bod. 1, 4.] if you do them” (John 13:16). Likewise in Psalm 81: “Vindicate the humble and the poor.”

## CHAPTER VI.—ALL GOOD [Note: [Col. 0735D] “Good also.” Bod. 1, 2, 4.] AND RIGHTEOUS PEOPLE MUST LABOR MORE, BUT MUST ENDURE IT, BECAUSE THEY ARE BEING TESTED

In Solomon: “The furnace tests the potter’s vessels, and the trial 306 of tribulation tests righteous people” (Ecclus. 27:6). Likewise in Psalm 50: “A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit; a contrite and humbled heart God will not despise” [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Does not despise.’ Bod. 2. ‘Will not reject.’ Lin. NC. 2. Bod. 3. Thu. Corb.]. Likewise in Psalm 33: “The Lord is near [Col. 0736A] to those who are contrite [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Troubled in heart.’ Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott.] in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.” Likewise there: “Many are the afflictions [Note: [Col. 0735D] ‘Many are the scourges.’ Bod. 3. ‘Many are the tribulations.’ NC. 2. Cott.] of the righteous, but [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘And from all.’ Corb.] from all of them the Lord will deliver them.” On this same subject in Job: “Naked I came forth from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall also go [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘I shall go into the earth.’ Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Cott.] beneath the earth. The Lord gave; the Lord has taken away. As it pleased the Lord [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘As seemed good to the Lord.’ Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Thu. Corb. Cott.], so it has been done. Blessed be the name of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Blessed forever.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]. “In all these things that befell him [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Befell him, nothing.’ Bod. 2.], Job sinned in nothing with his lips in the sight of the Lord” (Job 1:21). On this same subject in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Blessed are those who mourn [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Happy.’ Bod. 4. Thu. ‘Those who grieve.’ Bod. 1. ‘Those who grieve.’ Cott. ‘Those who mourn now.’ Lam. NC. 1.], for they shall be comforted” (Matt. 5:4). Likewise according to John: “I have spoken these things to you so that you may have peace in me; but in the world you will have affliction [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Affliction, but.’ Thu. Bod. 1, 3, 4.]. But take courage [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Have confidence.’ Bod. 1, 3.], because I have conquered the world” [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Conquered the age.’ Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Corb.] (John 16:33). On this same subject, in the Second Epistle to the Corinthians: “There was given to me a thorn in my flesh, an angel of Satan, to strike [Col. 0736B] me, so that I should not be exalted. Because of this I asked the Lord three times that it might depart from me, and he said to me: ‘My grace is sufficient for you, for power is perfected in weakness’” (2 Cor. 12:7–9). On this same subject, to the Romans: “We boast in the hope of the glory of God; and not only this, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance, endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope. Hope, moreover, does not put us to shame, because the love of God has been poured [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Poured abroad.’ Cott.] into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us” (Rom. 5:2–5). On this same subject according to Matthew: “How broad and spacious is the road that leads to destruction, and many are those [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Enter.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb.] who enter by it! How confined and narrow is the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it!” (Matt. 7:13). On this same subject in Tobit: “Where are your righteous deeds? See what you are suffering” [Col. 0736C] (Tob. 2:24). Likewise in the Wisdom of Solomon: “In the places of the impious, the righteous groan. But at their destruction the righteous shall abound” [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘At their destruction they shall howl.’ Cott. ‘Their destruction.’ Printed edition.] (Prov. 28:28).

## CHAPTER VII.—THE HOLY SPIRIT WHOM WE HAVE RECEIVED MUST NOT BE GRIEVED [Note: [Col. 0736D] “Not to grieve.” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.]

Paul [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Paul to.’ Oxon. Corb. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 3.] the apostle to the Ephesians: “Do not grieve God’s Holy Spirit, in whom you were sealed for the day [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘For the day.’ Thu. Corb. Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2.] of redemption. Let all bitterness, wrath, indignation, shouting, and blasphemy [Note: [Col. 0736D] ‘Be removed.’ Thu. Corb. ‘From you, together with all malice.’ Vir. Cott.] be removed from you” (Eph. 4:30).

[Note: [Col. 0737D]

**CHAPTER VIII.—Without cause.** Cassian, book VIII, chapter 20, writes that *without cause* is read in certain copies, and adds that the words *without cause* are superfluous and were added by those who thought that anger arising from just causes should by no means be imputed as guilt—although, of course, no one who is moved to anger, however irrationally, says that he is angry without cause. Jerome also, in his comments on chapter IV [Col. 0738D] of the Epistle to the Ephesians and chapter V of Matthew, from which this passage was taken, says that *without cause* is added by certain manuscripts and that it should be deleted, because the anger of a righteous man does not accomplish the righteousness of God. See Erasmus’s annotations on this passage in Matthew, and René Massuet on book IV of Irenaeus, chapter 13.]

## CHAPTER VIII.—ANGER MUST BE OVERCOME, LEST IT COMPEL ONE TO SIN

[Col. 0737A]

In Solomon, in Proverbs: “A patient man is better than a strong man. For one who restrains anger [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘Despises anger.’ Bod. 3, 4. ‘One who restrains anger shall capture a city.’ Cott.] is better than one who captures a city” (Prov. 16:32). Likewise [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘In the Parables.’ Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2. ‘Proverbs.’ NC. 2.] there: “A foolish person declares his anger on that very day, but a shrewd person conceals his own dishonor” (ibid. 12:16). On this same subject [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘Paul.’ Oxon. Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2. Absent from the printed editions.], to the Ephesians: “Be angry, and do not sin [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘Transgress.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 4.]. Do not let the sun set upon your anger” (Eph. 4:26). Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “You have heard that it was said [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘It was said by the ancients.’ Lam. NC. 1.] to the ancients: ‘You shall not kill; but whoever kills shall be answerable to the court.’ But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause shall be answerable to the court” (Matt. 5:21).

## CHAPTER IX.—BROTHERS MUST BEAR WITH ONE ANOTHER

[Col. 0737B]

To [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘Paul to.’ Oxon. Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2.] the Galatians: “Each of you keeping watch [Note: [Col. 0737C] ‘You, brothers, even if a person has been overtaken in some transgression, you who are spiritual, attend to such a person in [Col. 0737D] a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself lest you too be tempted. Bear one another’s burdens.’ Cott.] lest you too be tempted. Bear one another’s [Note: [Col. 0737D] ‘One another’s burdens.’ NC. 2. Lin. ‘Your burdens.’ NC. 1. Bod. 2.] burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ” (Gal. 6:1).

## CHAPTER X.—ONE MUST TRUST IN GOD ALONE [Note: [Col. 0737D] “In God alone.” Bod. 2.] AND BOAST IN HIM

In Jeremiah: “Let not the wise person boast in his wisdom, nor the strong person boast in his strength, nor the rich person boast in his riches; but let the one who boasts boast in this [Note: [Col. 0737D] ‘Let the strong person boast.’ Cott. ‘Let the strong person who boasts, boast.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]: in understanding and knowing [Note: [Col. 0737D] ‘He ought to know.’ Thu. ‘And let him know that I am the Lord.’ Cott.] that I am the Lord, who exercises mercy, judgment, and righteousness upon the earth, because in these things is my will, says the Lord” (Jer. 9:22). On this same subject in Psalm 54: “I have hoped in the Lord; I shall not fear what a human being may do to me.” Likewise there: “My soul is subject [Col. 0737C] to God alone” [Note: [Col. 0737D] ‘Suddenly to God.’ Bod. 2.]. Likewise in Psalm 117: “I shall not fear what a human being may do to me; the Lord is my helper” [Note: [Col. 0737D] ‘Aid.’ Lam. Lin. Bod. 2. ‘And I shall look upon my enemies.’ [Col. 0738C] Cott.]. Likewise there, 307: “It is better to trust in the Lord [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘The Lord.’ Thu. Cott. ‘In the Lord.’ Oxon.] than to trust in a human being [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘In human beings.’ Thu. Bod. 4. Cott.]. It is better to hope in the Lord than to hope in princes” [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘In princes.’ Bod. 1, 2, 4.]. On this same subject in Daniel: “Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar: [Col. 0738A] ‘O king, we have no need to answer you concerning this matter [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘To answer you concerning this discourse.’ Bod. 2.]. For the God whom we serve is able to rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire, and he will deliver us from your hands, O king. But if not, let it be known [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘And now let it be known.’ Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] to you that we do not serve your gods, and we do not worship the golden image that you have set up’” [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘Nor do we worship the golden image that you have set up.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. ‘We shall worship.’ Corb.] (Dan. 3:16–18). Likewise in Jeremiah: “Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human being; and blessed is the person who trusts in the Lord, and his hope will be in God” (Jer. 17:5). On this same subject in Deuteronomy: “You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve” (Deut. 6:13). On this same subject, to the Romans: “And they worshiped and served the creature, abandoning the Creator [Note: [Col. 0738C] ‘The Creator, who is blessed forever.’ Lam. NC. 1. [Col. 0738D] Bod. 2. Cott.]. Therefore God also handed them over to passions of dishonor” (Rom. 1:25). On this same subject in John: “Greater is the one who is in you than the one who is in this [Col. 0738B] world” (1 John 4:4).

[Note: [Col. 0739D]

**CHAPTER XI.—Our commonwealth.** See Fronton du Duc’s notes on Chrysostom’s Homily XLVI, on Saint Julian [Col. 0740D] the martyr.]

## CHAPTER XI.—ONE WHO HAS ATTAINED FAITH, HAVING PUT OFF THE FORMER [Note: [Col. 0738D] “Having stripped off the former.” Thu.] PERSON, MUST THINK ONLY OF HEAVENLY AND SPIRITUAL THINGS AND MUST NOT ATTEND TO THE WORLD, WHICH HE HAS ALREADY RENOUNCED

In Isaiah: “Seek the Lord; and when you find him, call upon him. But when he draws near to you, let the impious person abandon his ways, and the criminal man [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘The criminal man, his paths.’ Corb. ‘The unrighteous man, his counsels.’ Lin.] his thoughts, and let him turn to the Lord, and he will obtain mercy, because he will abundantly [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘Because he is exceedingly merciful and will forgive.’ Bod. 4.] forgive your sins” (Isa. 55:6). On this same subject in Solomon: “I saw all the works that are done beneath the sun, and behold, all is vanity” (Eccles. 1:14). On this same subject in Exodus: “This is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your [Col. 0738C] shoes [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘And your boots.’ Lam. NC. 1. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott.] on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. For it is the Passover of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘It is the Lord’s Passover.’ Thu.] (Exod. 12:11). On this same subject in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Do not be anxious, saying: ‘What shall we eat, or what shall we drink [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘What do we eat, or what do we drink?’ Cott.], or what shall we wear?’ For the nations seek these things [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘The nations seek.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.]. But your Father knows [Note: [Col. 0738D] ‘For the Father knows.’ Cott.] that you need all these things. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added [Col. 0739A] to you.” Likewise there: “Do not be anxious about tomorrow. For tomorrow [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘For tomorrow itself.’ Bod. 1.] will take thought [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘Takes thought.’ Bod. 1. ‘Took thought.’ Bod. 3, 4.] for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own evil” (Matt. 6:31–34). Likewise there: “No one who looks back and places his hand upon the plow is fit for the kingdom of God” (Luke 9:62). Likewise there: “Look at the birds of heaven: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘Your heavenly Father nourishes them.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 3. Cott.]. Are you not worth more than they?” (Matt. 6:26). On this same subject according to Luke: “Let your loins [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘Your loins girded.’ Lam. Lin. Bod. 2. NC. 1, 2. Cott.] be girded and your lamps burning [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘Burning in your hands.’ Bod. 1, 3.], and you be like people awaiting their master when he comes [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘When he returns.’ Cott.] from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him. Blessed are those servants whom the master, when he comes, finds watching” (Luke 12:35–37). On this same subject in Matthew: “Foxes [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘Foxes have dens.’ Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. NC. Thu. Corb.] have dens, and the birds of heaven have resting places [Note: [Col. 0739C] ‘The birds of heaven, nests.’ Cott.], but the Son of Man [Col. 0739B] has nowhere to lay [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘To incline his head.’ Thu. ‘To rest it.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] his head” (Matt. 8:20). Likewise there: “Anyone who does not renounce everything that belongs to him cannot be my disciple” (Luke 14:33). On this same subject, in the First Epistle to the Corinthians: “You are not your own. For you were bought [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘You were bought at a great price.’ Lam. Bod. 2, 4. NC. 1.] at a great price. Glorify and bear God in your body” (1 Cor. 6:19). Likewise there: “The time has been shortened [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘For the time is short.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.], as though they did not mourn; those who rejoice, as though they did not rejoice; those who buy, as though they did not buy; those who possess, as though they did not possess; and those who use this world [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘Make use of this world.’ Cott.], as though they did not use it [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘As though they did not make full use of it.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]. For the form of this world is passing away” (ibid. 7:29–31). Likewise there: “The first man was from the clay of the earth [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘From the earth, from clay.’ Bod. 2, 4. ‘From clay.’ Corb. ‘Earthly, from clay.’], the second man from heaven [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘Heavenly, from heaven.’ Cott.]. Just as [Col. 0739C] we have borne the image of the one who is from clay, let us also bear the image of the one who is from heaven” (ibid. 15:47–49). On this same subject, to the Philippians: “All [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘For all.’ Lam. NC. 1. ‘They seek their own interests.’ Bod. 1. Cott.] seek their own interests, and not those of Christ [Note: [Col. 0739D] ‘Likewise there: Many walk, of whom I often used to tell you, but now tell you even with tears: they are enemies of the cross of Christ.’ [Col. 0740C] Cott.]” (Phil. 2:21); “Their end is destruction, 308 their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘In shame.’ Thu. ‘In their shameful parts.’ Bod. 1.], they who are intent upon earthly things. But our commonwealth is in heaven; from there we also await as Savior our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0740A] who will transform the body of our humility, conforming it [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Configured.’ Bod. 3. ‘Into conformity.’ Cott.] to the body of his glory” (Phil. 3:19–21). On this same subject, to the Galatians: “But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world” (Gal. 6:14). On this same subject, to Timothy: “No one serving as a soldier for God entangles himself in worldly troubles [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Entangles himself in affairs.’ NC. 2. Cott.], so that he may please the one to whom he has commended himself. And even if someone competes [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Competes in the contest.’ Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1. Cott.], he will not be crowned unless he has fought according to the rules” (2 Tim. 2:4). On this same subject, to the Colossians: “If you have died with Christ to the elements of the world [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Of this world.’ NC. 1. Bod. 2.], why [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Why still?’ Cott.], as though living in the world [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Do you make decrees concerning this world?’ Cott.], do you pursue vain things?” (Col. 2:20). Likewise on this same subject: “If you have risen together [Note: [Col. 0740C] ‘Risen with Christ.’ Bod. 2, 4. ‘Risen together with Christ.’ [Col. 0740D] Lam.] with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at God’s right hand. Set your mind upon the things that are above, not upon earthly things [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Not upon the things that are upon the earth.’ Cott.]. For you have died, [Col. 0740B] and your life is hidden with Christ in God. But when Christ, your life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory” (ibid. 3:1–4). On this same subject, to the Ephesians: “Put off [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Lay aside.’ Corb. ‘Purge away your former way of life.’ Cott.] the old person belonging to your former way of life, who is being corrupted according to deceitful desires [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘The desires of error.’ Cott. ‘Be renewed—the person.’ Cott.]. But be renewed in the spirit of your understanding, and put on the new person [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘The person who.’ Bod. 3. Thu.], the one who has been fashioned according to God [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Has been created in righteousness.’ Cott.] in righteousness, holiness, and truth” (Eph. 4:22–24). On this same subject in Peter’s Epistle: “As guests and strangers, abstain from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul; but maintain [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Maintain good conduct among the Gentiles.’ Lam. Cott.] good conduct among the Gentiles, so that while they malign [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Speak about you.’ Cott. ‘Think that you should be maligned.’ Bod. 1.] you as evildoers [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘As malefactors.’ Cott.], they may look upon your good works and magnify God” (1 Pet. 2:11). On this same subject in John’s Epistle: “The one who says that he remains in [Col. 0740C] Christ ought himself to walk as Christ walked.” Likewise there: “Do not love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love is not in him, because everything in the world is the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the ambition of the age, which is not from the Father but from the desire of the age [Note: [Col. 0740D] ‘Its desire and the world.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2.]; and the world will pass away, and its desire. Bod. 2.], not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth” (1 Cor. 5:7–8).
