**CHAPTER XII.—He will not be justified.** The English edition adds from a certain old book: “so that if he swears in vain, he will be punished twice.” There, however, it is noted that these words are absent from the printed editions; they do occur in chapter XXIII of the book [Col. 0742D] of Ecclesiasticus, but in different words.

601 **Again you have heard.** The passage from these words through “On this same subject” was added from Lamonius’s manuscript and the Grenoble manuscript.]

## CHAPTER XII.—ONE MUST NOT SWEAR

In Solomon [Note: [Col. 0741C] ‘Solomon: much.’ Bod. 1, 3, 4.]: “A man who swears much [Note: [Col. 0741C] ‘Will be filled.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Cott.] will be filled with iniquity, and a plague will not depart from his house; and if he swears vainly, he will not be justified” [Note: [Col. 0741C] Oxon. adds: ‘And if he swears in vain, he will be punished twice.’] (Ecclus. 23:11). On this same subject according to Matthew: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancients: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall render your oaths to the Lord.’ But I say to you: Do not swear at all [Note: [Col. 0741C] ‘Do not swear in any way.’ Oxon.], either by heaven, because it is the Lord’s throne; or by the earth, [Col. 0741B] because it is the footstool of his feet; or by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great king. Nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black. Let your speech be: ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever exceeds these comes from evil” (Matt. 5:34–37). On this same subject in Exodus: “You shall not take the name of the Lord your God [Note: [Col. 0741C] ‘Into your mouth in vain.’ Bod. 3.] in vain” (Exod. 20:7).

## CHAPTER XIII.—ONE MUST NOT CURSE

In Exodus: “You shall not curse, nor shall you speak evil of the ruler of your people” (Exod. 22:27–28). Likewise in Psalm 33: “Who is the person who desires life and loves to see [Note: [Col. 0741C] ‘And longs to see.’ NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1. Cott.] good days [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘The best days.’ Lam. Bod. 4. Thu.]? Restrain [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Keep your tongue.’ Cott.] your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit” [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘From speaking treacherously.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Ver. Bod. 2. Thu.]. On this same subject in Leviticus: “And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: ‘Bring the one who [Col. 0741C] has cursed outside the camp, and all who heard shall place their hands upon his head, and the whole congregation of the children of Israel shall stone [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘They shall stone.’ Thu. Cott.] him’” (Lev. 24:13). On this same subject in Paul’s Epistle to the Ephesians: “Let no evil word proceed 309 from your mouth [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Come forth.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 4.], but only what is good for the edification of faith, so that it may give grace to those who hear” (Eph. 4:29). On this same subject, to the Romans: “Blessing [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Bless, and do not curse.’ Cott.], and not cursing” (Rom. 12:14). On this same subject, [Col. 0742A] in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Whoever says to his brother, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Shall be liable to Gehenna.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Corb. Cott.] of fire” (Matt. 5:22). On this same subject according to the same Matthew: “But I say to you that for every idle word [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Empty word.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.] that people speak, they shall give an account of it on the day of judgment. For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned [Note: [Col. 0741D] ‘Damned.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.]” (Matt. 12:36).

## CHAPTER XIV.—ONE MUST NEVER GRUMBLE, BUT MUST BLESS GOD FOR EVERYTHING THAT HAPPENS [Note: [Col. 0741D] “Happens, always.” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.]

In Job: “‘Speak some word against the Lord [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘Against the Lord.’ Cott.], and die.’ But he looked at her and said: ‘You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘Accepted.’ Bod. 3.] good things from the Lord’s hand, why should we not endure [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘Shall we not endure evil things?’ Bod. 1, 2, 4.] evil things?’ In all [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘In all.’ Bod. 2.] these things that befell him, Job sinned in nothing with his lips in the sight of the Lord” (Job 2:9). Likewise there: [Col. 0742B] “Have you considered [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘Have you considered my servant?’ Lin. ‘Have you considered the servant?’ Lam. Bod. 1, 3, 4. NC. 1. ‘Have you seen the servant?’ Cott.] my servant Job? For there is no one like him on earth: a man without reproach, a true worshiper of God, abstaining from every evil [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘Every evil work.’ Bod. 3.]” (Job 1:8). On this same subject in Psalm 33: “I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall always be in my mouth.” On this same subject in Numbers: “Let their murmuring against me cease, and they shall not die” (Num. 17:10). On this same subject in the Acts of the Apostles: “But around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and giving thanks to God, while the prisoners [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘The other prisoners.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.] listened to them” (Acts 16:25). Likewise in Paul’s Epistle to the Philippians: “But do everything out of love [Note: [Col. 0742C] ‘For pleasure.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.], without murmuring [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Without murmuring and hesitation.’ Cott.] or disputing, so that you may be blameless and spotless [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Spotless, like.’ Cott. Bod. 2.] children of God” (Phil. 2:14).

## CHAPTER XV.—PEOPLE ARE TEMPTED BY GOD SO THAT THEY MAY BE TESTED [Note: [Col. 0742D] “So that they may be examined.” NC. 2. Bod. 1, 4.]

[Col. 0742C]

In Genesis: “And God tested Abraham and said to him: ‘Take your son [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘That son of yours.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Thu.], your only son Isaac, whom you love [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Whom you have loved.’ Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu.], and go into the high land [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘High.’ Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Cott. Oxon. omits it.], offering [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘And you shall offer.’ Bod. 1, 2, 3. Corb. ‘As a whole burnt-offering, a sacrificial victim’: the printed edition and most manuscript copies.], upon one [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Upon one.’ Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] of the mountains of which I shall tell you’” [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Which I shall tell you.’ Cott.] (Gen. 22:1). On this same subject in Deuteronomy: “The Lord your God is testing [Note: [Col. 0742D] ‘Has tested you.’ Cott.] you, so that he may know [Col. 0743A] whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul” (Deut. 13:3). On this same subject in the Wisdom of Solomon: “And even if they have suffered torments in the sight of human beings, their hope is full of immortality; and though chastised in a few things, they shall be well provided for in many, because God tested them [Note: [Col. 0743C] ‘Tested them and found them worthy to be—and as a whole burnt-offering.’ Cott.] and found them worthy of himself. Like gold in the furnace he tested them, and like whole burnt-offerings and sacrificial victims [Note: [Col. 0743C] ‘A whole burnt-offering and sacrificial victim.’ Bod. 1. ‘The sacrificial victim of a whole burnt-offering.’ Lam. NC. Bod. 2, 3. ‘A whole burnt-offering, a sacrificial victim.’ Ben. Ver. Thu.] he accepted them; and at the appointed time [Note: [Col. 0743C] ‘At that time.’ Bod. 1.] there will be a visitation for them” [Note: [Col. 0743D] ‘At the time of their visitation they will shine; they will run like sparks through reeds.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.]. “They shall judge nations and rule over peoples, and their Lord shall reign forever” (Wis. 3:4). On this same subject in Maccabees [Note: [Col. 0743D] ‘In Genesis.’ Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]: “Was not Abraham found faithful under testing, and was it not reckoned to him as righteousness?” (1 Macc. 2:52).

## CHAPTER XVI.—ON THE GOOD OF MARTYRDOM
In the Proverbs of Solomon: “A faithful [Col. 0743B] witness delivers a soul from evils” [Note: [Col. 0743D] “His own soul” Lam. NC. 1. Cott.; “a witness of God” Bod. 2.] (Prov. 14:25). Likewise there: “Then the righteous will stand with great constancy against those who oppressed them and took away their labors [Note: [Col. 0743D] “Who plundered their labors” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Cott.]. When they see them, they will be troubled with terrible fear and will marvel at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation, saying among themselves [Note: [Col. 0743D] “They will say among themselves” Thu.], repenting [Note: [Col. 0743D] “Doing penance” Cott.] and groaning in anguish of spirit: ‘These are the ones whom we once held in derision [Note: [Col. 0743D] “As a laughingstock and as an object of reproach” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Corb. NC. 1. Cott.] and as an object of reproach. In our folly we reckoned their life madness and their end dishonorable. How [Note: [Col. 0743D] “Behold how” Bod. 3.] have they been numbered among the children of God, and how has their lot come to be among the saints! Therefore we strayed from the way of truth; the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise for us. We wearied ourselves [Note: [Col. 0743D] “We were dislocated” Cott.] in the way of iniquity and destruction, and we walked through difficult deserts, but [Col. 0743C] we did not know the way of the Lord. What did pride profit us [Note: [Col. 0743D] “To what end did pride profit us?” Cott.], or what did the boasting of riches bring us? All those things passed away like a shadow’” (Wis. 5:1–9).

On this same matter, in Psalm 115: “Precious [Note: [Col. 0743D] “Precious is” Lam. NC. 1.] in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints” [Note: [Col. 0743D] “The death of the righteous” Bod. 1, 4. Thu.]. Likewise in Psalm 125: “Those who sow in tears will reap in exultation [Note: [Col. 0743D] “In joy” Lin. Cott.]. As they went [Note: [Col. 0743D] “They went and wept, carrying” Lin.; “they were walking” Thu.; “they walk and weep” Corb.; “Going, they will go and weep, [Col. 0744C] casting” Cott.], they walked and wept, casting their seed; but as they return, they will come in exultation, carrying their armfuls [Note: [Col. 0744C] “Carrying their own sheaves” Lin. Bod. 1; “bearing” Cott.].”

310 On this same matter, in the Gospel according to John: “He who loves his life will lose it, and he who hates his life in this age will find [Note: [Col. 0744C] “Preserves” Bod. 2. Lam. NC. 1; “will preserve” Lin. Bod. 1, 4. Thu. Corb.] [Col. 0744A] it unto eternal life” (John 12:25). Likewise there: “When they hand you over, do not consider what you are to say. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you” (Matt. 10:19). Likewise there: “The hour will come when everyone who kills you [Note: [Col. 0744C] “Who has killed you” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.] will think [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Will think it a service” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu.; “a judgment for God” Cott.] that he is rendering a service to God. And they will do this because they have known neither the Father nor me” (John 16:2).

On this same matter, according to Matthew: “Blessed are those who have suffered persecution for righteousness’ sake [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Because of righteousness” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2.], for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5:10). Likewise there: “Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Destroy in Gehenna” Lam.; “cast into Gehenna” Cott. NC. 1. Thu.]” (Matt. 10:28). Likewise there: “Whoever confesses me before men, I too will confess him before my Father [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Before my Father and his angels” Bod. 1.] who [Col. 0744B] is in heaven. Cott.] to the end will be saved” (Ibid. 32:22).

On this same matter, according to Luke: “Blessed will you be when men hate you, exclude you, drive you out, and curse your name as evil because of the Son of Man. Rejoice on that day and exult; for behold, your reward is great [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Great in heaven” Bod. 1, 4; “is abundant” Cott.] in heaven” (Luke 6:22). Likewise there: “Amen, I say to you, there is no one [Note: [Col. 0744D] “There is no one here” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] who leaves [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Who has left” Bod. 4.] house or parents [Note: [Col. 0744D] “House or field” Corb.], or brothers, or wife, or children [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Or children or fields” Cott.] for the kingdom of God, and does not receive seven times as much in this present time, and in the age to come eternal life [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Will possess eternal life” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.]” (Luke 18:29).

On this same matter, in the Apocalypse: “And when he had opened the fifth sign [Note: [Col. 0744D] “The fifth seal” Bod. 1.], I saw beneath God’s altar the souls of those slain because of the Word [Col. 0744C] of God and their testimony; and they cried out in a loud voice, saying: ‘How long, holy and true Lord, will you refrain from judging and avenging our blood upon those who dwell on the earth?’ And white robes were given [Note: [Col. 0744D] “And a white robe was given to each one” Thu.] to each of them, and they were told to rest for yet a short time [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Yet a short time” Corb.], until the number [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Until there is supplied” Bod. 2.] of their fellow servants and brothers should be completed—those who would afterward be killed after their example” (Rev. 6:7–11).

Likewise there: “After these things I saw a great multitude, which no one among them could number [Note: [Col. 0744D] “Which no one could number” Lam. Lin. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lin.], from every nation, every tribe, every people, and every language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. [Col. 0745A] They were clothed in white robes, and palms were in their hands; and with a great cry they said: ‘Salvation belongs to our God [Note: [Col. 0745C] “Praise to our God” Bod. 3.], who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.’ And one of the elders answered and said to me [Note: [Col. 0745C] “And one of the elders, answering, said to me” Bod. 3.]: ‘Who are these who are clothed in white robes, and from where [Note: [Col. 0745C] “Who are these, and from where” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 3.] have they come?’ And I said to him: ‘My lord, you know’ [Note: [Col. 0745C] “Lord, you know” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.]. And he said to me: ‘These are they who have come out of the great tribulation and have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Therefore they are [Note: [Col. 0745C] “For this reason they are” Lam. NC. 1. Thu. Corb. Cott.] before the throne of God and serve him day and night in his temple; and he who sits upon the throne will dwell over them. Cott.] nor ever thirst; neither will the sun fall upon them, nor will they suffer any heat [Note: [Col. 0745D] “Any pain” Bod. 3.], because the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shelter [Note: [Col. 0745D] “Will rule” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.] them and lead them [Note: [Col. 0745D] “To lead them” Bod. 2.] to springs of the waters of life [Note: [Col. 0745D] “To the spring of life” Cott.; “to the spring of the water of life” Bod. 3.], and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes [Note: [Col. 0745D] “From the eyes” Bod. 1, 3.]’” (Rev. 7:[Col. 0745B]9–17).

Likewise there: “To him who conquers, I will give to eat of the tree of life [Note: [Col. 0745D] “From the tree” Bod. 1, 3, 4.] that is in the paradise of my God.” Likewise there: “Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life” (Rev. 2:7–10). “Blessed [Note: [Col. 0745D] “Happy” Bod. 1, 4. Thu.] will be those who keep watch and preserve [Note: [Col. 0745D] “Who keep watch and preserve” Bod. 1. Cott.] their garments, lest they walk naked and people see their shame” (Rev. 16:15).

On this same matter, Paul in the Second Epistle to Timothy [Note: [Col. 0745D] “Likewise Paul to Timothy” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Thu. Corb.]: “I am already being poured out as a libation [Note: [Col. 0745D] “I am already being offered” Bod. 1, 2. Thu.], and the time of my departure is at hand [Note: [Col. 0745D] “My departure is at hand” Bod. 1, 3, 4; “of my laying to rest” Cott.]. I have fought the good contest [Note: [Col. 0745D] “The good struggle” Bod. 2. Cott.; “I have completed the course” Cott.], I have finished the course, I have kept the faith. Now there remains [Note: [Col. 0746C] “For the rest, there is laid up” Cott.] for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous [Note: [Col. 0746C] “That righteous” Bod. 1, 2, 4.] judge, will give me on that day; and not only to me, but also to all who have loved his coming” (2 Tim. 4:6–8).

But if children, then also heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ—provided that we suffer together with him [Note: [Col. 0746C] “That we suffer together and be glorified together” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2; “that we be glorified together” Bod. 1.], so that we may also be glorified together with him” (Rom. [Col. 0745C]8:16).

On this same matter, in Psalm 118: “Blessed [Note: [Col. 0746C] “Happy” Bod. 1, 4. Thu.] 311 are those who are undefiled in the way and who walk in the law of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Who walk in the way of the Lord” Bod. 1, 2. Thu. Corb.]. Blessed are those who search out his testimonies [*martyria*] [Note: [Col. 0746D] “His testimonies, and seek him with their whole heart” Bod. 1.].”

**CHAPTER XVII.—On this same matter, in Maccabees.** This passage and those that follow down to the end of the chapter were added from the English edition and the manuscript of Foix, and also from the Tours manuscript. [Col. 0746D]]

## CHAPTER XVII.—THAT THE THINGS WE SUFFER IN THIS AGE ARE LESS THAN THE REWARD THAT HAS BEEN PROMISED

In Paul’s Epistle to the Romans: “The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the coming [Note: [Col. 0746D] “The future glory” Bod. 1.] glory that will be revealed in us” (Rom. 8:18).

On this same matter [Note: [Col. 0746D] The words “On this same matter, in Maccabees” are absent from the printed editions, but are acknowledged by Veron. Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.], in Maccabees: “Lord, who possess holy knowledge, it is evident that, though I could be delivered from death, [Col. 0746A] I endure the most severe bodily pains as I am beaten with scourges; but in my soul I willingly suffer these things because of my fear of you” (2 Macc. 6:30). Likewise there: “You indeed, powerless as you are, destroy us out of this present life. But the King of the world will raise us, who have died for his laws, to an eternal resurrection of life.” Likewise there: “It is better for those given over to death by men to await hope from God, since we shall be raised again by him. For you, however, there will be no resurrection to life.” Likewise there: “Though you possess authority among men, you are corruptible and do what you please. But do not think that our people have been forsaken by God. Wait and see how his great power will torment you and your offspring.” Likewise there: “Do not wander vainly into error. For we suffer these things on our own account, because we have sinned against our God. But do not suppose that you will go unpunished, since you have undertaken [Col. 0746B] to fight against God” (2 Macc. 7:9–19).

## CHAPTER XVIII.—NOTHING IS TO BE PREFERRED TO THE LOVE OF GOD AND CHRIST

In Deuteronomy: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength” (Deut. 6:5). Likewise in the Gospel according to Matthew: “He who loves father or mother above me [Note: [Col. 0746D] “More than me” Cott.] is not worthy of me; and he who [Note: [Col. 0746D] “And he who cherishes” Corb.] loves son or daughter above me is not worthy of me; and he who does not take up his cross and follow me is not my disciple” (Matt. 10:37).

Likewise in Paul’s Epistle to the Romans: “Who will separate us [Note: [Col. 0746D] “What will separate us?” Thu.] from the love of Christ [Note: [Col. 0746D] “From the *agapē* of Christ” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 4. Corb.]? Affliction, or distress, or persecution [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Tribulation, distress” Cott.], or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword? As it is written: ‘For your sake [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Because of you” Bod. 3.] we are killed [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Put to death” Cott.] all day long; we have been reckoned as sheep [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Sheep for slaughter” Bod. 1. Cott.] destined for sacrifice.’ But in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us” (Rom. 8:35–37).

## CHAPTER XIX.—WE MUST OBEY NOT OUR OWN WILL, BUT GOD’S

[Col. 0746C]

In the Gospel according to John: “I did not come down from heaven to do my own will, but the will of him [Note: [Col. 0746D] “Of my Father who sent me” Cott.] who sent me” (John 6:38). On this same matter, according to Matthew: “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not what I will, but what you will [Note: [Col. 0746D] “But what you will” Cott.]” (Matt. 26:39). Likewise in the daily prayer: “Your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.” Likewise according to Matthew: “Not [Col. 0747A] everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven—he will enter the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 7:21). Likewise according to Luke: “But that servant who knows his lord’s will and has not obeyed his will shall be beaten with many blows [Note: [Col. 0747D] “With many lashes” Cott.]” (Luke 12:47). In John’s Epistle: “But he who does the will of God abides forever, just as he himself abides forever [Note: [Col. 0747D] “God abides forever” Cott.]” (1 John 2:17).

[Note: [Col. 0747D]

**CHAPTER XX.—Likewise in Deuteronomy.** This passage and those that follow, down to “Likewise in Psalm 33: Fear the Lord,” [Col. 0748D] were added from the manuscript of Saint-Albin and the Arras manuscript of Saint Eligius.]

## CHAPTER XX.—THAT THE FOUNDATION AND SUPPORT OF HOPE AND FAITH IS FEAR

In Psalm 110: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” On this same matter, in the Wisdom of Solomon: “The beginning of wisdom is to fear God” (Sir. 1:16). Likewise in the Proverbs of the same author: “Blessed is the man who is wary of everything through fear [Col. 0747B] [Note: [Col. 0748D] “Of everything because of fear” Cott.]” (Prov. 28:14).

On this same matter, in Isaiah: “And upon whom else shall I look, except upon one who is humble and quiet and trembles at my words?” (Isa. 66:2). On this same matter, in Genesis: “And the angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said to him: ‘Abraham, Abraham.’ He said: ‘Here I am.’ And he said: ‘Do not lay [Note: [Col. 0748D] “Bring” a hand, Cott.] your hand upon the boy, nor do anything to him. For now I know that you fear your God and have not spared your most beloved son for my sake’” (Gen. 22:11).

Likewise in Psalm 2: “Serve the Lord in fear and exult before him with trembling.” Likewise in Deuteronomy, the voice of God to Moses: “Assemble the people before me, and let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear 312 me all the days that they live upon the earth” (Deut. 4:10).

Likewise in Jeremiah: “Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will establish [Col. 0747C] a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel. After those days, says the Lord, I will put my law into their understanding and write it there; and I will be their God, and they will be my people. Each one will no longer teach his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest; for I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more. If heaven should be raised on high, says the Lord, and if the earth should be brought low beneath, even then I will not reject [Col. 0747D] the race of Israel, says the Lord, for all that they have done. Behold, I will gather them from every land into which I scattered them in my anger, my fury, and my great indignation; and I will bring them into this place and leave them in fear. They will be my people, and I will be their God; and I will give them another way and another heart, so that they may fear me all their days, for their own good and that of their children. I will establish with them an eternal covenant, so that I will not turn away from following them; and [Col. 0748A] I will place fear in their heart, so that they may not depart from me. I will visit them to do them good and to plant them in their own land, in faithfulness and with all my heart and all my soul” (Jer. 31:31–41).

Likewise in the Apocalypse: “And the twenty-four elders sitting upon their thrones in the presence of God fell upon their faces and worshiped God, saying: ‘We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty, who are and who were, because you have taken up your great power and have begun to reign. The nations were enraged, and your wrath came, together with the time for the dead to be judged, and for a reward to be given to your servants the prophets and to the saints who fear your name, small and great, and for those who corrupted the earth to be destroyed’” (Rev. 11:16–18).

Likewise there: “And I saw another angel flying through midheaven, possessing an everlasting Gospel to proclaim to those dwelling upon the earth and [Col. 0748B] to every nation, tribe, language, and people. He said in a loud voice: ‘Fear God and give him honor, because the hour of his judgment has come; and worship him who made heaven and earth and sea and the springs of waters’” (Rev. 14:6–7).

Likewise there: “And I saw what appeared to be a glassy sea mingled with fire, and those who had conquered the beast, together with its image and the number of its name, one hundred and forty-four, standing upon the glassy sea and holding the harps of God. They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: ‘Great and marvelous are your works, Lord God Almighty; righteous and true are your ways, King of the nations. Who will not fear and give honor to your name? For you alone are holy, and all nations will come and worship in your sight, because your righteous acts have been revealed’” (Rev. 15:2–4).

Likewise in Daniel: “There was a man dwelling in Babylon whose name was Joachim, [Col. 0748C] and he took a wife named Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah, who was exceedingly beautiful and feared God. Her parents were righteous, and they instructed their daughter according to the law of Moses” (Dan. 13:1–3).

Likewise in Daniel: “Today we are humbled throughout all the earth because of our sins, and at this time there is no prince, prophet, or leader, no burnt offering, oblation, sacrifice, or incense, and no place in which to sacrifice before you and find mercy from you. But receive us with a humble soul and spirit, as burnt sacrifices of rams and bulls and as many thousands of the fattest lambs. Thus let our sacrifice be made before you today, and let their power be brought to an end, for those who trust in you will not be put to shame. And now we follow you with our whole heart; we fear you and seek your face. Do not hand us over to reproach, [Col. 0748D] 313 but deal with us according to your gentleness, and deliver us according to the abundance of your mercy” (Dan. 3:37, 42).

Likewise there: “And the king rejoiced exceedingly and commanded Daniel to be brought out of the lions’ den; and the lions had done him no harm, because he trusted and believed in his God. Then the king gave orders, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel and cast them into the lions’ den, together with their wives and their children. Before they reached [Col. 0749A] the floor of the den, the lions seized them and crushed all their bones. Then King Darius wrote: ‘To all nations, tribes, and languages within my kingdom: May peace be with you from my presence. I decree and command that all who are in my kingdom shall fear and tremble before the Most High God whom Daniel serves, because he is the living Lord who abides forever; his kingdom will not pass away, and his dominion endures forever. He alone performs signs, wonders, and marvels in heaven and on earth; he delivered Daniel from the lions’ den’” (Dan. 6:24–28).

Likewise in Micah: “With what shall I approach the Lord and take hold of him—in sacrifices, in burnt offerings, in year-old calves? Is the Lord favorably disposed toward an acceptable gift of thousands of fat goats? Or shall I give my first fruits for my impiety, the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul? It has been declared to you, [Col. 0749B] O man, what is good, or what else the Lord requires: only that you perform judgment and righteousness, love mercy, and be prepared to walk with the Lord your God. The voice of the Lord will be invoked in the city, and he will save those who fear his name” (Mic. 6:6–9).

Likewise in Micah: “Shepherd your people with your rod, the sheep of your inheritance, and gather those who dwell apart in the midst of Carmel. They will graze Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old; and as in the days of their departure from the land of Egypt, I will show them wonders. The nations will see and be confounded despite all their strength, and they will place their hands over their mouths. Their ears will become deaf, and they will lick the dust like serpents. Dragging along the earth, they will be troubled and will lick the dust. From within their confinement they will dread the Lord their God and will be afraid because of you. Who is a God like [Col. 0749C] you, who takes away injustice and passes over acts of impiety?” (Mic. 7:14–18).

And in Nahum: “The mountains were shaken by him and the hills trembled; the earth was laid bare before his face, together with all who dwell upon it. Who will endure before his wrath, and who can resist the anger of his spirit? His fury causes principalities to melt away, and the rocks are dissolved by him. The Lord is good to those who wait for him in the day of affliction, and he knows those who fear him” (Nah. 1:5–7).

Likewise in Haggai: “And Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the tribe of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all who remained of the people heard the words of the Lord their God, because the Lord had sent him to them; and the people feared before the face of God” (Hag. 1:12).

Likewise in Malachi: “The covenant was with life and peace, and I gave them fear, that they might fear me before my name” (Mal. [Col. 0749D]2:5). Likewise in Psalm 33: “Fear the Lord, all his saints, for those who fear him suffer no want.” Likewise in Psalm 18: “The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever and ever” [Note: [Col. 0749D] “The fear of the Lord is holy, abiding forever” Cott.].

## CHAPTER XXI.—ONE MUST NOT JUDGE ANOTHER RASHLY

[Col. 0750A]

In the Gospel according to Luke: “Do not judge, lest you be judged; do not condemn, lest you be condemned” (Luke 6:37). On this same matter, to the Romans: “Who are you to judge another’s servant? Before his own master he stands or falls. But he will stand, for God is able to make him stand” (Rom. 14:4). And again: “Therefore you are without excuse [Note: [Col. 0749D] “Inexcusable” Cott.], O every man who judges. For in judging another, you condemn yourself, since you do the very things that you judge. Do you suppose, you who judge those who do evil and yet do the same things, that you yourself will escape the judgment of God?” (Rom. 2:1–3).

Likewise in Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Let him who thinks that he stands take care lest he fall” (1 Cor. 10:12). And again: 314 “If anyone thinks [Note: [Col. 0749D] “Hopes himself” Bod. 2.] that he knows something, he does not yet know [Note: [Col. 0749D] “Does not yet know this” Corb.; “has not yet understood” Cott.] as he ought to know” (1 Cor. 8:2).

[Note: [Col. 0749D]

**CHAPTER XXII.—Forgive us our debts.** See Erasmus’s [Col. 0750D] annotations on the sixth chapter of Matthew.]

## CHAPTER XXII.—WHEN AN INJURY HAS BEEN RECEIVED, IT MUST BE REMITTED AND FORGIVEN

[Col. 0750B]

In the Gospel [Note: [Col. 0749D] “In Matthew’s Gospel: Forgive” Cott.], in the daily prayer: “Forgive [Note: [Col. 0749D] “Release us from” Bod. 2. Corb., and so thereafter.] us our debts, as we too forgive our debtors” (Matt. 6:12). Likewise according to Mark: “And when you stand for prayer, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your sins. But if [Note: [Col. 0749D] “But if you.” These words are absent from Thu.] you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your sins” (Mark 11:25). Likewise there: “With whatever measure you have measured [Note: [Col. 0749D] “You shall have measured” Corb.], it will be measured back to you” (Mark 4:24).

## CHAPTER XXIII.—EVIL MUST NOT BE REPAID IN KIND

In Paul’s Epistle to the Romans: “Repay no one evil for evil.” Likewise there: “Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer [Col. 0750C] evil with good [Note: [Col. 0749D] “Into good” Thu. Corb. Cott.]” (Rom. 12:17, 21).

On this same matter, in the Apocalypse: “And he said to me: ‘Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book, because the time is already near. Let those who persist in doing harm continue to do harm, and let him who is in filth become filthier still; but let the righteous still do more righteous things [Note: [Col. 0750D] “The righteous will do more righteous things” Bod. 1. Cott.], and likewise the holy still holier things. Behold, I am coming quickly, and my reward is with me, to repay each one according to his deeds [Note: [Col. 0750D] “His works” Cott.]’” (Rev. 22:10).

## CHAPTER XXIV.—THAT ONE CANNOT COME TO THE FATHER [Note: [Col. 0750D] “Come to the Father” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4.] EXCEPT THROUGH HIS SON JESUS CHRIST [Note: [Col. 0750D] “Except through Christ” Bod. 1, 2. Thu. Corb.; “except through the Lord” Cott.]

In the Gospel according to John: “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me” (John 14:6). Likewise there: “I am the door [Note: [Col. 0750D] “I am the gate” Bod. 1, 3. Cott.]. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved” (John 10:9).

## CHAPTER XXV.—THAT NO ONE CAN REACH THE KINGDOM OF GOD UNLESS [Note: [Col. 0750D] “Unless one has been baptized” Cott.] HE HAS BEEN BAPTIZED AND BORN AGAIN

[Col. 0750D]

In the Gospel according to John: “Unless one has been born again [Note: [Col. 0750D] “Has been born” Bod. 3, 4.] of water and the Spirit [Note: [Col. 0750D] “And the Holy Spirit” Lam. Lin. NC. 1.], he cannot enter the kingdom [Col. 0751A] of God. For that which is born of flesh is flesh, and that which is born of spirit is spirit” (John 3:5). Likewise there: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in you” (John 6:54).

## CHAPTER XXVI.—THAT IT IS OF LITTLE AVAIL TO BE BAPTIZED AND RECEIVE THE EUCHARIST UNLESS ONE ADVANCES BY DEEDS AND ACTION

In Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all indeed run, yet one receives the prize [Note: [Col. 0751C] “Receives the *brabeion* [prize]” Bod. 3.]? Run in such a way [Note: [Col. 0751C] “Run, all of you” Thu.] that you may obtain it [Note: [Col. 0751C] “That you may all lay hold of it” Cott.]. They do so to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible one [Note: [Col. 0751C] “But we an incorruptible crown” Cott.]” (1 Cor. 9:24).

In the Gospel according to Matthew: “Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and cast into the fire” (Matt. 3:10). Likewise there: “Many will say to me on that day: ‘Lord, Lord, did we not [Col. 0751B] prophesy in your name, and in your name drive out demons [Note: [Col. 0751C] “We drove out demons” Cott. Voss. 3.], and in your name perform great miracles [Note: [Col. 0751D] “Many miracles” Bod. 1. Cott.]?’ And then I will say to them: ‘I never knew [Note: [Col. 0751D] “Recognized” Cott.] you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity’” (Matt. 7:22). Likewise there: “Let [Note: [Col. 0751D] “Thus let” Cott.] your light shine before men, so that they may see your good works and glorify [Note: [Col. 0751D] “And magnify” Bod. 2.] your Father who is in heaven” (Matt. 5:16). Likewise Paul to the Philippians: “Shine like [Note: [Col. 0751D] “To the Philippians: Among whom you shine like” Cott.] lights in the world” (Phil. 2:15).

## CHAPTER XXVII.—THAT EVEN ONE WHO HAS BEEN BAPTIZED LOSES THE GRACE HE HAS RECEIVED UNLESS HE PRESERVES INNOCENCE

In the Gospel according to John: “Behold, you have been made well; now sin no more, lest something worse happen to you [Note: [Col. 0751D] “Lest something worse befall you” Bod. 1. Voss. 3.]” (John 5:14). Likewise in Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Do you not know [Col. 0751C] that you are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone [Note: [Col. 0751D] “But if anyone” Cott.] violates God’s temple, God will destroy [Note: [Col. 0751D] “Has violated it, will violate him” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Cor.] him” (1 Cor. 3:16). On this same matter, in Chronicles: “God is with you while you are with him. If you forsake him, he will forsake you” (2 Chron. 15:2).

## CHAPTER XXVIII.—THAT HE WHO SINS AGAINST GOD CANNOT BE FORGIVEN IN THE CHURCH

In the Gospel according to Matthew: “Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come” (Matt. 12:32). Likewise [Col. 0752A] according to Mark: “All sins and blasphemies will be forgiven the children of men. But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven [Note: [Col. 0751D] “But whoever blasphemes does not have forgiveness” Thu. Corb. Voss. 3; “will not have forgiveness” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lam. Lin. NC. 1; “forgiveness” Cott.], but will be guilty of an eternal sin” (Mark 3:29).

On this same matter, in the First Book of Kingdoms: “If in committing an offense 315 a man sins [Note: [Col. 0752C] “If in committing an offense he has sinned” Corb. Thu.; “if in committing an offense he has offended” Cott.] against a man, they will pray [Note: [Col. 0752C] “A priest will pray” NC. 2; “the righteous will pray” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] to the Lord for him [Note: [Col. 0752C] “To the Lord” Bod.]. But if a man sins against God, who will pray for him?” (1 Sam. 2:25).

[Note: [Col. 0751D]

**CHAPTER XXIX.—Likewise in Baruch.** This passage and those that follow down to the end of the chapter were added from the two manuscripts mentioned shortly before. (These passages seem all the more carefully to deserve preservation because the words attributed here to the prophet Baruch, all that survive of them, are found neither in the original texts of Holy Scripture nor in any translation, whether Greek or Latin. EDD.) [Col. 0752D]]

## CHAPTER XXIX.—ON THE HATRED OF THE NAME FORETOLD BEFOREHAND

In the Gospel according to Luke: “And you will be hated by all men because of my name” (Luke 21:17). Likewise according to John: “If the world hates you, know that it hated me first [Note: [Col. 0752D] “Me first” Cott.; “hates me who came before” Bod. 1. Voss. 3.]. If you belonged to the world, the world would love what was its own; but because you do not belong to the world, and I chose you out of the world, the world therefore hates you. Remember [Col. 0752B] the word that [Note: [Col. 0752D] “The words that” Thu.; “the words that I spoke” Corb.] I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master’ [Note: [Col. 0752D] “Than his master, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1. Cott.]. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also” (John 15:18).

Likewise in Baruch: “For the time will come when you, and those who come after you, will seek me in order to hear the word of wisdom and understanding, and you will not find it. The nations will desire to see a wise man, but it will not be granted to them—not because the wisdom of this earthly age will be absent or fail, nor because the word of the law will be absent from the age. For wisdom will be found among a few who are watchful, silent, and quietly converse among themselves, because some will shudder at them and fear them as evil men. Others will not believe the word of the law of the Most High. Others, astonished in speech, will not believe and yet will believe; and, contradicting, they will be adversaries who hinder the spirit of truth. Others will be wise according to the spirit of error and will proclaim their pronouncements as the decrees of the Most High and Mighty One. [Col. 0752C] Others will be ‘personal’ in faith [*personales fidei*; reading uncertain]. Others will be receptive and strong in the faith of the Most High, and hateful to what is alien [reading uncertain].”

## CHAPTER XXX.—THAT WHAT ONE HAS VOWED TO GOD MUST QUICKLY BE PAID

In Solomon: “When you have made a vow to God, do not delay in paying it” (Eccl. 5:3). On this same matter, in Deuteronomy [Note: [Col. 0752D] “Likewise in Deuteronomy” Imp.]: “If you make a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay in paying it, because the Lord your God will surely require it from you, and it will count as sin [Note: [Col. 0752D] “As sin in you” NC. 1. Bod. 2; “If you do not observe the things that proceed from your lips” Voss. 3.]. You shall observe the things that proceed from your lips and make [Note: [Col. 0752D] “And you shall make a gift to the Lord your God” Cott. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] the gift that you promised with your mouth [Note: [Col. 0752D] “From your mouth” Cott.]” (Deut. 23:21).

On this same matter, in Psalm 49: “Offer [Note: [Col. 0752D] “Sacrifice” Cott.] to God a sacrifice of praise, [Col. 0753A] and pay your vows to the Most High. Call upon me in the day of affliction [Note: [Col. 0753C] “Of tribulation” Cott.], and I will rescue you [Note: [Col. 0753C] “And I will deliver you” Cott.], and you will glorify me [Note: [Col. 0753C] “Magnify me” Cott.].”

On this same matter, in the Acts of the Apostles: “Why has [Note: [Col. 0753C] “Why has Satan” Thu. Cott.] Satan filled your heart [Note: [Col. 0753C] “For you to lie before the Holy Spirit” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Benev. Ver.] so that you would lie to the Holy Spirit, when the land was [Note: [Col. 0753D] Thus Bod. 1. Cott. Voss. 3. The printed editions read: “When the land was in your.” Oxon.: “When the land had been sold, it was in your power.”] in your power? You have not lied to men, but to God” (Acts 5:3). Likewise in Jeremiah: “Cursed [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Cursed is the man” Lam. Bod. 1. NC. 1. Cott.] is he who performs the works of God negligently” (Jer. 48:10).

## CHAPTER XXXI.—THAT HE WHO HAS NOT BELIEVED HAS ALREADY BEEN JUDGED

In the Gospel according to John: “He who has not believed has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of God’s only [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Only-begotten” Cott.] Son. And this is the judgment: light came into the world, and men loved [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Loved darkness more” Bod. 2, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott.] darkness more than light” (John 3:18). On this same matter, in the Psalm: “Therefore the impious will not rise [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Will not stand” Bod. 1. Voss. 3; “therefore will not rise” Cott.] in judgment, nor sinners [Col. 0753B] in the council of the righteous.”

## CHAPTER XXXII.—ON THE GOOD OF VIRGINITY AND CONTINENCE
In Genesis: “Multiplying, I will multiply your sorrows and your groanings [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Filling, I will fill your griefs, your sighing, and in sorrow you shall bear your children” Cott.]; and in sorrow you shall bear sons, and your turning shall be toward your husband [Note: [Col. 0753D] “And your turning” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Voss. 3.], and he shall rule over you” (Gen. III, 16).

On this same matter, in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs [Note: [Col. 0753D] “So also there are eunuchs” Bod. 1. “Eunuchs” Cott.] who have castrated themselves for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let him who can accept it accept it” (Matt. XIX, 11).

Likewise, according to Luke: “The children of this age beget and are begotten. But those who have been deemed worthy of that age [Col. 0753C] and of the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Nor take wives” Bod. 1.]. For neither will they begin to die. For they are equal to the angels of God, since they are children of the resurrection” (Luke XX, 34). “Moreover, Moses signifies that the dead rise when he says at the bush [Note: [Col. 0753D] “At the bush I saw the Lord, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob” Bod. 1, 4. Corb.]: ‘The Lord, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, is not the God of the dead, but of the living’” (Exod. III, 6). “For all those people live” (Luke XX, 38). [Note: [Col. 0753D] “But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read in the book of Moses?” Cott.]

Likewise, in Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “It is good for a man not to touch a woman [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Not to touch a woman” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1. Cott.]. But because of fornication [Note: [Col. 0753D] “Because of fornications” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2.], 316 let each man have his own wife, and [Col. 0754A] let each woman have her own husband. Let the husband render what is due to his wife, and the wife likewise to her husband. The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise, the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does [Note: [Col. 0754C] “But the woman” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 2, 3, 4.]. Do not deprive one another except by agreement [Note: [Col. 0754C] “By agreement, and for a time” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Lin. NC. 1.], for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer; and then return again [Note: [Col. 0754C] “Return to it” Lam. NC. 1. Lin. “Turn back” Corb.] to the same practice, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control. I say this by way of permission [Note: [Col. 0754C] “By way of counsel” Bod. 3.], not by way of command [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Not by way of an order” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 4. NC. 1. Thu. Benev. Ver. “By way of indulgence, and not by way of command” Cott.]. Yet I wish all people to be as I am. But each has his own gift from God [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Has a *charisma* from God” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Voss. 3. Lin. NC. 1.], one in this way, another in that” (I Cor. VII, 1).

Likewise there: “The unmarried man thinks about the things of the Lord—how he may please God. But the man who has contracted marriage thinks about the things of this world—how he may please his wife [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Please God. But he who is with a wife thinks about the things of this world—how he may please his wife; and they are divided: the woman” Cott. Ver. “Please his wife; and the unmarried virgin” Lam. Cott. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]. So too the woman and the unmarried virgin think about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy [Col. 0754B] [Note: [Col. 0754D] “That she may be holy in body” Bod. 1, 3.] both in body and in spirit. But she who has married thinks about the things of this world—how she may please her husband” (Ibid. 32).

Likewise in Exodus, when the Lord had commanded Moses to sanctify the people for the third day, he sanctified them and added [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Added, saying” Lam. Lin. Bod. 1, 2. NC. 1. Voss. 3.]: “Be ready: for three days [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Within three days” Cott.] you shall not approach women [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Keep away from women” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.]” (Exod. XIX, 15).

Likewise, in the First Book of Kings: “And the priest answered David and said: ‘There are no common loaves at hand with me, except one holy loaf [Note: [Col. 0754D] “I do not have loaves in abundance, except one loaf.”]. If the young men have been kept from a woman [Note: [Col. 0754D] “If the young men have been guarded” Cott.], they may eat’” (I Kings XXI, 4).

Likewise, in the Apocalypse: “These are they who have not defiled themselves with women. For they have remained virgins. These are they who follow the Lamb wherever he goes [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Wherever he goes” Bod. 3, 4. Cott. Voss. 4.]” (Apoc. XIV, 4).

## CHAPTER XXXIII.—THAT THE FATHER JUDGES NOTHING, BUT THE SON; AND THAT THE FATHER IS NOT HONORED BY HIM BY WHOM THE SON IS NOT HONORED

[Col. 0754C]

In the Gospel according to John: “The Father judges nothing, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father [Note: [Col. 0754D] “The Father who sent him” Lam. NC. 1. Voss. 3.]. He who does not honor [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Honors” Cott.] the Son does not honor the Father who sent him” (John V, 22).

Likewise, in Psalm LXXI: “O God, give your judgment to the king, and your justice to the king’s son, that he may judge your people [Note: [Col. 0754D] “Your peoples” Bod. 4. Cott.] in justice.”

Likewise, in Genesis: “And the Lord rained sulfur and fire from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord” (Gen. XIX, 24).

## CHAPTER XXXIV.—THAT A BELIEVER OUGHT NOT TO LIVE LIKE A GENTILE [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Must not” Corb.]

[Col. 0755A]

In Jeremiah: “Thus says the Lord: You shall not walk according to the way of the Gentiles [Note: [Col. 0755D] “The ways of the nations” Bod. 2, 4.]” (Jer. VII).

On this same matter—that one ought to separate oneself from the Gentiles, lest one become an associate in their guilt and a participant in their plague [Note: [Col. 0755D] “And become a participant in their plague, in the Apocalypse” Bod. 1, 2, 4.]—in the Apocalypse: “And I heard another voice from heaven saying: ‘Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her offenses and lest you be struck by her plagues; for her offenses have reached as far as heaven, and the Lord God has remembered her iniquities [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Her iniquity” Bod. 1, 3, 4.]. Therefore he has repaid [Note: [Col. 0755D] “He will repay her double” Cott.] her double, and in the cup in which she mixed, a double portion has been mixed back for her [Note: [Col. 0755D] “He has mixed back double” Bod. 1.]; and to the extent that she glorified herself and possessed delights, to that same extent [Note: [Col. 0755D] “So much was given” Bod. 2. “Is given” Bod. 1, 2, 3.] both torment and mourning have been given to her, because she says in her heart: “I am a queen, and I cannot be a widow, nor shall I see mourning.” [Col. 0755B] Therefore in one hour her plagues shall come [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Shall come” [singular] Bod. 1.]: death, mourning, and famine; and she shall be burned with fire, because mighty is the Lord God who will judge her. And the kings of the earth who committed fornication with her and lived amid her offenses [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Delights” Oxon.] shall weep and beat their breasts over her’” (Apoc. XVIII, 14).

Likewise, in Isaiah: “Come out from their midst, you who carry the vessels [Note: [Col. 0755D] “You who bear the vessels” Cott.] of the Lord” (Isa. LII, 11).

## CHAPTER XXXV.—THAT GOD IS PATIENT FOR THIS PURPOSE: THAT WE MAY REPENT OF OUR SIN AND BE REFORMED

In Solomon, in Ecclesiasticus: “Do not say, ‘I have sinned, and what sorrowful thing has happened to me [Note: [Col. 0755D] “‘And what has happened to me?’—so Corb. ‘Sorrow’ Bod. 2.]?’ For the Most High is a patient requiter [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Patient, and one who will repay” Cott. “The Most High and most patient” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.]” (Ecclus. V, 4).

Likewise, Paul to the Romans: “Or do you perhaps despise the riches of his goodness and patience [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Or the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience” Cott.], not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to [Col. 0755C] repentance? But according to your hardness and impenitent heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation of God’s just judgment, who will repay each person according to his works” (Rom. II, 4).

## 317 CHAPTER XXXVI.—THAT A WOMAN OUGHT NOT TO ADORN HERSELF IN A WORLDLY MANNER

In the Apocalypse: “And one of the seven angels who had the bowls came and approached me, saying: ‘Come, I will show you the condemnation of the great prostitute who sits upon many waters, with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication.’ And I saw a woman sitting upon a beast. And [Col. 0756A] that woman was clothed in a purple [Note: [Col. 0755D] “In a purple and scarlet cloak” Corb.] and scarlet cloak and was adorned with gold, precious stones, and pearls, holding in her hand a golden cup full of abominations, impurity, and the fornication of the whole earth” (Apoc. XVII, 1).

Likewise, to Timothy [Note: [Col. 0755D] “Likewise, Paul to Timothy” Lam. Bod. 2. Lin. NC. 1.]: “Let your women [Note: [Col. 0755D] “‘Let the women,’ he says” Bod. 2.] array themselves with modesty and chastity, not with braided hair, nor gold [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Gold, nor silver” Cott.], nor pearls [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Nor with precious pearls” Bod. 2.], or costly clothing, but, as befits women professing chastity, through good conduct” (I Tim. II, 9).

On this same matter, in Peter’s Epistle to the people of Pontus: “Let a woman’s adornment consist not in the outward adornment of gold or clothing, but in the adornment of the heart” (I Pet. III, 3).

Likewise, in Genesis: “Tamar covered herself with a cloak and adorned herself; and when Judah saw her, she appeared to him to be a prostitute” (Gen. XXXVIII, 14).

[Note: [Col. 0755D]

**CHAPTER XXXVII.—Meddling in the affairs of others.** Saint Augustine also reads it thus in chapter 10 of his *Unfinished Exposition of Paul’s Epistle* [Col. 0756D] *to the Romans*.]

## CHAPTER XXXVII.—THAT A BELIEVER OUGHT NOT [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Must not” Corb.] TO BE PUNISHED FOR OTHER OFFENSES, BUT ONLY FOR THE NAME

[Col. 0756B]

In Peter’s Epistle to the people of Pontus: “Let none of you suffer as a thief or murderer [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Be punished for acting as a murderer” Cott.], or as an evildoer, or as one who meddles in the affairs of others [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Be punished for meddling in the affairs of others” Bod. 2. “A spy upon another” Tert.], but as a Christian” (I Pet. IV, 15).

## CHAPTER XXXVIII.—THAT A SERVANT OF GOD OUGHT TO BE INNOCENT, LEST HE INCUR SECULAR PUNISHMENT

In Paul’s Epistle to the Romans: “Do you wish not to fear the authority? Do good, and you will have praise from it [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Praise from it” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 4.]” (Rom. XIII, 3).

## CHAPTER XXXIX.—THAT IN CHRIST AN EXAMPLE OF HOW TO LIVE HAS BEEN GIVEN TO US

[Col. 0756C]

In Peter’s Epistle to the people of Pontus: “For Christ suffered for us [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Christ suffered for you” Thu. Corb. Cott.], leaving you [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Leaving an example” Bod. 1, 3.] an example, so that you might follow his footsteps: he committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth; when he was cursed, he did not curse in return [Note: [Col. 0756D] “He did not curse” Bod. 2.]; when he suffered, he did not threaten [Note: [Col. 0756D] “He did not make threats” Corb.], but delivered himself to the one who judged [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Who judged him” Bod. 3.] unjustly” (I Pet. II, 21).

Likewise, Paul to the Philippians: “He who, established in the form of God [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Although he had been established in the form of God” Cott.], did not consider being equal to God an act of robbery, but emptied himself [Note: [Col. 0756D] “But himself” Bod. 1, 4. Cott. “Emptied” Thu. Corb.], taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness [Note: [Col. 0756D] “In the likeness” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Corb. Thu. “Of men” Bod. 2.] of a human being, and found in appearance [Note: [Col. 0756D] “Found in outward form” Cott.] as a man. He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore God also [Col. 0757A] exalted him and gave him a name above every name [Note: [Col. 0757C] “The name that is above” Bod. 3. Thu. Cott.], so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend [Note: [Col. 0757C] “Every knee shall bend” Cott. “Let every knee bend” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu.]—of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—and every tongue should confess [Note: [Col. 0757C] “Confess to God” Lam. NC. 1. Cott.] that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father” (Phil. II, 6–11).

On this same matter, in the Gospel according to John: “If I, your Teacher and Lord, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash the feet of others [Note: [Col. 0757C] “One another’s feet” Cott.]. For I have given you an example, so that, just as I have done [Note: [Col. 0757D] “I have done for you” Cott.], you also may do for others [Note: [Col. 0757D] “You also may do” Bod. 1. Voss. 3.]” (John XIII, 14).

## CHAPTER XL.—THAT ONE MUST NOT ACT BOASTFULLY OR NOISILY

In the Gospel according to Matthew: “Let your left hand [Note: [Col. 0757D] “What your left hand” Lam. NC. 1. Thu.] not know what your right hand is doing, so that your almsgiving may be [Note: [Col. 0757D] “In secret” Bod. 2. Cott. Lam. Lin. Bod. 2. NC. 1. Cott. Voss. 4.] in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, [Col. 0757B] will repay you.”

Likewise there: “When you give alms, do not sound a trumpet [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Do not blow a trumpet” Lin. NC. 2. “Make a commotion” Bod. 3. Benev. Ver. Voss. 4.] before you, as the hypocrites do in the streets and synagogues, so that they may be glorified [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Honored” Cott.] by men. Amen, I say to you, they have completed [Note: [Col. 0757D] “They have reckoned” Lam. Lin. Thu. NC. 1. Corb. Bod. 2, 4. “They have received” NC. 2. Cott. “They have received” Bod. 1. Voss. 3. “They have been compensated for” Benev. Ver.] their reward” (Matt. VI, 3, 2).

## CHAPTER XLI.—THAT ONE MUST NOT SPEAK FOOLISHLY OR BUFFOONISHLY

In Paul’s Epistle to the Ephesians: “Foolish talk [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Much talking” Bod. 3.] and buffoonery, which are not pertinent to the matter, must not even be named among you” (Eph. V, 4).

## CHAPTER XLII.—THAT FAITH IS OF BENEFIT IN EVERY RESPECT [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Faith alone” Voss. 3, 4. NC. 2. “That faith is of benefit” Thu.], AND THAT WE CAN DO AS MUCH AS WE BELIEVE

In Genesis: “And Abraham believed God, and it [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Was reckoned” Cott.] was accounted to him as righteousness [Note: [Col. 0757D] “For righteousness” Cott.]” (Gen. XV, 6).

Likewise, in [Col. 0757C] Isaiah: “And if you do not believe, neither will you understand” (Isa. VII, 9).

Likewise, in the Gospel according to Matthew: “O you of little faith, why did you doubt [Note: [Col. 0757D] “For what reason did you doubt?” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2, 4. Thu. Corb.]?” (Matt. XIV, 31).

Likewise there: “If you have faith [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Faith like” Bod. 1, 2.] like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Pass from here to there,’ and it will pass; and nothing 318 will be impossible for you” (Matt. XVII, 19).

Likewise, according to Mark: “Whatever things you pray for and ask, believe that you will receive them, and they will be yours” (Mark XI, 24).

Likewise there: “All things are possible [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Are possible” Corb. “All things are possible to believers” Cott.] to the one who believes” (Mark IX, 22).

In Habakkuk: “But the righteous person lives by my faith [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Will live by faith” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3. “But my righteous one, by faith” Cott.]” (Hab. II, 4).

Likewise, [Col. 0758A] in Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, believing in God, were delivered [Note: [Col. 0757D] “Believing, were delivered” Bod. 1, 2, 4.] from the flame of fire (Dan. III, 24, 52).

## CHAPTER XLIII.—THAT HE WHO HAS TRULY BELIEVED CAN OBTAIN IT AT ONCE [Note: [Col. 0758C] “Obtain baptism” Lam. NC. 1.]

In the Acts of the Apostles: “‘Look, here is water; what prevents me from being baptized [Note: [Col. 0758C] “What prevents me from being immersed” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 4. Thu. Corb. Cott. Voss. 1.]?’ Then Philip said [Note: [Col. 0758C] “Said to him” Corb.]: ‘If you believe with your whole heart [Note: [Col. 0758C] “In your whole heart” Bod. 1. Cott.], it is permitted’” (Acts VIII, 36).

## CHAPTER XLIV.—THAT BELIEVERS WHO HAVE DISPUTES AMONG THEMSELVES OUGHT NOT TO RESORT TO A GENTILE JUDGE

In Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Does any of you who has a case against another dare to have it adjudicated [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Does anyone among you dare to have a case adjudicated?” Cott.] before the unrighteous, and not before the saints? [Note: [Col. 0758D] “The saints? Do you not know” Bod. 1.] Or do you not know that the saints will judge this world [Note: [Col. 0758D] “The saints will judge the world” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Thu. Corb. Bod. 1, 2, 4. “Concerning this world” Cott. Voss. 3.]?”

And [Col. 0758B] again: “It is already altogether an offense [Note: [Col. 0758D] “So great an offense” Cott.] among you that you have lawsuits with one another [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Have with one another” Bod. 1. Cott.]. Why do you not rather suffer injury [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Suffer fraud” Lam. Bod. 1. NC. 1. “Endure it” NC. 2. “Receive injury” Bod. 1.]? Or why are you not rather defrauded? But you inflict injury and commit fraud, and this [Note: [Col. 0758D] “And this against brothers” Bod. 4.] against brothers! Do you not know [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Or do you not know” Thu. Corb.] that the unrighteous will not obtain the kingdom of God [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Will not possess” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.]?” (I Cor. VI, 1–9).

## CHAPTER XLV.—THAT HOPE CONCERNS FUTURE THINGS, AND THAT OUR FAITH MUST THEREFORE BE PATIENT REGARDING [Note: [Col. 0758D] “And therefore the believer regarding” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] THE THINGS THAT HAVE BEEN PROMISED

In Paul’s Epistle to the Romans: “We have been saved in hope. But hope that is seen is not hope. For why does anyone hope for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we hope with patience [Note: [Col. 0758D] “We hope with patience” Lam. Bod. 1. NC. 2. “We wait” Bod. 1. Voss. 3. Oxon.]” (Rom. VIII, 24).

## CHAPTER XLVI.—THAT A WOMAN OUGHT TO KEEP SILENT IN CHURCH

[Col. 0758C]

In Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Let women [Note: [Col. 0758D] “A woman” Corb. “Let your women” Lam. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Cott. NC. 1. Voss. 3. “Ought to keep silent in church” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] keep silent in church. But if they wish to say anything [Note: [Col. 0758D] “But if they wish to learn anything” NC. 2. “But if there are some women” Lin.], let them ask their own husbands at home” (I Cor. XIV, 34).

Likewise, to Timothy: “Let a woman learn in silence, with all subjection [Note: [Col. 0758D] “Humility” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb. “Submission” Bod. 1, 4. Thu. “With all modesty” Cott.]. But I do not permit a woman to teach or to be placed over [Note: [Col. 0758D] “To exercise dominion over” Cott.] a man, but to remain in silence. For Adam was formed first, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived” (I Tim. II, 11–14).

## CHAPTER XLVII.—THAT IT IS THROUGH OUR OWN OFFENSE AND DESERT THAT WE SUFFER AND DO NOT EXPERIENCE GOD’S AID IN ALL THINGS

[Col. 0759A]

In Hosea: “Hear the word of the Lord, children of Israel, because the Lord has a judgment [Note: [Col. 0759D] “A judgment comes from the Lord” Lam. Bod. 2. “Of the Lord” Voss. 1.] against the inhabitants of the land, [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Of the land, because” Bod. 4.] because neither mercy, nor truth, nor knowledge of God is upon the land, but cursing, lying, murder, theft, and adultery have spread over the land. They heap blood upon blood. Therefore the land shall mourn with all its inhabitants, with the beasts of the field, with the serpents of the earth, and with the birds of heaven; and the fish of the sea shall perish, so that no one may judge [Note: [Col. 0759D] “So that there may be no one to judge.”], no one [Note: [Col. 0759D] “No one who” Lin.] may refute” (Hos. IV, 1–4).

On this same matter, in Isaiah: “Surely the Lord’s hand is not powerless [Note: [Col. 0759D] “To save” Lam. NC. 1, 2. Corb.] to save, nor has he made his ear heavy [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Made his ears heavy” Thu. Corb.] so that he cannot hear. But your sins separate you from God, and because of your offenses [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Because of your sins” Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 3, 4.] [Col. 0759B] he has turned his face away from you, so as not to have mercy. For your hands are stained with blood [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Are full of blood” Bod. 3. Voss. 4.], and your fingers with sins. Your lips have spoken wickedness, and your tongue meditates injustice. No one speaks truth, nor is there true judgment. They trust in vanities and speak empty things; they conceive [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Conceive deceit” NC. 2.] sorrow and give birth to [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Give birth to iniquity” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Corb.] wickedness” (Isa. LIX, 1–4).

Likewise, in Zephaniah: “‘Let everything utterly perish from the face of the earth,’ says the Lord. ‘Let man perish, and let the cattle perish, the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea; and I will remove the wicked from the face of the earth’” (Zeph. I, 2).

## CHAPTER XLVIII.—THAT MONEY MUST NOT BE LENT AT INTEREST

In Psalm XIII: “He who has not lent his money at interest [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Given at usury” Cott. “Given on interest” Bod. 1. Thu. Corb.], and has not accepted gifts against the innocent. He who has done these things [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Does these things” Corb.] shall not be moved [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Shall not be destroyed” Lam. Bod. 2. NC. 1.] forever.”

Likewise, [Col. 0759C] in Ezekiel: “But the man who is righteous will not oppress another, and will return the debtor’s pledge [Note: [Col. 0759D] “And will repay the debt” Corb. “Will return it to the debtor” Cott.], and will not commit robbery [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Let him not seize plunder” Bod. 1, 3, 4. Thu.], and will give his bread to the hungry, and will cover the naked, and will not lend his money at interest” (Ezek. XVIII, 7, 8).

Likewise, in Deuteronomy: “You shall not lend to your brother at interest—interest on money [Note: [Col. 0759D] “Interest” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. “At interest” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Lin. “Interest” Bod. 1. Lin. Thu. “Interest on money” Cott. Voss. 3, 4.] or interest on food” (Deut. XXIII, 20).

## 319 CHAPTER XLIX.—THAT EVEN ENEMIES MUST BE LOVED

In the Gospel according to Luke: “If you love those who love you, what favor is there for you? For even sinners love those who love them [Note: [Col. 0759D] “For sinners love those who love them” Lam. Lin. NC. 1, 2. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.]” (Luke VI, 32).

Likewise, according to Matthew: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father who is in [Col. 0760A] heaven, who causes his sun [Note: [Col. 0760D] “His sun” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Voss. 3. “The sun to rise” Oxon.] to rise upon the good and the evil, and rains upon the righteous and the unrighteous” (Matt. V, 44, 45).

## CHAPTER L.—THAT THE SACRAMENT OF FAITH MUST NOT BE PROFANED

In Solomon, in Proverbs [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Solomon, in the Parables” Oxon. And so always where the others read “Solomon” and “Proverbs.”]: “Do not say anything in the ears of the foolish, lest, when he hears it, he mock your judicious words” (Prov. XXIII, 9).

Likewise, in the Gospel according to Matthew: “Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Lest they trample them underfoot” Cott. “Trample them” NC. 2. Bod. 2.] and then turn and crush you” (Matt. VII, 6).

## CHAPTER LI.—THAT NO ONE OUGHT TO EXALT HIMSELF IN HIS WORK

In Solomon, in Ecclesiasticus: “Do not exalt yourself [Col. 0760B] in performing your work” (Ecclus. X, 29).

Likewise, in the Gospel according to Luke: “Which of you, having a servant who is plowing or tending sheep, says to him immediately when he comes [Note: [Col. 0760D] “A shepherd coming” Lam. Corb. NC. 1.] from the field, ‘Come over and recline at table [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Come over and recline” Corb.]’? Does he not instead say to him, ‘Prepare something for me to eat [Note: [Col. 0760D] “So that I may eat” Corb.], gird yourself, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk; and afterward you shall eat and drink’? Does he thank that servant [Note: [Col. 0760D] “When you have done” Thu.] because he did what was commanded him? So also you, when you have completed [Note: [Col. 0760D] “That servant” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2.] the things commanded you, say: ‘We are superfluous servants [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Unprofitable servants” Thu. Corb.]; we have done what we had [Note: [Col. 0760D] “What we were obliged to do” Bod. 1, 2, 4. Cott.] to do’” (Luke XVII, 7–10).

## CHAPTER LII.—THAT THE FREEDOM TO BELIEVE OR NOT TO BELIEVE IS PLACED IN OUR CHOICE

In Deuteronomy: “Behold, I have set before your face life and death, good and evil. Choose life for yourself, [Col. 0760C] that you may live [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Choose life, that you may live” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb.]” (Deut. XXX, 19).

Likewise, in Isaiah: “And if you are willing and listen to me, you shall eat the good things of the land [Note: [Col. 0760D] “You shall eat the things of the land” Cott.]. But if you are unwilling and do not listen to me, the sword shall consume you. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things” (Isa. I, 19).

Likewise, in the Gospel according to Luke: “The kingdom of God [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Behold, the kingdom of God” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Cott.] is within you” (Luke XVII, 21).

## CHAPTER LIII.—THAT GOD’S SECRETS CANNOT BE FULLY PERCEIVED, AND THAT OUR FAITH MUST THEREFORE BE SIMPLE

In Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Paul, in the First Epistle to the Corinthians” Corb.]: “Now we see through a mirror, in a riddle [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Through riddles” Lin.], but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Then I shall know” Bod. 1.] just as I also am known [Note: [Col. 0760D] “Just as I am known” Cott.]” (I Cor. XIII, 12).

Likewise, in Solomon, in Wisdom: “And seek him in simplicity [Col. 0761A] of heart [Note: [Col. 0761C] “Seek God” Thu. Voss. 4. “The Lord” Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Lam. Lin. NC. 2.]” (Wis. I, 1).

Likewise, in the same author: “He who walks simply walks confidently” (Prov. X, 9).

Likewise, in the same author: “Do not seek things higher than yourself, and do not investigate things stronger than yourself” (Ecclus. III, 22).

Likewise, in Solomon: “Do not be excessively righteous [Note: [Col. 0761C] “Excessively wise” Lin. “Excessively wise in your own estimation” Cott.], and do not reason more than is fitting [Note: [Col. 0761C] “Than is necessary” Lam. NC. 1. Bod. 2. Thu. Corb.]” (Eccles. VII, 17).

Likewise, in Isaiah: “Woe to those who are clever in their own estimation” (Isa. III, 9).

Likewise, in Maccabees: “Daniel, in his simplicity, was delivered from the mouths of the lions” (I Macc. II, 60).

Likewise, in Paul’s Epistle to the Romans [Note: [Col. 0761C] “Paul to the Romans” Corb.]: “O depth of the riches of God’s wisdom and knowledge! How incomprehensible [Note: [Col. 0761D] “How inscrutable” Lam. Lin. NC. 1. Bod. 1, 2, 3, 4. Thu. Corb. Voss. 3.] are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways! For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor? Or who has first given to him, and it shall be repaid to him? For from him, and through him, and [Col. 0761B] in him are all things; to him be glory forever and ever” (Rom. XI, 33–36).

Likewise, to Timothy: “Avoid foolish and ignorant questions, knowing that they generate quarrels. But a servant of God ought not to quarrel, but to be gentle toward all” (II Tim. II, 23, 24).
