The right of communion is received through the laying on of hands by the bishop and clergy, IV, 251. The order for attaining the right of communion, 252, 254, 255. The salutary remedies of delay, 306. The ruinous remedies of hastened communion, ibid., 310. Communion is not to be granted rashly, III, 779. Communion is granted to the unwary, 478. It ought not to be given before its time, 252. Those who give the Lord’s holy thing to dogs are censured, 295. Rash haste in obtaining peace is censured, 258, 259, 261, 295, 297, 301. The fruit of communion, III, 1023. *Communio* used for *communicatio*.—An actor must not be admitted to communion, 362. Those who granted peace to adulterers did not break communion with those who did not grant it, III, 793. Because of differing customs, there was never a departure from the peace and unity of the Church, III, 1159. Cyprian [Col. 1199] imposes no law upon anyone in the baptismal controversy, 410; III, 1050, 1125, 1147, 1151. The people are not immune from the contagion of guilt when they communicate with a sinful and lawfully deposed priest, III, 1169. Communion under one kind, 486. Unworthy communions punished by miracles, 485. See EUCHARIST. The joining together of the ecclesiastical body, III, 790. Christ’s companions, 802. Golden fetters, 460.

Councils before Cyprian, 398, 411; III, 1112. A council after the persecution had subsided, III, 767. Frequently held at Carthage, III, 811. Bishops customarily assemble at Carthage after Easter, IV, 348. Cyprian reads petitions concerning the lapsed at the council, 345. The cases of individuals were examined at the Council of Carthage, III, 766. Deliberation in councils with bishops, presbyters, deacons, and confessors, while the laity stood by, 258, 261, 287, 312. “It has pleased us, at the prompting of the Holy Spirit,” III, 860. The council on the Ides of May, III, 810. The council concerning the granting of peace to the lapsed, 347. Cyprian, together with his colleagues, replies to Rogatianus, 394. Together with his colleagues and fellow presbyters, he replies to the Church of Furni, 397. The first Council of Carthage concerning baptism, III, 1036. The second, 1046. The third, 1052. An opinion is given on behalf of absent bishops who had conveyed their instructions to the council, 1072, 1073. Cyprian exhorts each to state what he thinks, judging no one, III, 1052. Cyprian gives his opinion last of all, 1074. A great many bishops had assembled with presbyters and deacons, and the greater part of the people was also present, 1052. Councils held annually in Cappadocia, III, 1158. The Council of Iconium, 1161, 1170. The Roman Council, III, 766.

Enclosure within Christ’s camp and the dwellings of God the Father, III, 824. Saving concord, III, 795. Concord joined together cannot be conquered, III, 830. Indivisible concord, ibid. Concord commended, IV, 242. The bond of concord, III, 1050. While the bond of concord remains, III, 787. The concord of the priestly council, III, 763, 768. The divine concord of bishops, III, 1127. The concord of the priesthood, ibid., 1155. The glue of mutual concord, III, 995; IV, 517. Desires compel people to serve the devil, III, 792. The condition of the place, 230, 389, 394, 424. The common bodily condition, 558.

Confession of the name, III, 859. Confession of Christ, IV, 780, 793. Confession of the Lord, 654. The weapons of confession, III, 974. Its glorious crown, III, 976. A flourishing confession, IV, 275, 277. The virtues of confession, 800. The dignity of confession, III, 1197. Confession does not make one immune from the devil’s snares, IV, 515. Confession is the beginning of glory, not the merit of the crown, ibid. Confessors are praised, 327. How great the caution of confessors ought to be, 515. They are to be visited cautiously, 230. Among the confessors individual presbyters, each with an individual deacon, make the offering in turn, 231. More earnest care should be bestowed upon the confessors, 233. Many confessors were received by the brothers, ibid. Sixty-five come to Rome, 279. The Roman confessors unite the glory of confession with devotion to discipline, 288. This is truly to be a martyr and confessor, 289. How useful Cyprian’s letters were to the Roman confessors, 311. Confession cannot benefit anyone in heresy, III, 1196, 1197. A confessor speaks under God’s inspiration, IV, 431. The Lord speaks in the confessors, ibid. God inspires constancy in a confessor, 664. Confessors are a spectacle to God and examples to the brothers, 466. The people follow their shepherds in confession, 415, 418. Women and children among the confessors, 418, 419, 427, 466. The Church’s joy at the confessors’ return, 465. Pardon is given to one who confesses God, 563. An illustrious and true confessor, 234. Evangelical vigor befits none more than confessors, 310. The uncorrupted dignity of those who confess, III, 707. Nothing is more fitting than for a confessor to read the Gospel, 319, 323. More earnest care must be bestowed upon the bodies of those who die in prison without torture, 328. The days on which they die in prison are to be recorded, ibid. Whoever, after professing [Christ], is no longer alive within the day has confessed, 467. He is honored among the martyrs, 674. This is private confession, 467. The duties of confessors, 236 ff. The vices of some, 234, 237, 333. The minds of some were corrupted by five presbyters, 333. Frauds, debauchery, and adultery among certain confessors, 515. Even after their confession, some defiled the temples of God that had been sanctified by shameful intercourse, 238. Some destroy the glory of the name, ibid., 239. Exiles who return to their homeland without being ordered to do so are censured, ibid. Confessors ought to obey the presbyters and deacons, 234. They ought to fear the adversary, ibid. They ought to be admonished by presbyters and deacons, 253, 254. Divine censure instructs many in prison, 253, 255. The broken faith of some does not diminish the holiness of the confessors, 516. The greater part stands firm, ibid. Their position is enhanced by the lapse of others, ibid. Confessors seduced by Novatus and Novatian withdrew from the Church, 340, 341. On their departure from [Col. 1200] prison, schismatic and heretical error received them, 344. Good and glorious confessors could not long be detained outside the Church, III, 709. Some remained in schism because of communion with the confessors, ibid. The return of the Roman confessors from schism, III, 708, 709. They confess what they had done outside the Church, III, 719, 720. They ask that everything be erased by oblivion, ibid. Each is received in his own rank, III, 723. Everything is left to God, 724.

The sacrament of confirmation, III, 1114. What was lacking in those baptized was supplied by Peter and John, 1115. When hands were laid upon them, the Holy Spirit was poured forth, ibid. Those baptized in the Church are presented to the Church’s prelates so that they may be perfected by the Lord’s seal, ibid. Confirmation is given by bishops alone, III, 1197. Very many die after baptism without the laying on of a bishop’s hand, 1195. Nevertheless, they are regarded as fully initiated believers, 1196. If confirmation were necessary for salvation, salvation would be taken away from all bishops, 1197. A baptized person must be anointed, III, 1040. The Eucharist is that from which the baptized are anointed, ibid. Oil sanctified upon the altar, ibid.

To confess before the priests of God, 488. Confession must be made sorrowfully and candidly, ibid. The burden of the soul must be disclosed, ibid. Let each confess his sin while confession can still be admitted, 489. Basilides the bishop confessed that he had blasphemed, III, 1029. Many who do not confess the guilt upon their conscience are filled with unclean spirits, 485, 487. The crime of a concealed conscience, 486. Confession of secret thoughts is necessary, 488. Those who had contemplated sacrifice or the crime of obtaining a certificate confessed this very thing before the priests, ibid. Knowing that it is written, “God is not mocked,” ibid. There is no confession in the underworld, III, 794.

Conflict in adversity is a test of truth, 590, 591. Unlawful and dangerous unions, 366. A spouse is spurned in martyrdom, 795. Conscience carries great weight, 782. The vigor of a victorious conscience, 419. God is the judge of our conscience, 672. Conscience is crowned in peace, 676. The hiding places of conscience, 551, 645. The wounds of conscience, 553, 604. The modesty of a virginal conscience, III, 769. To shine brightly in the light of one’s own conscience, III, 776. A stained conscience, III, 764. Laws consented to sins, 215. Our assembly, 326. Factious conspiracies, 335.

Custom without truth is merely the antiquity of error, III, 1134. Truth is to be preferred to custom, III, 1064, 1070, 1171. Christ did not say, “I am custom,” III, 1064. One must not prescribe on the basis of custom but prevail by reason, 410; III, 1125. Reason and truth always exclude custom, III, 1069. One must follow not human custom but God’s truth, 383, 409. The differing customs of the churches, III, 1159. Roman custom, 1170. Because of differing customs, there was never a departure from the peace of the Church, 1159. The consulship was the highest honor among the Romans, 572. The pomp of consuls, 266. The consummated glory of a martyr, 328. CONSUS, god of counsel, 783. The contagion of poisonous speech, III, 829. Shameful and infamous contagion, 362, 363. The contamination of funereal food, III, 781. Virginal continence, III, 769. The glorious purpose of continence, III, 786. The strength of continence, 602. The palm of continence, 649. The good of continence, 753. The obstinacy of the wicked must be restrained, III, 712. The mockeries of insults, 627. Rash intruders, 507. Unauthorized assemblies, 433. An assembly of a ruined faction, 818. The assemblies of heretics, 509. Abuse is to be avoided, 239. To be despised, 808. Let the sober banquet resound with psalms, 222, 223. Wanton banquets are to be avoided, 457. Shameful, filthy banquets in the guild, III, 1030. Banquets with the wicked forbidden, III, 829. You do not regard the *corban* (an offering dedicated to God), 612. The heart of a person devoted to God, 664. Hearts are cleansed by faith, III, 1203.

CORNELIA, 279. CORNELIUS, bishop of Rome, III, 699, 703, 709, 710, 725, 731, 851. Chosen by Almighty God and our Lord Jesus Christ, III, 721, 722, 770, 771. Ordained by sixteen bishops, III, 790. Factional men obstruct the ordination of Cornelius, III, 699, 706, 711. Delegates from each side go to Africa, III, 703, 710. The letters of Cornelius’s adversaries are not read, III, 705. Delegates are sent to Rome, III, 703, 710. Meanwhile, everything remains in suspense; they write not to Cornelius but to the Church, III, 710. Cyprian advises the people of Hadrumetum not to address letters to Cornelius but to the Roman Church, ibid. Novatian’s delegates are rejected, III, 699. Those who ordained Cornelius write to Africa, III, [Col. 1201] 704, 705. The African delegates return, ibid. In council Cyprian writes on Cornelius’s behalf to all the bishops of Africa, 711. He also writes to Cornelius, 703. Letters to Cornelius from all Africa, III, 711. The episcopate of Cornelius is acknowledged by everyone in Africa, ibid. Cornelius’s character is praised, his election defended, and his unconquered constancy in the episcopate proclaimed, III, 766, 767, 770 ff. Cornelius ascended through all the grades of religious office to the lofty summit of the priesthood, III, 768. To communicate with Cornelius—that is, with the catholic Church, III, 763. The judgment of Cornelius and his colleagues concerning the lapsed, III, 767, 1031. He deliberates with many colleagues concerning the reception of Trophimus, III, 777. Fabricated charges against Cornelius, III, 778. Some accuse him of communicating with those who had offered incense, III, 763. They repeatedly assert that Cornelius was stained by the pollution of a certificate and communicates with bishops who sacrificed, 777. He is moved by the threats of Felicissimus, III, 797. He is to be numbered among the martyrs, III, 775. As leader of the confession, he persuaded the people to become confessors, III, 830. The entire Roman Church confessed, ibid. A blessed martyr, III, 974. Cornelius’s letters to Cyprian, III, 712, 715, 839. Cornelius the centurion, III, 1047.

A white crown for good works, 622. White and purple crowns, 249. The victor’s crown, 653. Baptism of blood, the crown of virtues, 654. The crown descends from God’s favor, 474. The crown of faith, 511. The crown of confession of the Lord, 350; III, 976. The crown of suffering, III, 833. The crown of justice, IV, 515. A purple crown for suffering, 622. The crowns of martyrs, 483. The crown of the Lord’s discipline, 289. The reward of heavenly crowns, 355. Crowns brought sufferings to an end, 246. One who is divided from the Church cannot be crowned in death, 783. Those who sacrifice bear the devil’s crown, 466.

The one body of our union, 360. The body of the Lord’s flock, 349. The body of the catholic Church, III, 702. The joining together of the ecclesiastical body, III, 790. They assail the Lord’s body, 478. The protection of Christ’s body and blood, III, 856. Our bodies are members of Christ, III, 792. The fellowship of our body, III, 795. An enervated body, IV, 363. The material of bodies is alike, 550. Their condition is common, 558. Good people heed correction, 776. Corrupters of the Gospel, 508. To belch up drunken excess from indigestion, 391. Even the persecutor is compelled to believe, 795. The living father of believers, 525. How great the power of believing is, 757. He had taught the creditor to recover what was entrusted to him, 434. CREDULA, martyr, 281. CREMENTIUS, subdeacon, 224, 229, 263. Crescens of Cirta, III, 1087. The crime of the will, 447. One who commanded a crime is a participant in it, 310. To alter the hair with counterfeit colors, 454. To dye the hair, 456, 490. Mountain crests, 786. Crocodiles, 553. The sign of the cross, 715. The sign of the cross upon the forehead, 514. Moses’ upraised hands in the sign and mystery of the cross, 662. Ingenious cruelty, 554. Washed in their own blood, 799. Cuiculi, III, 1097. Abundant stalks of grain, 800. Desire for heavenly glory, 312. A cleric cannot be the curator of a will, 398. Dog-headed peoples, 553.

CYPRIAN, who is Thascius, 400. Caecilius Cyprianus, 403. He lay in darkness and vice, 198. Conversion did not seem possible to him, 199. How he was changed, ibid. At Carthage he believed and grew in faith, 326. Bishop by the vote of the people and the judgment of God, 333. Five presbyters conspire against his episcopate, ibid. The people are indignant with them, 337. Cyprian overlooks the insults directed against his episcopate, 250, 251. He does nothing without the counsel of the clergy and the consent of the people, 234. He consults the clergy and people concerning ordinations, 318. Chosen bishop in time of peace by the vote of the whole people, III, 803. Serving discipline in tranquillity, proscribed in the storm, III, 804. Violently demanded by the clamor of the people, 262. How he was proscribed, 403. His withdrawal criticized by some, 224, 262. He defends himself, 262, 263. He withdrew out of concern for the peace of the brothers, 262. He avoids public view out of consideration for the Church’s interests, 232. The Lord commanded him to withdraw, 253. On withdrawing, he left a sum of money with the clerics, 232. He was absent only in body, 262, 295. He appointed deputies in his absence, 328. Cyprian has no rest, 303. He does not return lest he become the cause of peace being broken, 326. Lest he appear to have intensified the persecution, 335. He hopes to return soon, 326. He commends the confessors detained in prison, 327. He wishes to be present so that he might fulfill the duties of love toward them, 328. Five presbyters delay Cyprian’s return, 334. How burdensome the two-year exile was to Cyprian, 335. He desires that all [Col. 1202] the churches agree with one another in their judgment concerning the lapsed, 263, 274, 301, 315. He is indignant with the presbyters who had granted peace to the lapsed, 254 ff. He excludes from his communion anyone who communicates with the lapsed, 301; III, 763. He does not think a matter of such importance should be overlooked, 251. His grief over the lapse of his own people, 468. He considers himself prostrate in his prostrate brothers, ibid. He accords some weight to the martyrs’ certificates, 259, 260. He makes some concessions to mitigate the violence of the lapsed, 263. Certain rather harsh charges against Cyprian were inserted into the letter of the lapsed, 306. He communicated with none of the lapsed as long as the persecution raged, III, 767. He was more severe toward the lapsed while they were still able to prevail, 261; III, 764. His censure is praised, 295, 304. After Easter he deals with the case of the lapsed together with his colleagues, 338. He yields to the necessity of the times, III, 768. He does not depart from what was established in council, ibid. He maintains that lapsed bishops ought to be deposed and subjected to penance, III, 1027, 1028. Those who had deceived Stephen in order to be restored ought not to be restored, 1028. Through Cyprian’s efforts, the episcopate of Cornelius is acknowledged throughout Africa and Novatian is condemned, III, 710, 711. He regards the glory of the confessors as his own, 289. He sends the books *On the Lapsed* and *On the Unity of the Church* to the confessors, 345. His grief over the confessors’ schism, 343. The schismatics wander throughout the province and do not dare approach Cyprian, III, 824. Fearless, Cyprian considers it no concern of his by whom he is killed, III, 827. Cyprian’s fearless spirit, III, 804. He maintains that a case must be heard where the crime was committed, III, 821. The authority of bishops established in Africa is no less, III, 822. He was considering coming to the Thibaritans to exhort them, IV, 349. He serves God and Christ, and with pure lips unceasingly offers sacrifices both in persecution and in peace, 406, 407.

He prays in the sacrifices and prayers for Pope Lucius, III, 996. Cyprian’s candid heart, 422, 423. Pupianus’s invectives and calumnies against Cyprian, 400 ff. His manner of dealing with schismatics, III, 823, 826. He closes the Church to no one, forgives everything, and overlooks much, III, 824. He says that, by forgiving offenses more than is proper, he himself almost commits an offense, 825. He receives individually those who come to the Church, 402. One or two persons received by Cyprian, despite the resistance of the people, proved to be worse, III, 824. He serves the brethren daily, 402. Cyprian’s humility, 308. He exhorts more by affection than by authority, 443. He calls himself the last and least, ibid. Brethren and pagans alike know and love his humility, 402. He is accused of excessive leniency in the case of the lapsed, III, 764. Cyprian’s charity toward the poor, 327, 329; in ransoming captives, 360; in assisting martyrs, 421, 422, 424. He sends something from his own modest funds to assist the confessors, 240. He invites to Carthage the poor whom his own church cannot support, 363, 364. The extent of Cyprian’s personal means, 327. Through a revelation he learns of the coming persecution, 242; III, 799, 856. He foretells a persecution more cruel than the former one, 350. God reveals to Cyprian that peace will soon come, 239, 244. A revelation shown to Cyprian, 407. Through a revelation he learns that the day of trial is approaching for himself and Cornelius, III, 974. The brethren are not of one mind in prayer, 242. They grow drowsy during prayers, 243. Divine admonitions concerning frugal food and sober drinking, 244. It was often revealed to Cyprian that he should proclaim that the dead are not to be mourned, 596. He consults God, 407. In the baptismal controversy he imposes no rule upon others, III, 1081, 1110, 1126, 1147, 1151. To some he appears a preacher of truth and a betrayer of unity, III, 1116. He is called a pseudo-Christ and pseudo-apostle, III, 1176. He is censured without being named, III, 1185. He is said to be endowed with the obtuseness of heretics, ibid. He is accused of having wished to correct the errors of all the churches, ibid. Cyprian’s complaints concerning Stephen, III, 1133—especially that Stephen thinks priests who maintain truth and unity should be excluded from communion, ibid. He fights for the honor and unity of the Church, III, 1116. Cyprian considers it insufficient merely to raise up the people by his voice unless he also strengthens them by a reading from Scripture, 652, 653. In his books he identifies himself, 420. The usefulness of Cyprian’s writings, ibid. He always speaks with elevated thoughts, ibid. Firmilian received the writings sent by Cyprian as though they were his own, 1157. He did not read them cursorily, but often committed them to memory, ibid. Cyprian was exiled for confessing the Name, 414. He is the first in the proconsul’s official record to make his confession, 421, 423. He is first among the martyrs because he was the first to confess, ibid. Cyprian’s withdrawal before his passion, 432 [reading secessus for the apparent OCR successus]. He wishes to suffer martyrdom at Carthage, ibid.

## D

A demon cannot move the earth, but, foreknowing an earthquake, pretends that he will cause it, III, 1164. Demons are put to flight by Christians, 574, 575. The poets know demons, 573. Principal demons, III, 1164. Different punishments of the damned, 798. Daniel devoted to God, 667. He refused to worship Bel, 354; III, 973. He is praised, 482, 490. A meal is divinely provided for Daniel, [Col. 1203] 534, 609. Daniel consulted by Nebuchadnezzar, 606. He overcame the king’s threats, 793. DATIVA, 281. DATIVUS of Badis, III, 1061. Dativus confined in the mines, 414, 420. Saul persecutes David, 641, 667. David danced before the ark, 782. The Lord calls sins “debts,” 534. Tithes granted to the Levites, 398. From our patrimony we do not give even tithes, 518. DECIMUS, presbyter, 272. DECIUS, tyrant, III, 774. Defeated by war and arms, III, 774. His hatred of priests, III, 774. He heard more patiently that a rival emperor had been raised against him than that a priest of God had been appointed at Rome, ibid. He marvels at the steadfastness of Celerinus, 321. The faces of the dead are preserved by means of an image, 565. An affected boast, 590. The sloth of an overdelicate mind, 583. Transgressions blaze everywhere, 214. The vapor of seething transgressions, 296. Let us reckon up our transgressions, 483. Transgressions become religious observances, 212. To file down, 232. Enticements of the ears, 785. No fear of transgressing, 551. Demetrianus used to come repeatedly to Cyprian, 545. More from a zeal for contradicting than for learning, ibid. He sowed hatred against Christians, ibid. He said that all the calamities of the world ought to be imputed to them, 546. DEMETRIUS, bishop, III, 852. Demetrius of Leptiminus, III, 1065. Noah’s nakedness denounced by his son, 375. Felicissimus the schismatic lays waste to marriage, III, 797. Deposits offered to the Church, III, 726, 729, 756. Fabulous lusts are danced out, 785. Detraction forbidden, 777. To triumph utterly over, 786.

GOD is his name, 577. Gentiles know God the Father, III, 1068. God has no name, 577. The common saying, “God sees,” ibid. God is Lord of all, 575. He cannot be seen, 576. The whole world is God’s temple, ibid. The perpetual vision of God, 564. He receives interest through alms to the poor, 613. He sees the hearts and breasts of individuals, 488. He is the ruler and Lord of the world, 548. Nothing can happen unless God has either done it or permitted it to happen, ibid. Nothing happens either without God’s knowledge or without his permission, 483. He cannot be deceived, 672, 761. He is to be feared in the majesty of a judge, 492. God becomes angry, 549. He is not mocked, 488, 672. He must be appeased by prolonged satisfaction, 334, 478. God’s wrath must be appeased by fasts and tears, 489. God is indulgent and severe, 314. A diligent exactor of his commandments, ibid. The Lord’s indulgence in allowing us to call God Father, 526. God’s patience, 625. Why God is patient, 755. Ever indulgent and good, 494. He defers judgment so that man may be converted, 624. He is the hearer of the heart, 522. He penetrates hidden and secret things, 521. One who has God will lack nothing, provided that he himself does not fail God, 534. One God is Lord of all, 575. Bees have one king, flocks one leader, and the world one ruler, 576. He is one and, wholly present, is diffused everywhere, 577. Everything we are able to do belongs to God, 201, 202. He watches us as we contend, 356. Christ is God, the master of peace and concord, 524. God must be entreated, 241, 242. God alone is to be worshiped, 654, 657. Father of those who believe and understand, 531. He who does not have the Church as mother does not have God as Father, 503. Come to know God, even if late, 561. God must be believed, ibid. Man demands servitude from his servant yet does not acknowledge the Lord his God, 550. God is neither known nor feared, ibid. He is not worshiped, 568. He is neither sought nor feared, 548. God’s mysteries cannot be discerned, 760. God speaks within us, 354. He is the judge of our conscience, 672. God must be consecrated in our mind, 576, 577. He makes priests, III, 768, 401. God’s works are perfect, III, 1015. He shows no partiality, III, 1016. Nothing is to be preferred to the love of God and Christ, IV, 746. The unknown God, III, 1160.

Bracelets, 451. The devil perished through envy and brought ruin, 634, 640. He could not patiently endure that man had been made in God’s image, 634. He can do nothing without God’s permission, 772. Power against us is given to the devil, 537. Subtle in peace, violent in persecution, 640. Hidden weapons are more frequent, ibid. Seeing idols abandoned, he devised heresies and schisms, 497. He does not attack heretics, but those whom he sees standing firm, III, 904. He assails every stronger person all the more, 236. He does not eagerly seek to overthrow those whom he has already made his own, III, 834. The devil provokes those in whom he sees Christ dwelling, III, 835. This is always the devil’s work: to rend God’s servants with falsehood, III, 776. He had utterly triumphed over the whole world, 786. Always lying and deceitful, 338. He flatters in order to deceive, 460. The devil’s cunning and arts, 495. He prowls around us, 639. He frequently steals upon us and penetrates within, 339. Altars of the devil, III, 812; IV, 473. Comparison [Col. 1204] of the devil with Christ, 618. He is tormented by exorcists, 1151. The devil must be resisted, 779. How he is to be conquered, 653. To kill the devil, 421.

The apostles appointed deacons for themselves as ministers of their episcopate and of the Church, 396. When the solemn rites have been completed, the deacon offers the cup to those present, 485. Deacons, together with presbyters, customarily govern confessors, 253, 254. Individual deacons minister to presbyters among the confessors, 231. *Exomologesis* before a deacon, 259. A deacon insulting his bishop, 394. How ordinations of deacons are to be conducted, III, 1026. A deacon suspended because he was discovered in the same bed with virgins, 369. DIANA of Tauris, 571. The day dawns equally for everyone, III, 1149. It gives light equally, 620. Feast days, 565. The eighth day, that is, the first after the Sabbath, III, 1018. A day appointed for Christians to deny the faith, 467. The course of worldly days, III, 1015. To speak with the fingers, 785.

The gods worshiped by the gentiles are adjured and tormented by Christians, 555. They are cast wailing from bodies, ibid., 575. They tremble beneath the Christians’ hand, 555. When asked what they are, they answer while gentiles listen, ibid. Christians openly destroy the gods even in the forum itself, 554. They publicly confound them by declaring themselves Christians, ibid. The gods are shut up and kept under guard lest they perish, 555. It is shameful to worship those whom you yourself defend, ibid. Profane gods, 634. The Idaean mother of the gods, 571. The Romans’ home-bred gods, 569. Those whom the populace worships are not gods, 564.

DIOGA of Leptimagnensis, III, 1099. DIONYSIANA, III, 1095. Dionysius the schismatic, III, 713. Ecclesiastical discipline, 319, 333, 365; III, 729, 799. The vigor of ecclesiastical discipline enervated, IV, 781. Divine discipline, 648; III, 1022. Evangelical discipline, 311, 334. Christian discipline corrupted by a long peace, 468. The crown of the Lord’s discipline, 289. The discipline of innocence, 552. The severity of discipline, 415. The discipline of religion and truth, 386. The robust discipline of the Lord’s law, 286. The governance of discipline, 324. Examination of discipline, III, 768. God’s discipline must be observed, 769. Observance of discipline, 365. The foundation of religion and faith rests upon observance and discipline, 441. Discipline is the guardian of hope, the restraining bond of faith, a guide on the path of salvation, a stimulus and nourishment of good character, and a teacher of virtue, 440, 441. Nothing is so necessary as the due severity of divine vigor, 308. The Church’s welfare cannot be provided for unless the principle of discipline, always guarded, is obeyed, 309. The severity of discipline among the Romans, ibid. Gladiatorial training, 206.

The disciples abandoned Christ, III, 896. They are called the salt of the earth, 530. Those at discord are condemned, 536. The discordant are Christ’s adversaries, 503. Discord cannot attain the kingdom of heaven, 510, 539. Discord cannot be washed away even by the baptism of blood, 510, 536. The sowing of discord, III, 790. Discords break out afresh, III, 704, 833. The fury of discord, III, 835, 1050; IV, 505, 510, 512. The poison of discord, 650. A discordant style, III, 705. Discordant speech, IV, 509. Hair ornaments, 451. Divine ordering, 336; III, 704, 1123, 1130, 1147. Ecclesiastical ordering, 340. The evil of dissension, 517. The madness of dissension, III, 833. There is no place for dissimulation when the brotherhood is being deceived by certain persons, 251.

The unfruitful rich man, 613. No one is rich in this world, 611. The rich are always fearful, 219, 220. Their misery, ibid. The rich perish through their riches, 474. The mouth and tongue of the sinful rich man were tormented more severely, III, 800. Riches are not only to be despised but are also dangerous, 533. The truth of divinity rejected, III, 1160. Monthly distributions, 324. A teacher of hearers, 287. Presbyters as teachers, ibid. Adulterated doctrines, 336. Pain as witness to the truth [*versitatis*, perhaps OCR for *veritatis*], 582. To reckon a brother’s pain as one’s own, 360. One ought to grieve wisely, 438. A deceitful worker, III, 1176. Care for members of one’s household, 771. The dwelling place of unity and truth, III, 732.

To celebrate the Lord’s rite, 386, 612. To read in the church, 320. Christians dismissed from the church, 784. Servants ought to obey their masters, 771. Masters ought to be gentler toward their servants, ibid. The Lord is greater than the devil, 655; III, 1192. The Lord’s peace, III, 1127. The house of the Church, 506. DONATA, 281. DONATUS, 191 ff. Donatus, presbyter, 234. Donatus, bishop of Carthage, III, 810. Donatus, bishop, III, 852, 1036. Donatus of Cibaliana, III, 1069, 1095. Donatus [Col. 1205], martyr, 281. DONATULUS, 346. Donatulus of Capsa, III, 1070. Falling asleep, 368, 399. A legitimate doubt ought not to be censured, III, 763. A DUCENARIUS procurator, III, 1030. How “if two or three gather in Christ’s name” is to be understood, 509.

## E

The Church extends more widely into a multitude, 501. It stretches its rays throughout the whole world, 502. It extends its branches over the entire earth, ibid. One mother, abundant in the successes of her fruitfulness, ibid. The body of the whole Church, whose members are distributed throughout the various provinces, 307. One Church throughout the entire world, III, 790. The Catholic Church, 345. The Church consists in the bishop, the clergy, and all who stand firm, 299. The number of the lapsed is not the Church, ibid. Those who remain in God’s house are the Church, III, 807. The Catholic Church, which is one and true, III, 1037. Who cannot remain in the Church, III, 720. Only one who has not been planted in the commandments of God the Father can depart from the Church, III, 731. And remain with heretics, ibid. Those who depart from the Church were not planted by God, III, 807. The root and mother of the Catholic Church, III, 710. Wheat and tares in the Church, 344. God did not grant even the apostles the power to separate the chaff from the wheat, ibid.; III, 791. Christ presides and watches in the Church, 618. Christ established and made the Church, 509. A human church established by schismatics, III, 790. The body of the Catholic Church, III, 702. The Church is the people united to the priest, 406. Christ prayed that we might be one as the Father and the Son are one, 539. It is a different confession to confess that the Church is one, 343. The Church is one, 336, 406, 500, 517; III, 734, 1140. It is one and alone, 392. In Christ there is one body, to which our number has been united, 384. The Church is one body, 517. A dwelling place of unanimity, 506. Christ accords the greatest importance not to multitude but to unanimity, 508. The Church’s unity adheres to the heavenly sacraments, 504. A people united from the unity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, 536. The Church’s unity comes from divine steadfastness, 504. It comes from the ordering of the divine dispensation, III, 1046. The Lord, indicating that unity comes from divine favor, says: “I and the Father are one,” III, 1141. The unity of Christ and likewise of the Church, joined by indivisible bonds, III, 727. One God and one Church, 517. There is one house of God, 371. One Christ and one Church, III, 1116. There is no other house besides the one Church, 506. Why the Lord’s tunic was not torn, 505. The Lord’s flock has one soul and one body, 340. The Novatians lie in the baptismal interrogation, since they do not have the Church, III, 1144. If the Church was with Novatian, it was not with Cornelius, III, 1140. The devil promises a church in order to tear people away from the Church, 338. The Church is not among heretics, because it is one and cannot be divided, III, 1131. The schismatics repeatedly told their adherents that they would return together to the Church, III, 823.

Unity must be firmly maintained and defended, 501. Especially by bishops, ibid. The one Church that lives forever and gives life, 409. The Church cannot be rent or divided, III, 734, 1131, 1141. It does not depart from Christ, 106. Unity cannot in any way be separated and divided, III, 1141, 1142. The unity of the Church cannot be divided, III, 790; IV, 504. The Church’s unity comes from heaven and from the Father, 505. Criminal is the person who thinks God’s unity can be rent, ibid. Nothing will be able to separate the Church from Christ, 384. The Church cannot be adulterated, 502. She is incorrupt and chaste, ibid. The Church is incorrupt, III, 1117. The Church’s water cannot be adulterated or corrupted, ibid. The Church never departs at all from Christ’s teaching, III, 807. The Church is not rent or divided, but joined by the cement of priests adhering to one another, 406. All the churches joined with Cyprian by the bond of unity, 405. The consensus of all the churches in condemning Novatian, III, 994. On deferring the case of the lapsed, 335. On adjudicating the same case, III, 1033. The venerable authority of all the churches, III, 1184.

The Church alone possesses Christ’s grace and truth, III, 1044, 1065. All power and grace are established in the Church, III, 1161. All grace and truth are in the Church, 409. The Church holds and possesses all the power of her Bridegroom and Lord, III, 1116. The Church formerly barren, 688. The marriage of Christ and the Church, 383. When the Jews ceased, the people of the gentiles flocked to the marriage of Christ and the Church, ibid. The Church alone is Christ’s bride, III, 1132. She alone can beget children for God, ibid. The Church is Christ’s bride, 502. The Church alone bears children for Christ, III, 1167. Christ is not with those who gather outside the Church, 509. No salvation outside the Church, 503. Outside the Church, without communion and peace, they perish, III, 1050. Those who depart from the Church are condemned by themselves, 333; III, 726. One separated from the Church [Col. 1206] is condemned by himself, 513; III, 1116. The head and root of the one Church, III, 1111. One who resists the Church is not in the Church, 500. Nothing is permissible outside the Church, ibid. One should rejoice when wolves and dogs are separated from the Church, 506. So that they may not prey upon the doves and sheep, ibid. One who does not dwell in God’s house is an alien and a profane person, III, 1142. Neither life nor salvation exists outside unity, 371, 504. It is no easier to escape outside the Church than outside Noah’s ark, 503. One who separates himself from the fellowship of Christ’s clergy and people is not with Christ, 513. Whatever departs from the mother-stock will not be able to live, 517. Those outside the Church are dead, 409. Outside the Church nothing can be loosed or bound, III, 1114. The stain of heresy is not washed away even by blood, 510. No one outside the Church is a martyr, ibid. Martyrdom in heresy is not the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness, 511. Such a person can be killed but cannot be crowned, III, 783, 1124; IV, 511, 515. One killed outside the Church for the sake of the name is not crowned, III, 783. Death in confession of the name outside the Church is not the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness, III, 835. Those who persevere in shameless obstinacy can never be admitted into the Church, 370.

Christ built his Church upon the rock, III, 1061, 1168. Built upon Peter, III, 806, 1114; IV, 406, 410, 628. One Church, founded by Christ the Lord upon Peter with the origin and principle of unity, III, 1043, 1114; IV, 410. It is one and founded upon one man, who also received its keys, III, 1116. The Church’s foundations placed upon Peter, III, 1168. The first and one Church founded upon Peter, 668. Upon Peter alone, 500. The principal Church, III, 818. Mother Church, 341; III, 704, 1125. It is closed to no one, 627. The Church in the likeness of paradise, III, 1116. Hannah as a type of the Church, 522. What heretics and schismatics contrive among themselves does not affect the Church’s majesty, III, 808. Mother Church laments the ruin of very many, 249. Children of the Church, III, 1167. The Church’s glory is the glory of its prelate, 236. The Church is white and purple, 240. The structure of the ecclesiastical body, III, 790. The balance by which the Church is governed, III, 992. The seven churches, 689.

Ecstasy, 253. The ecstasy of a woman seized by a demon, III, 1164. Deadly edicts, III, 775; IV, 356. The presentation of a public show, 617. EGNATIUS, martyr, 323. Chosen for the reward of glory, 515.

Almsgiving commanded by Christ, 607. The good of almsgiving, 728. Almsgiving commended, 540, 603. It must be denied to no one, 730. Souls are delivered from death by alms, 492. Almsgiving cleanses sins, 603. It must not be done for display, 757. To persist in almsgiving, 492. One who gives to the least lends to God, 541. One who helps the poor wins favor through the prayers of many, 449. Whatever is rendered to a poor person is rendered to Christ, 620. One must lend to the Lord from one’s wealth and resources, 493. In almsgiving and modest work, the will is sufficient, 732. Christ must be fed, 449. The poor widow preferred Elijah to her children, 614. One who places himself and his children before Christ sins, 615.

The elements are not to be worshiped, 655. The eloquence of the world is not the kingdom of God, 770. EMERITA, 279, 281. The people of Emerita, III, 1021. She purchases [adornment] with defilement so that she may shine, 216. ENOCH translated, 598, 684. EPICTETUS, bishop of Assuras, 389.

God makes bishops, III, 711, 768, 803; IV, 396, 398, 401. A bishop is a judge given by God for the time, 402. The Church is established upon the bishops, 298. This is founded upon divine law, ibid. The Church over which, by the Lord’s indulgence, we preside, 361. God and his Christ made Cornelius bishop, III, 768, 770. Bishops ought to guard the camp divinely entrusted to them, III, 1135. Christ entrusted his bride to the bishops, III, 1068. The Lord chose the apostles, that is, the prelates, 396. They preside in the Church, 501. They are the successors of the apostles, III, 707, 1071, 1169. They govern the Church with the same power as the apostles, ibid. In the Church there is one priest and judge for the time, acting in Christ’s place, III, 803. The bishop is one, 403. One in the Church, 803. One chosen by divine appointment, III, 974. One in the Catholic Church, III, 727. An adulterous and alien bishop is not a bishop, III, 790. The bishop is in the Church, and the Church in the bishop, 406, 396. To establish another bishop is to establish another church, 340. If anyone is not with the bishop, he is not in the Church, 406. The episcopate is one, 501. A share of it is held wholly by each bishop, ibid. Since the episcopate of Cornelius was confirmed by the consent of all the bishops, whoever wishes to be bishop besides him is outside, III, 773. The one episcopate, diffused through the harmonious multitude of many bishops, III, 790. A portion of the flock assigned to each pastor, III, 821. Episcopal unity, III, 791. The body of priests joined by the bond of unity, III, 995. Many priests shepherd one flock, ibid. They ought to cherish all the sheep, ibid. The decree of Cornelius together with absolutely all the bishops appointed throughout the whole world, III, 1031; IV, 334, 335, 399. If any bishop attempts to create a heresy and lay waste the flock, the others ought to give aid and gather the sheep, III, 991.

How great a crime it is to curse priests, III, 802. How much reverence is owed to priests is proved from the Scriptures, 396. Bishops are vindicated by God, ibid. One who despises bishops is not with Christ, 513. One must rise in the bishop’s presence, 773. The authority of bishops, 298. Schisms arise from contempt for bishops, 402. A bishop can immediately punish an insulting deacon, 394. All his colleagues would regard this with approval, ibid. A deacon who insults his bishop ought to do penance for his audacity, 396. Even if lawfully ordained, a bishop is no longer a bishop if he withdraws from unity, III, 791. If bishops deposed for idolatry persist in their madness, the people must separate from them, 392. An adulterous and alien bishop, III, 790. Freedom granted to bishops in undecided matters, III, 787, 821, 1110, 1126, 1129. They will render an account of their actions to the Lord alone, ibid. How episcopal elections are to be conducted, III, 1025, 1026. The form of episcopal election, III, 768. Bishops appointed without the law of ordination, 507. An episcopate given by no one, ibid. Which bishops are to be chosen, III, 1027. Bishops are priests of God and Christ, 388. A bishop must not be quarrelsome or contentious, III, 1135. Sound and upright bishops, 392. They ought to be humble, 401. Bishops have a greater share in the common joy, 235, 236. The meeting of the bishops’ minds, III, 1158. The vigor of the episcopate, III, 798; IV, 394. Nothing ought to terrify a bishop, III, 798. It will be charged against bishops on the day of judgment if they have not cared for a wounded sheep, III, 780, 781. A bishop ought not only to teach but also to learn, III, 1135. He teaches better who daily grows and advances by learning better things, ibid. It befits a bishop to offer sacrifice in the presence of the brethren, III, 976. A bishop ought to provide for peace and tranquility, 335. Bishops subject to penance, III, 1029, 1031. The vices of very many bishops before the persecution of Decius, 470. Certain bishops sacrificed to idols, III, 777. Bishops of the worst manner of life, III, 1194. The condemnation of bishops who live wickedly, 390. Bishop of a bishop, 402. No one is a bishop of bishops, III, 1085. The authority of bishops in Africa is not inferior, III, 822. A bishop ought to write through clerics, 287.

A clerical letter, 229. An authentic letter, ibid. More lavish banquets are to be avoided, 244. To gape greedily after feasts and dinners, 391. The stretching rack, 213, 476. A body stretched upon the rack, 795. Wandering spirits, 203. Error in place of truth, 491. One must not continue in error merely because an error was once committed, III, 1125. One who errs in simplicity can be forgiven, III, 1117. One who deliberately and knowingly adheres to error sins without the pardon granted to ignorance, ibid. Those who err ought not to be followed, III, 1160. A participant in another’s error, 343. The error of custom, III, 1170. The condition of error, III, 1060. Schismatic and heretical error, 344.

ESAU lost his rights of primacy, III, 1126; IV, 634. Hostile to his brother Jacob, 641. ETECUSA, 277. Gentiles and publicans, III, 1143. The corrupt morals of the gentiles, 211. They hated Christians before knowing them, 575.

The Eucharist is the holy body of the Lord, 254. Institution of the Eucharist, 376. Christ offered his body and blood, ibid. He first offered himself as a sacrifice to the Father, 383. To celebrate the Eucharist, III, 1055. To celebrate the Eucharist with an invocation not to be despised, 1165. He commanded it to be done in remembrance of himself, so that he himself might be offered to the Father, 383. To give the Eucharist to the unworthy is to profane the Lord’s holy body, 254. To receive the Lord’s body with polluted hands, 484. To drink the Lord’s blood with a polluted mouth, ibid. With throats exhaling crime, they seize the Lord’s body, 478. They approach the Lord’s holy body with filthy hands, ibid. Violence is inflicted upon the Lord’s body and blood, 479. They sin more against the Lord with their hands and mouth than when they denied him, ibid. See LAPSED. The Eucharist did not remain in a violated body, 485. So great is the Lord’s power, so great his majesty, 486. Ashes in place of the Eucharist in the hands of a man who had denied the faith, ibid. A similar man mangles his own tongue with his teeth, 484. A woman kills herself with a sword after unworthy communion, 486. The Lord departs when he is denied, 487. The Eucharist carried in the hand, 486, 631, 784. Let the right hand that received the Lord’s body embrace him, 357. The Lord’s holy thing is stored in a chest for communion at home, 486. Firmilian is indignant that the unbaptized touch the Lord’s body and blood, III, 1172. How cautiously those who carry Christ’s body with them ought to proceed, 784. The Eucharist is received daily, 350. We receive the Eucharist daily, 531. The Eucharist cannot be celebrated among heretics, III, 1041.

Christ’s blood in the Eucharist, 384. Wine is mentioned so that the Lord’s blood may be understood, 378, 379. If someone [Col. 1208] offers wine alone, Christ’s blood begins to be without us, 384. If there is water alone, the people begin to be without Christ, ibid. Christ’s blood is not offered if wine is absent from the cup, 382. Christ’s blood cannot be in the cup when the cup lacks wine, 375. Christ’s blood is represented by wine, ibid. Christ called the wine his blood, 381. Water alone cannot represent Christ’s blood, 382. We could not drink Christ’s blood unless Christ had first been trodden and pressed, 379. To give forth the fragrance of Christ’s blood through the taste of wine, 386. We cannot shed our blood for Christ if we are ashamed to drink Christ’s blood, ibid.

The effects of the Eucharist, 382. When Christ’s blood has been drunk, the memory of the old man is cast away, 383. Christ’s blood must be given to penitents so that they may shed their own blood for Christ, III, 856. The faithful drink Christ’s blood daily so that they may shed their blood for Christ, 350. One whom the reception of the Eucharist does not strengthen is not fit for martyrdom, III, 856. The Eucharist is a protection for those who receive it, ibid. Mouths, after receiving the Lord’s body and blood, rejected the remnants of the idols, 466. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, ibid. The Eucharist must be received with fear, 774. We pray that, if some graver transgression intervenes and we are suspended, we may not be separated from Christ’s body, 531. The Eucharist does not benefit the unworthy, 487. Christ is the bread of those who touch his body, 531. Christ is our bread, ibid. The Lord’s sacrifices themselves also declare Christian unanimity, 384; III, 1141. The Eucharist avails nothing without works, 751. The Eucharist is that from which the baptized are anointed, III, 1040, 1041.

EUCHRATIUS, bishop, 362. Euchratius of Thenae, III, 1064. EUGENIUS of Ammedera, III, 1065. EUTYCIANUS, bishop, III, 1036; IV, 424. Evangelical law, 387; III, 1114. The evangelical law and the Lord’s tradition must be observed, 387. The unity of the evangelical sacrament, 343. Evangelical communion, 304. Evangelical truth, ibid. The Gospel cannot stand firm in one part and totter in another, 482. Martyrs can do nothing against the Gospel, 483. Martyrs are made through the Gospel, 304. Those who separate themselves from the Church wish in vain to defend the Gospel, 340.

EVARISTUS, from being a bishop, now not even a layman, III, 726. Evaristus the schismatic, III, 714. Strife for exaltation cannot exist among Christians, 645. What was committed by many must be examined by many, 312. The people’s faith is disarmed, III, 816. The *excessus* (departure or transgression) of Cyprian’s colleague, 228, 229. To be raised from the rank of presbyter, III, 730. Those things become precedents that have ceased to be regarded as crimes, 208. An example of a letter from certain lapsed persons, 303. Wandering away from the path of the true road, 517. The consummation of a glorious death, 329.

*Exomologesis*—confession and penitential acknowledgment, 251, 256, 257, 259, 260, 263, 281, 370, 479, 488, 490, 778; III, 794. According to the order of discipline, one proceeds to *exomologesis*, 251, 257. Daniel, even after the grace of innocence, makes *exomologesis*, 490. The power of exorcists, III, 1151. Praise of a certain exorcist, III, 1164, 1165. The force of exorcisms, 203 ff., 555, 559. To exorcise demons, 783. The day of the campaign, 519. Examination of discipline, III, 768. God’s testing, 391. A domestic assailant, 474. To discharge the needs of the brethren, 330. To love arrogance, 516. An exile, 261, 262, 272, 274, 276, 332. Exiles and fugitives, III, 781. Exiles stripped of all their possessions, 261. Exiles from the episcopal chair and the people, III, 726. Exultation in one’s mind, 419.

## F

**FABIAN**, a man of most noble memory, 312. Fabian, pope, III, 810. Fabian, bishop of Rome, III, 1140. Fabian’s place, that is, the chair of Peter, III, 772. Tale of Greek lust, 782. Those devoted to fables, 195. An uncorrupted face, 460. Troublesome through his own indulgence, 285. The truth of the crime is expressed through bodily pain, 554. Faction of heretical depravity, III, 726. A dissenting faction, III, 706. God’s handiwork must not be adulterated, 454. Opportunity for making a transcript, 316. Poisoned eloquence, III, 833. Deceit hateful to the faithful, 671. Blind and hidden deceit, 496. Consummate deceit, 613. Forgers, 552, 643. [Col. 1209] Eternal hunger, 363. The fasces of twelve consuls, 266. The three Fates, 278. The respite of the waning year, 194.

**FAUSTINUS**, bishop, III, 851. Faustinus of Lyons, III, 990. Germinius Faustinus, an African presbyter, 399.

**FAUSTUS**, bishop, III, 1021. Faustus of Timida Regia, III, 1069.

Torch. Torches for kindling faith, 296.

**FEVER** dedicated as a deity, 570.

**FELICIANUS**, acolyte, III, 809.

**FELICISSIMUS**, schismatic, 329, 330, 332; III, 707, 708, 728, 797, 808. He threatens that those who obey Cyprian will not communicate with him at death, 330. His presbyterate, III, 707. Five presbyters joined to him, 333. Excommunicated by Cyprian, 330. An attendant of Novatus, III, 728. He threatens clubs, swords, and stones, III, 798, 799. The party of Felicissimus consists neither of sacrificers nor of heretics, 333. He is able to assemble bishops, 818. More were present at the judgment of the schismatics than follow them, 823.

**FELICISSIMUS**, Catholic, 428.

**FELIX**, bishop, 346; III, 1021, 1036. Felix of Caesaraugusta, III, 1028. Felix confined in the mines, 414, 420, 423. Felix of Dagai, III, 1061. Felix of Amaccora, 1065. Of Uthina, 1063. Of Marazana, 1067. Of Busaceni, 1069. Of Gurgites, 1071. Felix, presbyter, 272; III, 1028. Felix, schismatic, III, 810.

A woman stronger than the men torturing her, 446. Praise of Christian women, 427. God commanded that we triumph in the Church together with women, ibid. He commands us privately to beware of feminine contests, ibid. A body is cast to wild beasts, 799. Wild beasts overcome by religious devotion, 786. A rabid beast is nourished for the punishment of man, 783.

That the faithful person must be innocent, 756. Why a faithful person should be corrected, 762. A faithful person must not live as a Gentile, 755. Trust must be placed in God alone, 737. The strength of those who trust, III, 785. Our faith must be simple, 760. The first outlines of faith, 677. The majesty of faith, 310. The unanimity of faith and truth, III, 1157. Faith is one, III, 1136. The unity of faith, deriving from God the Father and from the tradition of Jesus Christ, III, 1131. According to the merits of faith, each person receives only as much as he believes himself to receive, 665. God does not desire our blood, but seeks faith, 594. Faith is of great benefit, 757. The immovable strength of faith, III, 798. Unconquered faith, 347. The uncorrupted vigor of faith, 268. Faith in Christ must be maintained, 297. One cannot reach God the Father except through his Son Christ, 718, 750. Those of faith are children of Abraham, 377. Among schismatics faith cannot be sound, III, 1195. There can be no security between faith and faithlessness, III, 829. To recover faith, 273. Faith lying prostrate and almost asleep, 468. Rough faith, III, 1194. Failing faith that receives [reading uncertain], 665. Certain faith in things to come, 676. Hearts are cleansed by faith, 1204. Confidence under interrogation, 529.

**FIDUS**, bishop, III, 1013.

Earthly fabrications, 624. We are called children of God, 526. Made children of God through Christ, 564. Who the children of God are, 625. The children of God must be peaceable, 518. Love of children, 435. Children must be treated well by their fathers, 771. Children ought not to be degenerate, 624. The son avenges the wrong done to his injured father, III, 1121. Description of a son who repents badly, III, 789. Children of the Church, 337.

**SON OF GOD.** See **CHRIST**.

The approaching end of the age, 512.

**FIRMILIAN**, bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, III, 1154. He embraces Cyprian’s works as though they were his own, 1157. His zeal for and love of unity, ibid., 1175 ff. He wrote in reply to Cyprian approximately twenty-two years after the emperor Alexander, 1163.

**FIRMUS**, martyr, 281.

The property of Christians claimed by the treasury, 430. The treasury seizes it, 616. The treasury holds the possessions of exiles, 272. Spiritual scourges, 555. Perpetual flame, 550. Flame-colored hair, 456.

**FLORA**, prostitute, 570.

**FLORENTIUS PUPPIANUS**, 400.

The ministry of the more flourishing [reading uncertain], 277.

**FLORUS**, 346.

Four rivers, that is, the four Gospels, III, 1116. At the flow of blood the world trembled, 802. It is not lawful to lend at interest, 759. Lend your patrimony at interest to God, 449. [Col. 1210] A sealed fountain, III, 1139. The sealed fountain of the Church, III, 1173. A fountain scarcely drips with a little sweat, 547. To increase a loan through multiplying interest, 471. The vices of the forum, 213, 214. A cosmetically falsified appearance in women, 669. Timorousness deserving punishment, 793. Fornication is a grave offense, 768.

**FORTUNATA**, martyr, 281.

**FORTUNATIANUS**, bishop, 389.

**FORTUNATUS**, bishop, III, 701, 703, 708, 711, 1036. Fortunatus, schismatic and pseudo-bishop, 808, 809, 810, 824. Fortunatus of Tuchabori, III, 1089. Fortunatus, presbyter, 234. Fortunatus, subdeacon, 302, 303.

**FORTUNIO**, martyr, 281.

To turn a man into a woman, 211. A ruptured brotherhood, 334. Charity is the bond of brotherhood, 631. A brother must not be defrauded, 773. Fraud is a mortal crime, 631. Entangled in frauds, III, 817. Defrauders and adulterers, III, 791. The people’s gnashing threats, 800. To seize estates through treacherous frauds, 471. Leafy shelters, 196.

**FRUCTUS**, martyr, 281.

Fruits of good work, 291. We can be wheat, 344. Artificial cosmetics, 454 ff. Flight during persecution, 471, 472. Country and patrimony must be abandoned, ibid. The flight of Christians during persecution, III, 1164. Flight during persecution praised, III, 855. Their glory is no less, 857. Those who, because of the necessity of the time, are for a while separated from the flock in body but not in spirit ought not to dread flight, 352. Concerning clerics who withdrew during persecution, 301. The penalty imposed upon them, ibid. You have begun to carry your own funeral bier, 490. The hatred of a frenzied mind, 644. Furni, III, 1095.
